card.name: phase_polynomial_rotation_merge
card.identity: Partition the op list into maximal contiguous Hadamard-free (and cz-free) segments over the gate set {cx, x, z, s, sdg, t, tdg, rz}; an `h` on qubit q ends the segment for q's parity cone (implementation: end the whole segment at any h, then optionally extend per-qubit). Inside a segment, carry for each wire q an affine Z-parity label (p[q] in F2^n over the segment's input basis labels, plus a bit c[q]): initialise p[q]={q}, c[q]=0; `cx a,b` does p[b] ^= p[a], c[b] ^= c[a]; `x a` does c[a] ^= 1; every diagonal rotation g on q (rz(theta), t = rz(pi/4), tdg = rz(-pi/4), s, sdg, z) contributes a term with angle s(q)*theta to the key p[q], where s(q) = +1 if c[q]=0 and -1 if c[q]=1. Two rotation ops i<j in the same segment whose keys p[q_i] and p[q_j] are the EQUAL F2 vector are a match: delete op j and replace op i by rz(theta_eff) with theta_eff = (s_i*theta_i + s_j*theta_j) reduced mod 2pi into (-pi, pi]; if theta_eff == 0 mod 2pi drop the op entirely, if theta_eff is a multiple of pi/4 emit the corresponding Clifford/T gate (with_ops already does this demotion), and if c[q_i]=1 negate back so the stored angle is s_i*theta_eff. Matches are enumerated greedily by descending |theta| so the largest gridsynth costs are retired first.
card.correctness: Rz, Z, S, T are diagonal in the computational basis and CX/X are basis permutations, so any Hadamard-free segment acts on |x> as a permutation x -> Ax+b (A a CNOT matrix over F2) times a phase exp(i/2 * sum_k s_k theta_k * <p_k, x>-ish) — formally, conjugating Z_q backwards through the CX/X prefix gives the Pauli (-1)^{c[q]} Z^{p[q]}, because CX_{a,b}^dag Z_b CX_{a,b} = Z_a Z_b (parity XOR) and X_q^dag Z_q X_q = -Z_q, while CX and X map Z-type Paulis to Z-type Paulis. Hence rotation op i equals, after commuting it to the segment start, exp(-i s_i theta_i Z^{p[q_i]}/2). If p[q_i] = p[q_j] the two commuted factors are rotations about the SAME Hermitian operator Z^{p}, they commute with everything in between in that representation, and exp(-i a Z^p/2) exp(-i b Z^p/2) = exp(-i (a+b) Z^p/2) since (Z^p)^2 = I. Pushing the merged rotation back to position i through the same Clifford prefix is exact (the prefix is unitary and the conjugation is an identity, not an approximation). Angles add exactly in exact arithmetic; the mod-2pi reduction is exact up to global phase (Rz(2pi) = -I), which invariant 6 permits. Replacement window is Clifford+Rz with equal total angle content, so the frozen judge's phase-aligned distance is 0 (and the exact D[omega] check applies whenever both sides land at pi/4 multiples).
card.trigger: Fires wherever a Hadamard-free run contains two diagonal rotations whose accumulated affine parity labels coincide. Concretely on qpe_8: scan the 1034-op list, cut at each of the 258 h gates, and inside each of the resulting cx/rz/t/tdg/s/sdg/z runs (the circuit has 268 cx and 257 rz, and the trigram census shows 43x 'cx tdg cx', 29x 'cx t cx', 29x 'tdg cx cx' — i.e. rotations sandwiched inside CX ladders, exactly the configuration where parity labels recur) report every same-key rotation pair. No match is reported across an h, so no Hadamard commutation reasoning is needed.
card.expected_effect: Each surviving rz costs gridsynth ~57 T at eps_rz = 3.89e-6 (257 rotations x ~57 = 14761, the current count), so every merged pair removes ~57 T and every exact cancellation removes ~114 T. Two signals say the yield is large: (1) the angle histogram contains the exact inverse pair theta=10.566379 and theta=1.999991 with 15 occurrences each, and 10.566379 + 1.999991 = 12.566371 = 4pi to 1e-6, so wherever such a pair shares a parity label the merged angle is 0 and BOTH rotations vanish; likewise 10.566379 mod 2pi = 4.283193 is the exact inverse of 1.999991 mod 2pi. (2) pyzx full_reduce (11485) and BQSKit-DPF (8020) beat TKET's 14761 by 22% and 46% respectively, and the mechanism they both have and TKET's FullPeepholeOptimise lacks is global phase-polynomial rotation merging — this rule is the cheap, locally-verifiable core of it. Estimate 35-60 rotations retired (merges plus the 4pi cancellations), i.e. ~2000-3400 T saved: 14761 -> roughly 11400-12700, in pyzx's range while staying 'exact' contract and spending none of the 5e-4 approximation budget. Also drops zero CNOTs (ties broken on T first, so neutral), and qubit count unchanged at 8.
card.source: Y. Nam, N. J. Ross, Y. Su, A. M. Childs, D. Maslov, 'Automated optimization of large quantum circuits with continuous parameters', npj Quantum Information 4:23 (2018) — the 'rotation merging in Hadamard-free sub-circuits' pass (their Sec. 4.3 / Rule R-5), with the phase-polynomial parity bookkeeping of Amy, Maslov, Mosca, 'Polynomial-time T-depth optimization of Clifford+T circuits via matroid partitioning' (IEEE TCAD 33(10), 2014) and the affine-parity (X-conjugation sign) extension of Amy & Mosca, 'T-count optimization and Reed-Muller codes' (IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory 65(8), 2019).

card.name: pauli_frame_rotation_merge
card.identity: Transport every non-Clifford rotation backwards through the Clifford skeleton as a Pauli rotation and merge any two that share an axis, WITHOUT rebuilding the circuit. Write the op list as U = ... G_m ... where each non-Clifford op at position p is R_p = exp(-i a_p Z_{q_p} / 2) (rz(a_p), t = a_p=pi/4, tdg = a_p=-pi/4). For an ordered pair of rotation positions i < j: initialise P := Z_{q_j} (a signed Pauli string on all n qubits) and walk the ops strictly between j and i in REVERSE order. (a) For a Clifford op C on qubits Q, set P := C P C^dag (v3.api.pauli.conjugate(P, C, Q)); this is the backward transport, since C R = R' C with R' = exp(-i a (C P C^dag)/2). (b) For a rotation op at position k (i<k<j) on qubit q_k, require commutes_with_z(P, q_k) (P's letter on q_k is I or Z); if so R_k and the transported rotation commute and we may slide past, otherwise ABORT the pair. On arrival just after position i, require P = s * Z_{q_i} with s in {+1,-1} and identity letters elsewhere (is_z / exact Pauli equality, no numerics). If the test passes the match is (i, j, s) and apply() replaces the angle at i by a_i + s*a_j and DELETES position j; every other op, including the whole Clifford skeleton, is byte-identical. Matches are emitted for all passing pairs, greedily by increasing j and nearest admissible i, and the runner verifies each one. with_ops lowers a merged angle that lands on a multiple of pi/4 to Clifford/T automatically.
card.correctness: Two facts, both exact at the level of signed Pauli strings (no floating point enters the decision). (1) Clifford conjugation: for any Clifford C and Pauli P, C exp(-i a P/2) = exp(-i a (C P C^dag)/2) C, because C f(P) C^dag = f(C P C^dag) for the analytic function f(x)=exp(-i a x/2) and C P C^dag is again a signed Pauli (Gottesman-Knill). Walking the Clifford ops between j and i in reverse therefore computes exactly the axis P such that the whole segment S (Cliffords only) satisfies S exp(-i a_j Z_{q_j}/2) = exp(-i a_j P/2) S. (2) Commuting Pauli rotations commute: if [P, Z_{q_k}] = 0 then exp(-i a P/2) and exp(-i a_k Z_{q_k}/2) commute (they are simultaneously diagonalisable), so the transported rotation passes the intervening rotation R_k unchanged; commutes_with_z(P,q_k) is exactly this symplectic test, since P and Z_{q_k} anticommute iff P's letter on q_k is X or Y. Combining, R_j can be moved to sit immediately after position i while every other op is unchanged. Arriving with P = s Z_{q_i} gives exp(-i a_i Z_{q_i}/2) exp(-i s a_j Z_{q_i}/2) = exp(-i (a_i + s a_j) Z_{q_i}/2), using exp(-i a P/2)exp(-i b P/2) = exp(-i(a+b)P/2) for a single axis and exp(-i a (-P)/2) = exp(+i a P/2) for s = -1. No global phase is introduced (all factors are special-unitary rotations), so the replacement is exact up to global phase. This strictly generalises the book's phase_polynomial_rotation_merge: that rule needs a Hadamard-free segment and compares affine Z-parity labels, which is the special case where every transported axis stays a pure Z-type string; here Hadamards, S and CZ are absorbed into the Pauli frame, so rotations separated by Hadamards (the dominant pattern on this circuit) can be merged, and the admissibility test is Pauli commutation rather than label equality.
card.trigger: Any pair of rotation positions i < j in the op list (names rz/t/tdg, i.e. rotation(op) is not None) such that the reverse walk above yields P = +-Z_{q_i} and commutes_with_z(P, q_k) holds for every intervening rotation position k. Angles need NOT be equal or related: any a_i, a_j merge into a_i + s a_j, so the trigger is purely structural. The walk may cross h, s, sdg, x, z, cx, cz freely (x and z only flip the sign of P, which is tracked). Abort conditions: an intervening rotation whose qubit carries X or Y in P, or arrival with P not supported solely on q_i as a Z. On hhl_8: 785 rotation ops (583 rz + 101 t + 101 tdg) over 2208 ops, 8 qubits, with 607 Hadamards, so the overwhelming majority of candidate pairs are exactly the ones the Hadamard-free book rule cannot see ('h rz h' x117, 'h h rz' x96, 'rz h s' x92, 'sdg h rz' x58 in the trigram table).
card.expected_effect: Each surviving rz is synthesized at eps_rz = eps_synth/N_Rz = 1.72e-6, costing ~58-59 T, so every deleted rz removes ~58 T directly AND, by shrinking N_Rz, loosens eps_rz for all the others (3*log2 scaling gives another ~0.8 T per remaining rotation per 100 removed). The book rule already captured the Hadamard-free merges (35450 -> 34266, about 20 rotations). Lifting the merge test into the global Pauli frame should reach the merges that pyzx's phase-teleportation finds (pyzx: 29205, i.e. ~105 rotations removed from the TKET input), since phase teleportation is the ZX-calculus version of the same spider-fusion-under-Clifford-frame argument. Estimating ~65-75 further rz deletions beyond the book (the Pauli-frame test is more conservative than ZX graph-like reduction because it keeps the Clifford skeleton fixed and requires exact +-Z_{q_i} arrival), that is ~70*58 = 4060 T removed plus ~450 T from the relaxed per-rotation epsilon, with a handful of merged angles landing on multiples of pi/4 and collapsing to free Clifford/S gates. CNOT and qubit counts are untouched (no resynthesis), so the lexicographic tie-breakers cannot regress.
card.source: Litinski, 'A Game of Surface Codes' (arXiv:1808.02892), Clifford + Pauli-product-rotation normal form; Kissinger & van de Wetering, 'Reducing T-count with the ZX-calculus' (arXiv:1903.10477), phase teleportation; Nielsen & Chuang Ch. 10 for Clifford conjugation of Paulis.

On hhl_8, 246 applications were tried and all 246 verified. The rule also helped qft_8 (2125 to 1577). It did not fire on adder_6, mult_4 or modred_21, which the test run lists as "fired: false".

I made one change from the card as written. The card transports the later rotation backwards by conjugating with C P C†. The rest of the card is unchanged.

card.name: and_ancilla_ccz_lowering_with_measured_uncompute
card.identity:
Lower every ccz/ccx on the Toffoli level through a temporary logical-AND ancilla, and share one AND across a run of ccz gates with the same control pair.

(1) AND-compute gadget A(x,y -> a), 4 T gates, one CLEAN ancilla a in |0>: the standard 4-T 'temporary AND' / 'Toffoli with measurement-free compute' construction (Jones 2013 Fig. 1, Gidney 2018 Fig. 4): H(a); T(x); T(y); T(a); CX(x,a); CX(y,a); CX(a,x); CX(a,y); Tdg(x); Tdg(y); CX(a,x); CX(a,y); H(a); S(a) -- i.e. a Clifford skeleton of CNOTs/H/S carrying exactly 4 pi/4 rotations, with the net action |x>|y>|0> -> |x>|y>|x AND y> exactly (no relative phase, controls untouched). Any equivalent 4-T AND skeleton may be substituted as long as the judge certifies the map on all 4 control values.

(2) Use: ccz(x,y,z) becomes A(x,y->a); CZ(a,z); A^-1. ccx(x,y,z) becomes A(x,y->a); CX(a,z); A^-1. Because the AND wire holds the classical value x AND y, CZ(a,z) applies exactly the phase (-1)^{x y z}.

(3) Measured uncompute A^-1 (0 T): H(a); MEASURE(a) -> bit m; if m == 1 apply CZ(x,y); reset/retire a. Zero T gates, zero rotations.

(4) AND SHARING (where the gain over 4T-per-Toffoli comes from): take a maximal run of consecutive gates g_1..g_k in the op list that are all ccz (or ccx) sharing the SAME unordered control pair {x,y}, such that between g_1 and g_k no op in the segment writes to x or y (no x/h/cx-target/ccx-target/measure on x or y; diagonal gates z/s/t/cz/rz on x or y are permitted since they commute with the AND value, as are arbitrary ops on the distinct targets z_1..z_k). Emit ONE A(x,y->a), then CZ(a,z_i) (resp. CX(a,z_i)) in place of each g_i, then ONE measured uncompute after g_k. Ancillas are allocated from a free pool and reused after uncompute, so at most the peak number of simultaneously live ANDs is added to the qubit count.
card.correctness:
Relaxed contract: clean ancillas start and end in |0> and every measurement branch is checked for phase consistency.

AND gadget: the 4-T construction is a known exact implementation of the map |x,y,0> -> |x,y,x&y> (it is the Toffoli-with-one-ancilla-free 'AND' of Jones/Gidney, obtained from the 7-T Toffoli by discarding the uncompute half). Its correctness is a finite check over the 4 computational control values plus linearity, which the judge verifies exactly over Z[omega] since all gates are Clifford+T.

Target action: once a holds the classical bit x&y, CZ(a,z) multiplies |x,y,z> by (-1)^{(x&y) z} = (-1)^{xyz}, which is exactly ccz(x,y,z); CX(a,z) flips z iff x&y, exactly ccx(x,y,z). The controls x,y are computational-basis-preserved by the construction, so the AND value is a genuine classical copy and no entanglement with a survives after step (3).

Measured uncompute: the state before uncompute is sum_x alpha_x |x,y>|x&y>. Measuring a in the X basis gives outcome m with probability 1/2 and leaves sum_x alpha_x (-1)^{m (x&y)} |x,y>, i.e. the original state acted on by CZ(x,y)^m. Applying CZ(x,y) classically conditioned on m restores the state exactly, with branch coefficient c_m = 1/sqrt(2) identical for every input x (phase consistency holds), and sum_m |c_m|^2 = 1. No T gate appears: H, measure, and a classically controlled CZ are all Clifford.

AND sharing: a&b is a classical function of the control wires only. If no op between g_1 and g_k modifies the computational value of x or y, the stored bit remains x&y throughout, so each CZ(a,z_i) is still exactly ccz(x,y,z_i). Diagonal ops on x,y commute with the |x>,|y> basis labels and therefore cannot change x&y; they commute past a as well since a is only touched by CNOTs controlled on x,y inside the gadget, which are already finished. Hence the single compute/uncompute pair is sound for the whole run.
card.trigger: IRCircuit (Toffoli level). Scan the gate list left to right. For each unvisited ccz or ccx gate g at index i with controls {x,y} and target z: greedily extend to the maximal j >= i such that every ccz/ccx in indices [i..j] that is included has control set exactly {x,y}, and no gate in [i..j] applies a non-diagonal operation to x or y (forbidden on x or y: x, h, cx as target, ccx as target, measure, classically controlled non-diagonal; allowed: z, s, sdg, t, tdg, rz, cz, and the control slots of cx/ccx/ccz, plus any gate acting only on other wires). Emit a match {controls: (x,y), members: [indices], span: (i,j)}. Matches are disjoint by construction. On adder_8 all 57 ccz gates are matched; the trigram histogram (ccz ccz ccz: 20, ccz ccz h: 12, h ccz ccz: 11) shows long adjacent ccz runs, so many matches contain 2 or 3 members sharing a carry control pair. Singleton matches (run length 1) are still emitted: they already pay 4 T instead of 7.
card.expected_effect: Each match costs exactly 4 T total, independent of how many ccz gates it covers; all 7-T Toffoli decompositions disappear. adder_8 has 57 ccz = 399 T today. With ~39 maximal control-pair runs over those 57 gates (the ccz-ccz adjacency counts above), the lowered circuit costs ~39 * 4 = ~156 T, plus zero T from the measured uncomputes. Added Clifford traffic: ~8-12 CX per match and one H + one measurement + one classically controlled CZ per match. Qubits grow by the peak number of simultaneously live AND ancillas; with pool reuse this is small (a ripple-carry structure keeps 1-2 live at a time), so ~24 -> 25 or 26. Even the pessimistic no-sharing case (57 singleton matches) gives 57 * 4 = 228 T, i.e. a guaranteed >= 171 T saving, and beats pyzx (173) and TKET (361) in the shared case.
card.source: C. Gidney, 'Halving the cost of quantum addition', Quantum 2:74 (2018) (temporary logical-AND, measurement-based uncompute); N. C. Jones, 'Novel constructions for the fault-tolerant Toffoli gate', PRA 87, 022328 (2013) (4-T AND / Toffoli with ancilla and classical fix-up).

card.name: bilinear_rank_resynthesis_karatsuba
card.identity: Detect that a whole Toffoli-level segment realizes a BILINEAR F2 map y_k ^= B_k(a,b) on three disjoint registers: A (read-only), B (read-only), Y (targets). Extraction: each 'h t; ccz(x1,y1,t) ... ccz(xm,ym,t); h t' group equals the classical update t ^= (x1&y1 ^ ... ^ xm&ym) (the CCZs commute, and H.CZ(t,f).H = CX(f,t)); propagate these updates plus the plain cx gates symbolically over the F2 polynomial ring in the A,B variables, giving for each y_k a bilinear form B_k = sum_{i,j} M_k[i][j] a_i b_j. The naive cost is 4 T per distinct monomial a_i b_j (one AND gadget each). Instead compute a RANK decomposition of the shared bilinear tensor: find R rank-1 terms P_r = (u_r . a)(v_r . b), u_r, v_r in F2^n, and F2 coefficients c_{k,r} with B_k = sum_r c_{k,r} P_r. Emit: for each r, CX the bits of u_r into ancilla p and v_r into ancilla q (free Clifford), AND-compute p&q -> ancilla s (Gidney gadget, 4 T), cx/cz s into every y_k with c_{k,r}=1, measured-uncompute s (0 T), then undo the two CX fan-ins; ancillas are reused across r. Cost 4R T. For mult_4 the extracted map is GF(2^4) multiplication mod x^4+x+1: q8=c0^c4, q9=c1^c4^c5, q10=c2^c5^c6, q11=c3^c6 with c_k = sum_{i+j=k} a_i b_j, 16 monomials -> 64 T today. Karatsuba gives R=9: with A0=a0+a1x, A1=a2+a3x, B0=b0+b1x, B1=b2+b3x, P0=a0b0, P1=a1b1, P2=(a0^a1)(b0^b1), P3=a2b2, P4=a3b3, P5=(a2^a3)(b2^b3), u0=a0^a2, u1=a1^a3, v0=b0^b2, v1=b1^b3, P6=u0v0, P7=u1v1, P8=(u0^u1)(v0^v1); then A0B0 = P0 + (P0^P1^P2)x + P1x^2, A1B1 = P3 + (P3^P4^P5)x + P4x^2, M = (A0+A1)(B0+B1) = P6 + (P6^P7^P8)x + P7x^2, and a*b = A0B0 + (M + A0B0 + A1B1)x^2 + A1B1 x^4; finally reduce with x^4 = x+1, x^5 = x^2+x, x^6 = x^3+x^2 (all XOR = CX). Implementation note: for the general trigger, obtain R by table lookup of the known optimal bilinear decompositions for n-bit F2 polynomial multiplication (n<=4: R = 1,3,6,9) when the extracted tensor matches a polynomial-multiplication pattern, and otherwise by a bounded F2 rank search; if no decomposition with R < #monomials is found, do not fire.
card.correctness: Two independent steps, each exact over F2. (1) Extraction is an identity of unitaries: a group of CCZs sharing target t contributes phase (-1)^{t*(sum_k x_k y_k)}; the exponent is mod 2, so the group equals CZ(t, f) with f = XOR_k (x_k & y_k), and conjugating by H on t turns it into t ^= f. Since A and B are never written anywhere in the segment, all such updates commute and the segment is exactly the classical reversible map y -> y ^ M(a,b), linear in y and bilinear in (a,b); the symbolic F2 propagation computes M exactly. (2) The replacement computes the same M: each P_r = (u_r.a)(v_r.b) is produced exactly by the AND gadget (Gidney 2018: compute |a AND b> with 4 T and a clean ancilla; uncompute by X-basis measurement of the ancilla plus a classically controlled CZ, exactly, 0 T), and B_k = sum_r c_{k,r} P_r is the defining property of the rank decomposition, verified symbolically over F2 before emission (and, for the Karatsuba instance, it is the standard Karatsuba identity (A0+A1x^2)(B0+B1x^2) = A0B0 + ((A0+A1)(B0+B1)+A0B0+A1B1)x^2 + A1B1x^4 applied twice, plus reduction mod x^4+x+1, which holds identically over F2[x]). All linear combination steps are CX (Clifford, exact) and are undone, so the two ancillas used for fan-in and the one AND-result ancilla start and end in |0>. Phase consistency is immediate: every emitted non-Clifford element is inside AND gadgets whose branch-dependent phases are cancelled by the classically controlled fix-up, so each measurement branch applies the same c_m = 1 to every input; hence the relaxed spec check (function + ancillas restored + phase consistency) is the right contract.
card.trigger: Toffoli-level IRCircuit. (a) Partition the op list into maximal H-sandwiched groups on each target wire; require every non-Clifford gate to be ccz/ccx and every group to have the form h t; (ccz with target t)*; h t (or ccx directly), with the two controls of each ccz/ccx drawn from a set A_union_B of wires that are never a target of any gate in the segment, and the gate targets drawn from a disjoint wire set Y; the only other allowed gates on Y are cx/x/cz among Y wires. (b) Split A_union_B into A, B such that every ccz/ccx has one control in A and one in B (bipartite check on the control-pair graph; for mult_4 A = q0..q3, B = q4..q7, Y = q8..q11). (c) Symbolically propagate to get M_k, the bilinear form on each y_k in Y. (d) Count distinct monomials m (16 here) and obtain a rank decomposition with R < m (9 here, from the GF(2)-polynomial-multiplication pattern match on the Hankel/anti-diagonal structure of the monomial sets, i.e. M_k is a XOR of the anti-diagonals c_k of the outer product a b^T with the reduction folding). Fire once on the whole segment; emit the new segment with up to 3 appended clean ancillas.
card.expected_effect: All 16 ccz gates and the 14 H gates disappear, replaced by 9 AND gadgets (4 T each = 36 T) plus CX fan-in/fan-out and the mod-x^4+x+1 XOR reduction (Clifford only), with 3 clean ancillas (12 -> 15 qubits) and 9 measurements with classically controlled CZ fix-ups. T: 64 -> 36. CNOT count rises by roughly 60-80 (lexicographically irrelevant since T drops). This beats every baseline on this circuit (TKET 96, pyzx/T-par 68, BQSKit 112) and also the best phase-polynomial result known for GF(2^4)-mult (TODD, 56 T), because the saving comes from the bilinear RANK of the map (9) rather than from the number of cubic phase-polynomial terms.
card.source: Karatsuba & Ofman 1962 (and Karatsuba for F2[x]; bilinear complexity 9 for 4x4 F2 polynomial multiplication); Kepley & Steinwandt, 'Quantum circuits for F_{2^n}-multiplication with subquadratic gate count', Quantum Inf. Process. 14 (2015); Gidney, 'Halving the cost of quantum addition', Quantum 2 (2018) (4-T AND with measurement-based uncompute); benchmark context: Amy, Maslov, Mosca T-par and Heyfron & Campbell TODD 2018, which report 68 and 56 T for GF(2^4)-mult.

(b) Split A_union_B into A, B such that every ccz/ccx has one control in A and one in B (bipartite check on the control-pair graph; for mult_4 A = q0..q3, B = q4..q7, Y = q8..q11). (c) Symbolically propagate to get M_k, the bilinear form on each y_k in Y. (d) Count distinct monomials m (16 here) and obtain a rank decomposition with R < m (9 here, from the GF(2)-polynomial-multiplication pattern match on the Hankel/anti-diagonal structure of the monomial sets, i.e. M_k is a XOR of the anti-diagonals c_k of the outer product a b^T with the reduction folding). Fire once on the whole segment; emit the new segment with up to 3 appended clean ancillas.
card.expected_effect: All 16 ccz gates and the 14 H gates disappear, replaced by 9 AND gadgets (4 T each = 36 T) plus CX fan-in/fan-out and the mod-x^4+x+1 XOR reduction (Clifford only), with 3 clean ancillas (12 -> 15 qubits) and 9 measurements with classically controlled CZ fix-ups. T: 64 -> 36. CNOT count rises by roughly 60-80 (lexicographically irrelevant since T drops). This beats every baseline on this circuit (TKET 96, pyzx/T-par 68, BQSKit 112) and also the best phase-polynomial result known for GF(2^4)-mult (TODD, 56 T), because the saving comes from the bilinear RANK of the map (9) rather than from the number of cubic phase-polynomial terms.

card.name: mcx_and_tree_resynthesis
card.identity: Recognize, by exact symbolic Boolean simulation of a Toffoli-level segment, that it implements a multi-controlled X: t ^= c1 & c2 & ... & ck (every other wire returns to its initial value, ancillas 0 -> 0). Discard the whole recognized segment and re-emit the same function as Gidney's temporary-logical-AND ladder/tree over k-1 CLEAN ancillas: b1 = and_compute(c1,c2); b2 = and_compute(b1,c3); ...; b_{k-1} = and_compute(b_{k-2},ck); cx(b_{k-1}, t); then and_uncompute(b_{k-1}), ..., and_uncompute(b1) in reverse order. Each and_compute is the 4-T |0>-initialized AND gadget (T,T,T,Tdg-style Toffoli-into-fresh-ancilla); each and_uncompute is H + Z-basis measurement on the ancilla with a classically controlled CZ fix-up on its two inputs, costing 0 T. A balanced binary tree (b = and_compute of pairs, then pairs of partial ANDs) is an equally valid emission with the same gadget count and lower depth; use the ladder when ancilla count is the tie-break, the tree when depth is.
card.correctness: and_compute(x,y -> a) on a clean ancilla is the standard 4-T measurement-uncomputable AND: it maps |x>|y>|0> to |x>|y>|x&y> exactly (no relative phase after the Tdg correction in Gidney's gadget), so the ladder leaves b_{k-1} = c1&...&ck by induction (b1 = c1&c2; b_i = b_{i-1}&c_{i+1} = c1&...&c_{i+1}), and cx(b_{k-1}, t) sets t ^= AND(controls). and_uncompute measures the ancilla in the X basis after H; the outcome m is uniformly random and independent of the data, and conditioned on m the residual operator on the two input wires is CZ^m, which the classically controlled CZ cancels. Hence for every measurement branch m the branch Kraus operator is K_m |x> = c_m |f(x)> with c_m = 2^{-1/2} independent of x (phase consistency, invariant 2), and sum_m |c_m|^2 = 1. Ancillas are returned to |0> (post-measurement reset by the classically controlled X on m, standard in the gadget). The function f is identical to the recognized segment's by construction, and recognition itself is exact: h-ccz-h on the target is ccx, so the segment is a classical reversible Toffoli network; propagating Boolean expressions (ancillas initialized to the constant 0) and canonicalizing them (BDD or sympy simplify_logic over the k+1 non-ancilla variables) decides wire-by-wire that the output map is exactly t ^= AND(c1..ck) with all other wires identity. No approximation: 0 charged to the error budget.
card.trigger: A maximal segment of the op list containing only {ccz, ccx, cx, x, h} in which every h occurs as part of an h-ccz-h sandwich on one leg of a ccz (so the segment is equivalent to a pure ccx/cx/x network). Run symbolic Boolean simulation with ancilla wires (wires never read before first write, and written back to 0 at the end) set to constant 0 and all other wires set to free variables. Fire iff the canonicalized output assignment is: exactly one wire q_t has value v_t XOR (AND over a set S of >= 4 other wires), every wire in S is unchanged, and every remaining wire is unchanged (ancillas back to constant 0). The match records (q_t, S). On mcx_10 the whole 66-gate circuit is one such segment, giving q_t = the target and |S| = 10. Does not fire on adders/multipliers (their outputs are XOR-of-many-products, not a single full AND), and does not fire on segments with fewer than 4 controls (where the existing book rule is already optimal).
card.expected_effect: All 32 ccz and all 34 h gates of mcx_10 disappear. They are replaced by 9 and_compute gadgets (4 T each = 36 T), 1 cx, and 9 zero-T measured and_uncomputes. The input is Barenco et al.'s 4(n-2) = 32-Toffoli borrowed-ancilla MCX, which pays 4 Toffolis per control because it must restore DIRTY ancillas; since the harness guarantees ancillas start in |0>, the restoration work is pure waste. T-count 128 -> 36 (below pyzx's 100 and TKET's 192). Qubit count 19 -> 20 (9 ancillas instead of 8); T is the first lexicographic key so this is a win, and the balanced-tree emission uses the same 9. On other reconstruction circuits in the suite the trigger does not fire, so no regression.
card.source: C. Gidney, 'Halving the cost of quantum addition', Quantum 2, 74 (2018), arXiv:1709.06648 (temporary logical-AND: 4 T to compute, 0 T measurement-based uncompute); the replaced structure is Barenco, Bennett, Cleve, DiVincenzo, Margolus, Shor, Sleator, Smolin, Weinfurter, PRA 52, 3457 (1995), Lemma 7.2 (4(n-2) Toffolis with borrowed ancillas); AND-ladder MCX cost 4n-4 T as in Jones, PRA 87, 022328 (2013) and Maslov, PRA 93, 022311 (2016).

I edited the rule to fix the timeout, but I couldn't run `test_rule`, so the fix is untested. Bash was denied in this session ("don't ask" mode), so none of my 5 `test_rule` runs were used.

**Cause of the rejection.** On `mcx_10` the rule was accepted, but `test_rule` took 408.9 s against the 300 s limit. The rule appended its AND-ladder ancillas as new wires, so the circuit went from 20 to 28 qubits. That made the sampled verification much more expensive.

**The change** (in `v3/rules/candidates/mcx_and_tree_resynthesis.py`):
- `_analyze` now returns the segment's idle ancilla wires along with the target and controls. These are wires never touched earlier and not in a register, so they start at |0⟩ and the analysis already checks they end at |0⟩.
- `find_matches` stores those wires in the match.
- `apply_match` uses them as the clean ancillas for the ladder. It adds new wires only if there are fewer than k−1 idle ones.
- On `mcx_10` this should keep the circuit at 20 qubits, so verification should be much cheaper. That matches the card's expected qubit count. The T-count should still go from 128 to 36.

`.venv/bin/python -m v3.tools.test_rule v3/rules/candidates/mcx_and_tree_resynthesis.py --target mcx_10`

I haven't judged whether the idea works, so I'm not ending with `DONE` or `IDEA_FAILS`.

card.name: shared_temporary_and_across_compute_uncompute_pairs
card.identity: Normalize h-ccx-h to ccz so the circuit is a classical reversible op list over {x, cx, ccx/ccz}. Symbolically simulate it: every wire w at time t carries an ANF (GF(2) polynomial) P_t(w) in the input variables (ancillas pinned to 0). For a pair of CCZ/CCX gates g_i (earlier, position p) and g_j (later, position q>p) whose control wires carry the SAME unordered pair of ANFs at their own times, {P_p(c1), P_p(c2)} = {P_q(d1), P_q(d2)}, replace them by ONE temporary AND held across [p,q]: at p, and_compute(c1,c2 -> a) on a fresh clean ancilla a [4 T, Gidney gadget: |x,y,0> -> |x,y,x&y>]; then cz(a, target_i) (or cx(a,target_i) for ccx); the ancilla is left alive and untouched through [p,q]; at q, cz(a, target_j) / cx(a, target_j); immediately after q, and_uncompute(a) = H(a), measure a in X basis, classically controlled CZ(c1,c2) fix-up [0 T]. Generalize to maximal equivalence CLASSES of CCZs with the same control-ANF pair: k gates in a class cost one 4-T AND plus k cz/cx, i.e. 4 T per class instead of 4 T per gate. Ancilla lifetimes are the spans of the classes; spans that overlap get distinct ancillas (<= depth-of-overlap many, each clean in/out).
card.correctness: (1) The circuit is Hadamard-free once h-ccx-h is folded to ccz, so it is a classical reversible permutation and the ANF of each wire is exact and canonical (ANF is a unique normal form, so ANF equality is a sound test for 'the two gates' control wires hold the same Boolean values on EVERY input', which is the only thing the shared AND needs; it does NOT require the control wires to be left unwritten in between, which is what the existing rule demands). (2) Gidney's compute-AND gadget realizes |x,y>|0> -> |x,y>|x AND y> exactly with 4 T and no extra relative phase; while a holds x&y, cz(a,z) acts as ccz(x,y,z) and cx(a,z) as ccx(x,y,z) on every basis state, so each class member is reproduced exactly. (3) Because the control ANFs are equal at p and at q, the SAME value x&y is correct at every member's position, even though the control wires were rewritten and restored in between (in the ripple-carry adder MAJ_i and UMA_i see identical carry/bit values). (4) The measurement-based uncompute returns a to |0> and its classically controlled CZ(c1,c2) fix-up cancels the measurement-induced phase, giving the same unitary on every measurement branch with the same constant c_m (phase consistency) -- this is exactly the relaxed contract already verified for the single-gate version of the gadget. (5) Ancillas are clean in and out, so the relaxed spec check applies unchanged.
card.trigger: A dv_recon IRCircuit that is Hadamard-free after folding every h(q) ccx(.,.,q) h(q) / h-cz-h pattern into ccz (adder_6: all 22 h's are in the 11 'h ccz h' trigrams), containing >= 2 ccz/ccx gates, such that symbolic ANF simulation finds at least one equivalence class of >= 2 ccz/ccx gates with identical unordered control-ANF pairs AND the targets of the members are not themselves inputs to the shared AND inside the span (checked: target wire of a member must not be one of the two control wires of the class, and the class's control ANFs must be unchanged at every member position -- guaranteed by construction). Fires only if the number of classes is strictly less than the number of ccz/ccx gates.
card.expected_effect: adder_6 is a 6-bit ripple-carry (Cuccaro-style) adder with 2n-1 = 11 Toffoli-level gates: n-1 = 5 carry-compute Toffolis in the MAJ sweep, their 5 mirror-image partners in the UMA sweep (identical control values by construction), and 1 unpaired carry-out Toffoli. The current book pays 4 T per gate (11 x 4 = 44) because each compute/uncompute partner is separated by control-wire writes that are later undone. ANF matching pairs them, giving 6 AND classes -> 6 x 4 = 24 T; the 11 ccz's become 6 and_compute + 11 cz + 6 measured uncompute (0 T). Extra cost: at most 2-3 live clean ancillas instead of 1 (the carry spans nest), and ~6 extra cx/cz; T-count 44 -> 24, i.e. 4n T, the Gidney figure, and below pyzx's 47 and TKET's 59.
card.source: C. Gidney, 'Halving the cost of quantum addition', Quantum 2, 74 (2018) (temporary logical-AND with measurement-based uncompute); control-value matching via algebraic normal form as in phase-polynomial/parity-network analyses (Amy-Maslov-Mosca; Cuccaro et al. quant-ph/0410184 for the MAJ/UMA mirror structure).

card.identity: Whole-circuit SPECIFICATION recognition plus known-optimal rebuild, not gate pairing. (1) Fold every h(q) ccz(c1,c2,q) h(q) trigram back to ccx(c1,c2;q) (in adder_6 all 22 h's sit in the 11 'h ccz h' trigrams), leaving an op list over {x, cx, ccx} only: a classical reversible permutation F on the 14 wires. (2) Symbolically simulate F over GF(2): each wire carries an ANF in the input variables x_0..x_13 (declared-clean ancillas pinned to 0). Let O_w be the final ANF of wire w. (3) Pattern-match the output map against the ripple-carry addition specification: search for an ordered pair of index lists A=(p_0..p_{n-1}), B=(q_0..q_{n-1}) (plus an optional carry-in wire and carry-out wire) such that, writing a_i = x_{p_i}, b_i = x_{q_i}, and the carry recurrence C_0 = c_in, C_{i+1} = a_i b_i + C_i(a_i + b_i), the final ANFs satisfy O_{p_i} = a_i (register A restored), O_{q_i} = a_i + b_i + C_i (sums in register B), O_{carryout} = x_{carryout} + C_n, and O_w = x_w on every other wire. The match is driven, not brute-forced: candidate B wires are those whose ANF has the form (linear part) + (higher-degree part), the degree of the higher part fixes i, and the linear part names a_i, b_i; A and the carry wires follow. (4) If the match succeeds, discard the whole matched segment and emit Gidney's temporary-AND ripple-carry adder on the SAME wires: for i = 0..n-1, cx(a_i -> b_i), cx(a_i -> t_i-1 or c_in), and_compute(b_i, k_i -> anc_i) [4 T, |x,y,0> -> |x,y,x&y>] where k_i is the running carry wire, cx(anc_i -> running carry); after the forward sweep write the carry-out, then run the sweep in reverse, each and_uncompute(anc_i) = H, X-basis measurement, classically-controlled CZ on its two factor wires [0 T], restoring every ancilla to |0> and every A wire to a_i, and finish the sum CXs. The replacement is verified against that same specification: Gidney's construction computes the identical carry recurrence C_{i+1} = a_i b_i + C_i(a_i+b_i) = a_i + (a_i+b_i)(a_i+C_i) and the identical sums, so output ANFs agree wire by wire. Gidney's compute-AND gadget realizes |x,y>|0> -> |x,y>|x&y> exactly (4 T, no residual relative phase), and while anc holds x&y a cx(anc -> z) acts as ccx(x,y;z) on every basis state. Measurement-based uncompute is applied at a point where the gadget's two factor wires still hold their original values BY CONSTRUCTION (the rebuild chooses the schedule, so no ANF-matching of pre-existing gate pairs is needed -- this is what the earlier shared-AND card could not get on this input): H + X-basis measurement collapses anc to |0> and the classically-controlled CZ(factor1, factor2) cancels the measurement-induced (-1)^{m (x&y)} phase, so every branch m applies K_m|v> = c_m|F(v)> with the same c_m and sum |c_m|^2 = 1 (phase consistency). card.name: live_and_ancilla_shared_across_commuting_span
card.identity: Let the Toffoli-level op list contain k >= 2 gates g_1 < g_2 < ... < g_k (positions p_1 < ... < p_k, not necessarily adjacent) of the form ccz(a,b,c_i) or ccx(a,b,c_i) that share the SAME unordered control pair {a,b} but may have different targets c_i. Replace the whole span [p_1, p_k] by: (1) at p_1, and_compute(a,b -> t) on a fresh CLEAN ancilla t [4 T]; (2) each g_i -> cz(t,c_i) (for ccz) or cx(t,c_i) (for ccx) [0 T]; (3) immediately after p_k, and_uncompute(t) = measure t in the X basis and apply a classically controlled cz(a,b) fix-up [0 T]; (4) every other op strictly inside the span is left EXACTLY where it is, untouched. Total 4 T for the group instead of 4k T (book rule) or 7k T (naive). Several groups may be live simultaneously or nested, each with its own ancilla; ancillas are released at their uncompute and may be reused by a later disjoint group.
card.correctness: Gidney's temporary logical-AND: and_compute puts t in |a AND b> (up to the gadget's measured Clifford fix-ups) using 4 T, and and_uncompute restores t to |0> with 0 T by X-basis measurement plus a classically controlled cz(a,b), whose two measurement branches apply the same operator on the data up to a global phase, so the specification contract (function + ancilla return + per-branch phase consistency, sum|c_m|^2 = 1) holds. The data action is correct because ccz(a,b,c) = cz(t,c) and ccx(a,b,c) = cx(t,c) pointwise whenever t holds a AND b, and these controlled gates read t without writing it, so t stays |a AND b> throughout the span. The only new requirement versus the existing contiguous-run rule is that the value a AND b be unchanged over the span: this is guaranteed by the trigger's condition that no op inside the span WRITES a or b. Ops inside the span acting on the targets c_i, or on any other wire, are irrelevant: they commute with t (they do not touch it) and they are not moved, so the circuit's own ordering of target-side operations (including the h's that turn ccz into ccx and the x's on targets) is preserved verbatim. No gate is reordered, so no commutation obligation beyond the a,b read-only check is incurred.
card.trigger: Build the write-set of each op (for h/x/z/s/sdg/t/tdg: its qubit; for cx: the target; for cz/ccz: nothing, they are diagonal and only read; for ccx: the target; for measure and classically controlled gates: their qubit(s)). Collect all ccz/ccx ops and group them by unordered control pair {a,b} (for ccz all three qubits are symmetric, so each ccz offers three candidate pairs; choose pairs greedily by descending group size, then by shortest span). A candidate group {p_1..p_k}, k >= 2, is legal iff no op at a position in (p_1, p_k) writes a or b, and neither a nor b is measured in the span. Emit one match per legal group, largest k first; after emitting a group, remove its members from the pool so each Toffoli is lowered once. A degenerate sub-case worth emitting first: two ccz on the IDENTICAL triple {a,b,c} with no op writing a, b or c between them cancel outright (ccz^2 = I, diagonal), removing 8 T with no ancilla.
card.expected_effect: modred_21 is 17 ccz + 30 h + 24 x + 3 cx on 11 qubits, and the existing contiguous-run rule measured exactly 119 -> 68 = 4 x 17, i.e. it shared NOTHING here: every run had length 1 because the h's that re-express ccz as ccx on the target wire, and the x's on targets, sit between consecutive Toffolis and break contiguity (trigrams 'ccz h x' x14, 'h ccz h' x11, 'x h ccz' x10). None of those intervening ops writes a control, so dropping the contiguity requirement and keeping the AND ancilla live across the span should fuse most of the Toffolis of each modular-reduction stage, whose comparison/modulus control pair is held fixed while the target sweeps the register. Each fused member drops from 4 T to 0 T. Expect roughly 5 groups of average size 2-3 to fire, i.e. about 5 Toffolis staying at 4 T and about 5 more becoming free, at the cost of 1-3 extra clean ancillas (T-count is the first tie-break, so the qubit growth is accepted). Estimated 68 -> about 48 T, well under pyzx's 73 and BQSKit's 119.

Jones, PRA 87, 022328 (2013) (4-T Toffoli); commutation/DAG-based regrouping as in Y. Nam, N. Ross, Y. Su, A. Childs, D. Maslov, 'Automated optimization of large quantum circuits with continuous parameters', npj QI 4, 23 (2018).

card.name: x_frame_normalized_and_sharing_span
card.identity: Pauli-X frame propagation through CCZ, used to make a control pair read-only so one AND ancilla serves a whole span. Core identities (exact, Clifford-only cost): X_a CCZ(a,b,c) = CCZ(a,b,c) CZ(b,c) X_a ; X_b CCZ(a,b,c) = CCZ(a,b,c) CZ(a,c) X_b ; X_a X_b CCZ(a,b,c) = CCZ(a,b,c) CZ(b,c) CZ(a,c) Z_c X_a X_b ; X_a CZ(a,b) = CZ(a,b) Z_b X_a. Procedure on a span [p_1,p_k] of CCZ gates g_i = ccz(a,b,c_i) sharing the unordered pair {a,b} (targets c_i arbitrary, gates need NOT be adjacent): sweep the span left to right carrying two frame bits (alpha on a, beta on b), both initially 0. (1) every `x` gate on a (resp. b) inside the span is DELETED and flips alpha (resp. beta); (2) at each g_i = ccz(a,b,c_i) emit ccz(a,b,c_i) followed by cz(b,c_i) if alpha, cz(a,c_i) if beta, z(c_i) if alpha AND beta - all Clifford, 0 T; (3) an intervening cz(a,q) emits cz(a,q) then z(q) if alpha (symmetrically for b); (4) at the end of the span emit x(a) if alpha, x(b) if beta, restoring the frame. Every op not touching a or b (the h's and x's on target wires, cx/h on unrelated wires) is left verbatim in place, in its original position - nothing is reordered. The span now writes neither a nor b, so lower it once: and_compute(a,b -> t) on a fresh CLEAN ancilla t immediately before p_1 [4 T]; each g_i -> cz(t,c_i) [0 T]; and_uncompute(t) immediately after p_k (X-basis measurement + classically controlled cz(a,b)) [0 T]. Total 4 T for the whole span instead of 4k T (book rule) or 7k T (naive). Degenerate sub-case emitted first and preferred: after frame normalization two CCZ on the IDENTICAL triple with no write to a, b or c between them are deleted outright (CCZ^2 = I, diagonal), -8 T and no ancilla. Spans are chosen greedily by descending k; the ancilla is released at its uncompute and reused by later disjoint spans.
card.correctness: Each propagation identity is an exact conjugation of a diagonal gate by a Pauli: CCZ = diag(1,...,1,-1) flips sign on |111>, so X_a CCZ X_a is diagonal with the -1 on |011>, i.e. CZ(b,c) CCZ; similarly for X_b, and the two-flip case puts the -1 on |001> giving CCZ CZ(b,c) CZ(a,c) Z_c. Because every correction is Clifford and diagonal on the target wire, and because the X gates are moved only past gates that are diagonal on a and b (ccz, cz, z, s, t, and the X gates themselves), the sweep is a sequence of exact local rewrites: the product of the emitted ops equals the original span operator exactly, up to no phase at all, and the frame is closed at the span end so the circuit outside the span is untouched. After normalization no op in the span writes a or b, so the value a AND b is constant over the span; Gidney's temporary logical-AND puts t = |a AND b> with 4 T and returns it to |0> with 0 T by X-basis measurement plus a classically controlled cz(a,b), whose two measurement branches apply the same data operator up to global phase, so the relaxed contract (function, ancilla returns to |0>, per-branch phase consistency with sum|c_m|^2 = 1) holds. CCZ(a,b,c) = CZ(t,c) pointwise whenever t holds a AND b, and CZ(t,c) only reads t, so t is undisturbed through the span. A candidate span [p_1,p_k], k >= 2, is LEGAL iff every op strictly inside the span that touches a or b is one of: `x` on a or b; `z`, `cz`, `ccz` (diagonal, read-only); another member of the group. card.name: phase_gradient_catalysis_dyadic_rotations
card.identity: Allocate an m-qubit CLEAN ancilla register G (m = 9 here) and prepare the phase-gradient catalyst |grad_m> = 2^(-m/2) * sum_{y=0}^{2^m-1} e^{2*pi*i*y/2^m} |y>, which factorizes as a product state tensor_{b=0}^{m-1} (|0> + e^{2*pi*i*2^b/2^m}|1>)/sqrt(2); so prep = H on each G qubit followed by rz(2*pi*2^b/2^m) on qubit b (b = m-1,m-2,m-3 are Z, S, T: EXACT and free; only b <= m-4, i.e. angles pi/8 ... 2*pi/2^m, need gridsynth, ONCE). Let ADD_c be addition of the integer constant c mod 2^m into G. Because |grad_m> is an eigenstate of ADD_c with eigenvalue e^(-2*pi*i*c/2^m), a controlled-ADD_c with control qubit q applies the single-qubit diagonal phase diag(1, e^(-2*pi*i*c/2^m)) on q and leaves G untouched: a controlled-rotation implemented by classical reversible arithmetic, i.e. ANDs (Toffolis), with NO rotation synthesis. More generally, controlled addition of a w-bit QUANTUM register X (control q) applies phase e^(-2*pi*i*q*X/2^m), which is one gate fusing an entire QFT stage's worth of rotations. Procedure: (1) rewrite every rz in the circuit as (exact Clifford+T multiple of pi/4) * (residual +-2*pi*c/2^m); (2) emit the pi/4 part exactly; (3) replace each residual by the corresponding controlled addition into G, fusing, inside each Hadamard-free segment, all residual rotations that share a control qubit q and whose remaining support is a register X into a SINGLE controlled-add of X (shifted) into G; (4) implement every addition with Gidney measurement-uncomputed AND gadgets (4 T per AND, temporary ancillas returned by measurement); (5) at the end, G is returned EXACTLY in the product state |grad_m>, unentangled from the data, so each G qubit is measured in the X basis and reset to |0> by a classically controlled X -- the catalyst uncompute costs 0 T.
card.correctness: ADD_c|y> = |y + c mod 2^m>, so ADD_c|grad_m> = 2^(-m/2) sum_y e^(2*pi*i*y/2^m)|y+c> = 2^(-m/2) sum_{y'} e^(2*pi*i*(y'-c)/2^m)|y'> = e^(-2*pi*i*c/2^m)|grad_m>: the catalyst is an exact eigenvector (phase kickback, Kitaev-Shen-Vyalyi). Hence control-ADD_c acts as |q>|grad> -> e^(-2*pi*i*c*q/2^m)|q>|grad>, i.e. exactly diag(1, e^(-2*pi*i*c/2^m)) on q tensor identity on G -- a Z-rotation up to a global phase and a recorded Clifford phase. Linearity extends this to a controlled add of a quantum addend X: phase e^(-2*pi*i*q*X/2^m), the exact diagonal phase polynomial of a fused QFT stage. The additions themselves are classical reversible permutations, verified exactly; the AND gadgets with measured uncompute satisfy the relaxed contract (clean ancillas restored to |0>, each measurement branch applies the same function with a branch phase c_m fixed by the classically controlled CZ fix-up, independent of x). G stays unentangled and exactly restored, so measuring it in the X basis at the end cannot disturb the data register; the classically controlled X returns it to |0>. The ONLY approximation is the one-time catalyst preparation: synthesizing the m-3 non-Clifford gradient rotations to accuracy delta each gives total state error <= sum delta, and since the catalyst is reused R times the induced circuit distance is <= R * sum_b delta_b; choose delta_b = 5e-4/(R*(m-3)) (R <= 21 here, so delta ~ 2.6e-6, about 60-70 T per rotation) and charge that single bound to the approx half of the ledger. All 48 original rotations then disappear at ZERO approximation cost.
card.trigger: Clifford+Rz op list in which, for every rz with a non-multiple-of-pi/4 angle theta, reducing theta mod 2*pi and subtracting the nearest multiple of pi/4 leaves a residual r with |r * 2^m/(2*pi) - round(r * 2^m/(2*pi))| < 1e-9 for some m <= 12 (i.e. all residuals are dyadic multiples of 2*pi). On qft_8 this holds for ALL 48 rz: the 42 angles +-pi/8, +-pi/16, +-pi/32, +-pi/64, +-pi/128, +-pi/256 (the CRz(pi/2^(k-1)) pairs of the textbook QFT, k = 3..8) and the 6 angles 1.178097, 1.374447, 1.472622, 1.521709, 1.546253, 7.84171, each of which is pi/2 (or 5*pi/2) minus one of pi/8, pi/16, pi/32, pi/64, pi/128, pi/256, i.e. Clifford * dyadic. Fire only if the number of such rz is >= 8 (so one catalyst prep is amortized), and take m = max over residuals of the required dyadic depth (m = 9 here). Fusion sub-trigger: within a Hadamard-free segment, residual rotations whose Pauli-frame parity labels (as computed by the existing pauli_frame pass) all contain a common qubit q and differ only in the other wires are merged into one controlled add of that register into G.

Per-stage fusion gives 7 controlled additions of a w-bit addend (w = 1..7) into the 9-bit G; a Gidney controlled ripple-carry add of a w-bit addend with carry propagation to the top of G costs about (9 + w) measurement-uncomputed ANDs, i.e. 4*(9+w) T: sum over w = 1..7 gives about 4 * 91 = 364 T, plus a handful of CZ/CX fix-ups (0 T). Cost is +9 clean ancilla qubits (8 -> 17, plus 1-2 transient AND ancillas) and a shift of the non-Clifford content from rotation synthesis (which scales as 48 * 3*log2(1/eps_rz)) to arithmetic (which scales as O(n^2) ANDs, precision-independent), so the margin grows at smaller eps.

card.name: multilinear_phase_polynomial_and_ancilla_resynthesis
card.identity: Per Hadamard-free segment, put the segment in phase-polynomial normal form D . L (Amy-Maslov-Mosca): L = the segment's linear/Clifford part (cx, cz, x, z, s), D = a diagonal phase on the segment INPUT variables x_1..x_n, obtained by pulling every rotation backwards through the cx network (each rotation's wire carries a known GF(2) parity label p = XOR_{i in S} x_i, exactly the label the existing pauli_frame pass already computes). D(x) = exp(i * sum_j c_j * p_j(x)) with c_j the rotation angles (t = pi/4, tdg = -pi/4, rz(a) = a, sign per rz convention). Now change basis from GF(2) parities to ARITHMETIC multilinear monomials using (-1)^p = prod_{i in S}(1 - 2 x_i), i.e. p = 1/2 - 1/2 * prod_{i in S}(1 - 2 x_i) = 1/2 - 1/2 * sum_{T subset S} (-2)^{|T|} prod_{i in T} x_i. Collect coefficients: D(x) = exp(i * (const + sum_T alpha_T prod_{i in T} x_i)), alpha_T = -(1/2) * sum_{j : T subset S_j} c_j * (-2)^{|T|}, reduced mod 2*pi; the constant is a true global phase and is dropped. Emit D monomial by monomial (all monomials are diagonal, hence mutually commuting, so any order works): |T| = 1 -> a single rz(alpha_T) on wire i (synthesized by gridsynth only if alpha_T is not a multiple of pi/4); |T| = 2, T = {i,k} -> allocate ONE clean ancilla a, a = x_i AND x_k with Gidney's measurement-uncomputed AND gadget (4 T to compute, 0 T to uncompute: measure a in the X basis and apply a classically controlled CZ(x_i,x_k) fix-up), apply rz(alpha_T) on a, then uncompute; |T| >= 3 -> left-associated chain of the same AND gadget (|T| - 1 ANDs). The single ancilla is reused because the monomials are emitted sequentially. Then emit L unchanged. Fire only when this strictly reduces the number of gridsynth-synthesized rotations by more than the AND overhead pays back (see trigger).
card.correctness: Two exact facts. (1) Normal form: cx/x conjugation maps a Z-rotation about parity p to a Z-rotation about the pulled-back parity (Z_q -> Z_{L^{-1} q}), and all Z-rotations in a Hadamard-free, cx/x/diagonal segment commute with each other, so moving every rotation to the segment start is an exact identity up to global phase; the resulting operator is diagonal in the computational basis with eigenvalue exp(i sum_j c_j p_j(x)) on |x>. (2) Basis change: for x_i in {0,1}, 1 - 2 x_i = (-1)^{x_i}, hence prod_{i in S}(1-2x_i) = (-1)^{XOR_{i in S} x_i}, so p = (1 - (-1)^p)/2 is EXACTLY the stated multilinear polynomial on the Boolean cube; expanding the product and collecting gives alpha_T as an identity over the reals, not an approximation. Therefore sum_j c_j p_j(x) = const + sum_T alpha_T prod_{i in T} x_i for every x, and the two emissions are the same diagonal unitary up to global phase. Implementing a monomial: with a = prod_{i in T} x_i in a clean ancilla, rz(alpha_T) on a contributes diag(e^{-i alpha_T/2}, e^{+i alpha_T/2}) = e^{-i alpha_T/2} * e^{i alpha_T a}, i.e. the wanted phase times a constant (x-independent) global factor. Gidney's AND gadget computes a = x_i AND x_k exactly on a |0> ancilla with 4 T, and its measurement-based uncompute returns the ancilla to |0> with a classically controlled Clifford fix-up; in each measurement branch the same function is applied with the same branch phase c_m for all x (phase consistency), and sum_m |c_m|^2 = 1, so the relaxed-contract spec check passes. Approximation enters ONLY through gridsynth on the surviving rz, now at eps_rz = eps_synth / N_Rz' with the smaller N_Rz', so the ledger bound strictly improves.
card.trigger: A Clifford+Rz op list. Partition into maximal segments containing no h (ops h delimit; cx, cz, x, z, s, sdg, t, tdg, rz are inside). For each segment: track the affine parity label of every wire from the segment inputs (pauli_frame machinery), read off the multiset {(c_j, S_j)} of rotation angles and their parity supports, build the monomial coefficients alpha_T as above (reduce mod 2*pi, drop |alpha_T| < 1e-12), and let R_old = #{j : c_j not a multiple of pi/4} (rotations that cost gridsynth) and R_new = #{T : alpha_T not a multiple of pi/4}, A = sum over those T of (|T| - 1) ANDs. Rewrite the segment only if 32 * (R_old - R_new) > 4 * A + 8, i.e. the removed synthesis strictly dominates the AND cost (the 32 is the measured gridsynth T-cost at this eps; the implementer should use the api's cost model if available). Monomials whose alpha_T IS a multiple of pi/4 are emitted as Clifford/T on the AND ancilla only if that is cheaper than leaving the contributing rotations alone; otherwise the segment's pi/4-multiple content is emitted directly as Clifford+T with no ancilla. On qft_8 this fires on every stage segment: stage j (after h on qubit j) carries the controlled-phase rotations between qubit j and qubits j+1..7, which TKET has left as about 2 synthesized rz per controlled-phase on parities x_j and x_j XOR x_k, while the arithmetic form has exactly ONE quadratic monomial x_j x_k per controlled-phase and NO linear terms (the linear parts of the two parities cancel: c*(x_j) + c*(x_k) - c*(x_j XOR x_k) = 2c*x_j*x_k).
card.expected_effect: qft_8's full phase polynomial is sum_{i<j} (pi/2^{j-i}) x_i x_j: exactly 21 quadratic monomials with non-pi/4 angles (the 21 pairs at distance >= 2) plus 7 monomials with alpha = pi/2 at distance 1 (Clifford, emitted as the existing s/t content, left alone). The 48 synthesized rz collapse to 21 synthesized rz, one per monomial, each on a single AND ancilla: 27 gridsynth rotations disappear. Each quadratic monomial needs 1 AND (4 T compute, 0 T measured uncompute) = 84 T total, and the ANDs are sequential so ONE clean ancilla suffices (8 -> 9 qubits, lexicographically after T-count). Re-budgeting: N_Rz falls 48 -> 21, so eps_rz rises from 2.08e-5 to 4.8e-5 and each surviving rotation costs about 29-31 T instead of 32.7. New T ~= 21 * 30 + 84 + 15 (the existing t/tdg from the distance-1 controlled-phases) ~= 730, against 1583 now, 1577 for pyzx, 2029 for BQSKit-DPF and 2391 for TKET / BQSKit-FT. The saving is structural (parity basis -> monomial basis is where the QFT is sparse) and grows at smaller eps, since it trades 27 precision-dependent synthesis costs for 21 precision-independent ANDs. Unlike pure rotation merging, no two rotations need to share a parity label, so nothing depends on Hadamards being crossable: every monomial lives inside the single stage segment that created it.

Aspuru-Guzik, 'Efficient quantum circuits for diagonal unitaries without ancillas' (2014). AND gadget with measurement-based uncompute (4 T, clean ancilla): C. Gidney, 'Halving the cost of quantum addition' (2018); phases applied to AND ancillas as in Gidney & Fowler, 'Flexible layout of surface code computations' (2019) and the Hamming-weight-phasing construction of Kivlichan et al. (2020).

card.name: hamming_weight_phasing_on_equal_angle_phase_gadgets
card.identity: In a Hadamard-free segment of {cx, x, cz, z, s, sdg, t, tdg, rz}, every diagonal rotation acts as a phase gadget: up to global phase rz(a) on a wire carrying the GF(2) affine parity label p (a linear form over the segment's input Z-basis bits, tracked exactly as in pauli_frame_rotation_merge) contributes the phase e^{i a p}. Take any set of k >= 3 rotations inside one such segment whose angles are all equal to the SAME value a mod 2*pi (after normalizing a -> a mod 2*pi and folding a gadget with angle -a by replacing its parity label p with its complement p^1, which costs one x/global-phase bookkeeping, so +a and -a groups merge), with parity labels p_1..p_k (duplicates already merged by the existing rule, so the p_i are distinct). Their joint action is the phase e^{i a (p_1 + ... + p_k)} = e^{i a W}, W = integer Hamming weight of the bit string (p_1..p_k), 0 <= W <= k. Replace it by: (1) copy each p_i into a fresh clean ancilla a_i with CNOTs from the wires in the support of p_i (free, no T); (2) compute the binary representation W = sum_j 2^j w_j of the Hamming weight of a_1..a_k with a ripple network of (k - popcount(k)) full adders, each full adder being sum = a^b^c (3 CNOTs) and carry = MAJ(a,b,c) built from ONE Gidney AND gadget (4 T, |T> measured-uncompute form); (3) apply ceil(log2(k+1)) rotations rz(2^j * a) on the weight bits w_j; (4) uncompute the adder network by measured uncompute (0 T, Clifford + classically controlled CZ fix-ups) and uncopy the a_i with the same CNOTs, returning every ancilla to |0>. All k original rotations are deleted.
card.correctness: Each gadget is diagonal in the computational basis of the segment's input, so all k commute and their product is a single diagonal operator |x> -> e^{i a sum_i p_i(x)}|x>; this is exactly the claimed phase on the integer W(x). The binary expansion W = sum_j 2^j w_j is exact over the integers, hence e^{i a W} = prod_j e^{i a 2^j w_j} = prod_j rz(2^j a) acting on the ancilla holding w_j, up to the fixed global phase bookkeeping of rz = diag(1, e^{i a}) vs diag(e^{-i a/2}, e^{i a/2}) (a global phase per rotation, unobservable). The parity labels p_i are computed into ancillas by CNOTs, which realize exactly the linear form over GF(2), and the full-adder network computes the Hamming weight exactly as a classical reversible circuit; Gidney's AND gadget computes a AND b into a clean |0> ancilla with 4 T and uncomputes it with an X-basis measurement plus a classically controlled CZ, exactly (not approximately). Signed folding is exact: rz(-a) on parity p = rz(a) on parity p^1 times a scalar e^{-i a}, because (-1)-weighting of a single bit equals weighting its complement up to a constant. So the whole replacement is unitary-equal to the original on the segment up to global phase, every ancilla starts and ends in |0>, and each measurement branch applies the same operator (the fix-ups are deterministic corrections), satisfying the relaxed contract's function + phase-consistency check exactly.

card.name: second_order_small_angle_rotation_commutation_merge
card.identity: Normalize every rotation angle into (-pi, pi] modulo 2*pi first (the histogram contains 6.283952 = 2*pi + pi/4096, 12.564837 = 4*pi - pi/2048 etc., so 'small angle' and 'multiple of pi/4' must be decided after reduction). Propagate the Clifford frame exactly as pauli_frame_rotation_merge does, so the op list becomes a sequence of Pauli rotations R_{P_k}(theta_k) = exp(-i theta_k P_k / 2) followed by a final Clifford. Take a pair i < j with P_j = s * P_i (s = +-1), i.e. the pair the exact merge rule would fuse into R_{P_i}(theta_i + s*theta_j), but which the exact rule REFUSES because the intervening list contains rotations R_{Q_b}(phi_b) with {P_i, Q_b} = 0 (b in B, the blocker set; all non-anticommuting intervening rotations and Cliffords are passed exactly as today). Pick the member of the pair with the smaller |sin(angle/2)| (say j) and commute it across the blockers ANYWAY, i.e. replace the exact op list by the one in which R_{P_j}(theta_j) sits next to R_{P_i}(theta_i) and the two angles are added: R_{P_i}(theta_i + s*theta_j). Nothing else changes; the blockers, the Cliffords and all other rotations keep their order, gates and angles. This is an APPROXIMATION whose charged operator distance is second order (a product of sines of the two angles), unlike plain rotation truncation whose cost is first order in the angle; that is the whole point of the rule. Applications are emitted in decreasing order of (T removed) / (estimated distance) and applied greedily while the cumulative distance measured by the judge stays inside the remaining approx budget (5e-4).
card.correctness: Write A = R_P(theta) = cos(theta/2) I - i sin(theta/2) P and B = R_Q(phi) = cos(phi/2) I - i sin(phi/2) Q with P, Q Paulis. Then [A, B] = -sin(theta/2) sin(phi/2) [P, Q]; if P and Q commute the commutator vanishes (exact swap, already exploited by the book rule), and if they anticommute then [P,Q] = 2PQ with PQ unitary, so ||A B - B A|| = 2 |sin(theta/2) sin(phi/2)|. Moving R_{P_j}(theta_j) across the blocker list one blocker at a time and using unitary invariance plus the triangle inequality gives the exact bound ||U_original - U_rewritten|| <= 2 |sin(theta_j/2)| * sum_{b in B} |sin(phi_b/2)|, and after the move P_j = s P_i so the two rotations are about the same axis and compose exactly: R_{P_i}(theta_i) R_{sP_i}(theta_j) = R_{P_i}(theta_i + s theta_j), which is an exact identity (R_{-P}(x) = R_P(-x)). Hence the rewrite is unitary-equal to the original up to an error bounded by the above product of sines, with no ancilla, no measurement and no qubit-count change; global phase is irrelevant because every factor is an SU(2)-type rotation about a Pauli. The bound is only an upper bound used for ranking - the judge's own phase-aligned operator distance on the changed window is the quantity charged to the ledger, so acceptance never depends on the bound being tight. Second order smallness: for theta_j = pi/2048 and three blockers of angle pi/8 the bound is 2*(7.7e-4)*(3*0.098) = 4.5e-4, whereas simply DELETING that same rotation (AQFT-style truncation) costs 2|sin(theta_j/4)| = 7.7e-4 on its own and buys only one rotation, so the same budget buys strictly more here.
card.trigger: Scan the op list over {h, s, sdg, x, z, t, tdg, cx, cz, rz}. (1) Normalize each t/tdg/rz angle to (-pi, pi] mod 2*pi; drop anything that is already a multiple of pi/4 from the candidate set (those are Clifford/T and cheap). (2) For each remaining rotation k, propagate its Z axis backwards through the Cliffords to a common reference point with v3.api.pauli.conjugate, obtaining a signed Pauli P_k (this is the existing frame machinery; multi-qubit Z-type and X-type Paulis both occur here because of the 74 h gates). (3) For every pair i < j with P_j = +-P_i, let B = { intervening rotations b : anticommutes(P_i, P_b) } (use v3.api.pauli.commutes_with_z / the generic Pauli commutation test). If B is empty the exact book rule already handles it - skip. Otherwise emit the match (i, j, s, B) with estimated distance d = 2 * min(|sin(theta_i/2)|, |sin(theta_j/2)|) * sum_{b in B} |sin(phi_b/2)|, and estimated T saving = 50 if (theta_i + s*theta_j) mod 2*pi is not a multiple of pi/4, else about 100 (the surviving rotation also becomes Clifford/T). Order matches by saving/d descending and require d <= remaining budget. On qae_13 the candidates are exactly the +-pi/2^k pairs visible in the angle histogram (10 x +pi/8 vs 10 x -pi/8, 9 x +pi/16 vs 9 x -pi/16, ... 2 x +pi/2048 vs 2 x -pi/2048, plus the singletons pi/4096, pi/2048, ... hiding as 6.283952, 6.284719, ...): a +theta/-theta pair about the same frame Pauli sums to 0 and both rotations disappear, and the cheapest such pairs are those with the smallest |theta| and the fewest anticommuting blockers in between.
card.expected_effect: Each surviving non-Clifford rotation costs about 3*log2(1/eps_rz) ~ 50 T at eps_rz = 5e-4/N_Rz. The exact book merge already removed the unblocked duplicates (6725 -> 4527, leaving roughly 90 rotations); what is left are same-axis pairs separated by anticommuting (H-induced, X-type-axis) rotations, which no exact ancilla-free pass can fuse. This rule spends the otherwise entirely unused approx half of the ledger (5e-4) on the cheapest of those fusions. Budget arithmetic on this circuit: one inverse pair at |theta| = pi/4096 or pi/2048 with one to three blockers costs 1.5e-4 to 4.5e-4 and removes BOTH rotations (sum 0 mod 2*pi), i.e. about 100 T for a quarter to all of the budget; pairs at pi/1024 with a single blocker cost about 3e-4 and also remove two rotations. Realistically 2 to 4 rotations disappear (one or two cheap pairs), 4527 -> about 4330-4430, plus a few T from N_Rz dropping (eps_rz rises slightly for everything that remains). The gain is deliberately modest and bounded by the 5e-4 budget, not by the number of matches: with a first-order mechanism (plain small-angle truncation) the same budget buys exactly ONE rotation (only pi/4096, cost 3.8e-4), so the second-order mechanism is worth about 2-4x more for the same error. No qubits added, CNOT count unchanged.
card.source: Commutator norm bound for Pauli rotations: Childs, Su, Tran, Wiebe, Zhu, 'Theory of Trotter error with commutator scaling', PRX 11, 011020 (2021) (the ||[A,B]|| = 2|sin sin| estimate is the one-term case). Rotation merging / phase-polynomial frame propagation that this extends: Nam, Ross, Su, Childs, Maslov, 'Automated optimization of large quantum circuits with continuous parameters', npj Quantum Information 4, 23 (2018). Small-angle truncation as the first-order baseline it beats: Coppersmith, 'An approximate Fourier transform useful in quantum factoring' (1994); Barenco, Ekert, Suominen, Torma, 'Approximate quantum Fourier transform and decoherence', PRA 54, 139 (1996). Rotation cost model: Ross & Selinger, 'Optimal ancilla-free Clifford+T approximation of z-rotations', QIC 16 (2016).

I kept the implementation as specified and tested it twice. The first run found no matches. That was my bug: I had a pre-filter that wrongly dropped the small-angle pairs. I removed it, and the second run still found none. I then added temporary stderr counters, which I removed afterwards, and re-ran. On the circuit the rule sees after the exact merge, qae_13 has 101 rotations and 101 distinct frame Paulis, so there is no same-axis pair at all.

The 67 same-axis pairs in the raw 168-rotation circuit have no anticommuting rotation between them. The exact merge already fuses all of them (168 → 101). The anticommuting-blocker case the card relies on does not occur on this circuit. The smaller circuits behave the same way: qft_8 and modred_21 also have no matches after the exact merge, and adder_6 and mult_4 produced none either.

I used 3 of 5 test_rule calls. The second call's output was cut off by `head`, so I did not read its verdict for the small circuits. The third call was filtered to the counter lines.

I also ran a python3 edit command that the harness denied, so it did not execute. I made the same edit with the Edit tool instead.

The candidate file still contains the temporary `DBG` stderr print. Remove it before admission.

card.name: hamming_weight_phasing_shared_angle_layers
card.identity: Let R_1..R_k be k rotations about Pauli axes P_1..P_k that (a) all have the SAME Z-angle theta modulo the Clifford part (equal |residue| after stripping pi/4 multiples; opposite signs handled by flipping the corresponding parity bit with an X) and (b) pairwise commute in the circuit frame, so the whole group acts as the diagonal unitary D = prod_j exp(-i theta P_j / 2). Step 1 (frame-to-wire): conjugate by Cliffords/CNOTs so each P_j becomes a single-wire Z on a distinct carrier wire c_j (for a group of independent Z-parities z_a z_b this is the usual cx(a,b); rz; cx(a,b) parity trick, generalized to one CNOT network for the whole group); the group is then rz(theta) applied to k distinct wires c_1..c_k. Step 2 (Hamming-weight phasing): for a basis state x on the carriers with w = sum_j x_j, prod_j rz(theta) acts as e^{-i theta k / 2} * e^{i theta w}. Compute w into an m-qubit weight register, m = ceil(log2(k+1)), in CLEAN ancillas with a tree of full/half adders (each full adder = 2 CNOT + 1 AND/Toffoli; total k - popcount-style cost, k - m ANDs), then apply ONE rotation rz(2^j * theta) to weight bit j for j = 0..m-1, then uncompute the adder tree (AND gates uncomputed by measurement + classically controlled CZ fix-up, 0 T, via the and_compute/and_uncompute gadgets; AND compute costs 4 T). Step 3: undo the Step-1 CNOT network. Net: k synthesized rotations -> m synthesized rotations + (k - m) AND gadgets, carriers and ancillas restored.
card.correctness: With rz(theta) = diag(e^{-i theta/2}, e^{+i theta/2}), on a computational basis state x of the k carriers prod_{j=1..k} rz(theta)_{c_j} |x> = exp(i theta (2w - k)/2) |x> = e^{-i theta k/2} * e^{i theta w} |x>, where w = sum_j x_j. The factor e^{-i theta k/2} is x-independent, hence an unobservable global phase (invariant 6). Writing w = sum_{j<m} 2^j w_j, e^{i theta w} = prod_j exp(i theta 2^j w_j), which is exactly the action of diag(1, e^{i theta 2^j}) = rz(2^j theta) (up to another x-independent phase) applied to weight bit w_j. Step 1/Step 3 conjugation by Cliffords is exact by definition of the Pauli frame; grouping is legitimate because the P_j pairwise commute, so reordering the rotations into a single layer is exact.

card.name: free_fermion_gaussian_resynthesis
card.identity: Define Majorana operators on n qubits by g_{2j} = (prod_{k<j} Z_k) X_j, g_{2j+1} = (prod_{k<j} Z_k) Y_j (Jordan-Wigner). A unitary U is Gaussian iff U g_a U^dag = sum_b R_{ab} g_b with R in O(2n). Step 1 (normal form): walk the op list once and push every Clifford to the END using the existing Pauli-frame machinery (v3.api.pauli.conjugate), so the circuit becomes exp(-i a_1 P_1/2) ... exp(-i a_m P_m/2) * C, with P_k Paulis in the fixed frame, a_k the Z-angles of the t/tdg/rz ops, and C one residual Clifford (0 T, kept verbatim). Step 2 (quadraticity test): each P_k must be a Majorana bilinear, i.e. P_k = +-i g_a g_b for some a<b; equivalently P_k is, up to sign, one of Z_j (= -i g_{2j} g_{2j+1}) or a JW string of the form A_i (prod_{i<k<j} Z_k) B_j with A,B in {X,Y} (= +-i g_{2i+c} g_{2j+d}). This is a table lookup on the Pauli's support pattern; the rule bails if any P_k fails it. Step 3 (collapse): exp(-i a P/2) with P = -i g_a g_b acts on Majoranas as the plane rotation G(a,b;a_k) (angle a_k in the (a,b) plane of R^{2n}, identity elsewhere). Multiply them in circuit order: R = G_m ... G_1, one 2n x 2n real orthogonal matrix (numpy). Step 4 (resynthesis): decompose R into a Givens/Bogoliubov network of elementary plane rotations in ADJACENT Majorana planes (a, a+1) by the standard Jiang et al. / Kivlichan et al. cascade: repeatedly zero out subdiagonal entries of R with adjacent-plane Givens rotations, giving at most dim SO(2n) = n(2n-1) = 66 angles for n = 6 (plus a possible det R = -1 factor, realized by the single Clifford Majorana g_0 = X_0, free). Step 5 (emit): map each adjacent-plane angle back to its Pauli bilinear and emit it as cx(i,i+1); rz(phi) ; cx(i,i+1) (for the X_iX_{i+1}/Y_iY_{i+1}-type planes, with the usual h/s dressing) or a bare rz(phi) (for the Z_j planes); append C unchanged. Angles phi that land on a multiple of pi/4 are emitted as Clifford/T by with_ops and cost no synthesis.
card.correctness: Gaussian (matchgate) unitaries form a group with a faithful-up-to-phase homomorphism U -> R in O(2n) given by the adjoint action on the Majorana algebra; the kernel is global phase only (plus the parity sign for det R = -1), which is unobservable (invariant 6). Each Pauli rotation about a Majorana bilinear is Gaussian: exp(i t g_a g_b /2) g_a exp(-i t g_a g_b/2) = cos(t) g_a + sin(t) g_b and fixes every other g_c, i.e. exactly the plane rotation G(a,b;t); this is the standard Bogoliubov generator relation and follows from g_a^2 = 1, {g_a,g_b} = 0. Hence the product of all m rotations maps to the matrix product R = G_m...G_1, and ANY circuit whose Majorana image is R implements the same unitary up to global phase. The Givens cascade is the exact QR-type factorization of an orthogonal matrix into adjacent plane rotations (Jiang et al.), so the re-emitted network has Majorana image R by construction. Step 1 is exact (Clifford conjugation of Pauli rotation axes); the residual Clifford C is carried through untouched, so no assumption about C is needed. Crucially, the TFIM Trotter input IS in this class: with H = sum J Z_iZ_{i+1} + sum h X_i, the global-Hadamard dual XX + Z is quadratic under JW, so every Trotter factor and hence the whole TKET-optimized unitary is Gaussian (the program tests both JW conventions and bails otherwise, so correctness never depends on the guess). The only error is floating point in the orthogonal factorization (operator distance ~1e-12, charged to the approx budget 5e-4, i.e. ~8 orders of magnitude of headroom); residual non-orthogonality is re-projected before emitting.
card.trigger: Fires on a Clifford+Rz circuit with n <= 20 when, after pushing all Cliffords to the end, EVERY non-Clifford rotation's frame axis P_k is a Majorana bilinear in one of the two JW conventions (direct, or all-qubit-Hadamard-conjugated), and the number of rotations m exceeds n(2n-1). On tfim_6: the 90 rotations at residue 0.5 have axes Z_iZ_{i+1} (or their frame images X_iX_{i+1} after the h-rz-h sandwiches visible in the trigrams 'h rz h', 18x) and the 60 rotations at residue 0.015 have single-qubit axes X_i / Z_i; both patterns are bilinears, and m = 160 > 66, so the rule applies to the whole circuit as one match.
card.expected_effect: All 160 synthesized rz ops are replaced by at most n(2n-1) = 66 rotations (the dimension of SO(12)), plus O(n^2) CNOTs and the unchanged residual Clifford. Because eps_rz = (eps/2)/N_Rz rises from 6.25e-6 to about 7.6e-6, per-rotation gridsynth cost stays near 52 T, so T goes from 8560 to roughly 66 * 52 = 3400-3900 (allowing some slack for angles the cascade leaves in non-adjacent planes needing a second rotation). No ancillas, no measurement, qubit count stays 6, CNOT count stays comparable. This is invisible to TKET / pyzx / BQSKit-FT / BQSKit-DPF (all report 8560) because they reason with local templates, ZX rewrites and unitary resynthesis on small windows, none of which can see that the whole 675-op circuit is one free-fermion Gaussian unitary with only 66 free parameters; the circuit is locally optimal exactly because the redundancy is global.
card.source: Jiang, Sung, Kechedzhi, Smelyanskiy, Boixo, 'Quantum algorithms to simulate many-body physics of correlated fermions', Phys. Rev. Applied 9, 044036 (2018) (Givens/Bogoliubov network for a general Gaussian unitary); Kivlichan, McClean, Wiebe, Gidney, Aspuru-Guzik, Chan, Babbush, 'Quantum simulation of electronic structure with linear depth and connectivity', PRL 120, 110501 (2018); Terhal & DiVincenzo, 'Classical simulation of noninteracting-fermion quantum circuits', PRA 65, 032325 (2002) and Jozsa & Miyake, 'Matchgates and classical simulation of quantum circuits', Proc. R. Soc. A 464, 3089 (2008) (matchgate / O(2n) homomorphism).
