card.name: window_angle_refit_to_clifford_grid
card.identity: Over-parameterized-window numerical refit. (1) Cut the op list into maximal contiguous windows W with |support(W)| <= 3 qubits and <= 40 ops, containing k >= 3 rotation ops whose angle is NOT a multiple of pi/4 (a window ends at the first op touching a 4th qubit). (2) Freeze W's own Clifford skeleton (its h/s/sdg/x/z/cx/cz ops and their order and wiring) and treat its k non-pi/4 angles as free parameters theta in R^k; the window unitary is the explicit matrix-product map U(theta) in U(2^m), m = |support| <= 3, built with numpy. (3) Choose a pin-set S of indices and target grid values g_i in (pi/4)Z (for i in S, g_i = the nearest multiple of pi/4 to the current theta_i, also trying 0 and +-pi/4 and +-pi/2 as alternatives), and solve min over the free angles theta_{not in S} of the phase-aligned residual d(theta) = min_phi || e^{i phi} U(theta_S = g_S, theta_free) - U(theta^0) ||_2 (operator 2-norm; phi eliminated analytically from the dominant eigenphase of U(theta)^dag U(theta^0)) with scipy.optimize.least_squares from 8 starts: theta^0 itself plus 7 random perturbations. (4) Greedy, largest-|theta| first: try to pin one more angle, keep the pin iff the refit residual d <= delta_w = 2e-6; on failure drop that index and continue with the next. Emit the window with the pinned angles written as exact Clifford/T gates (with_ops demotes pi/4 multiples) and the refitted free angles as rz. Cap the pass at 100 accepted windows so the total charge is <= 2e-4 of the 5e-4 approximation budget. One match = one window + its final pin-set, applied atomically.
card.correctness: Nothing is claimed to be an identity: the rule is an approximation with an explicitly measured error, which is exactly what the 'approx' contract charges. The replacement window unitary U' = U(theta_S = g_S, theta_free*) satisfies, by construction of the accept test in step (4), min_phi ||e^{i phi} U' - U||_2 <= delta_w = 2e-6, and the frozen judge re-measures this same phase-aligned operator distance on the changed window and charges it; with <= 100 accepted windows the total charge is <= 2e-4 < eps/2 = 5e-4, and distances compose subadditively because the operator norm is submultiplicative and unitary-invariant: ||A_1...A_r - B_1...B_r|| <= sum_j ||A_j - B_j|| when all factors are unitary. Global phase is unobservable (invariant 6), hence the phi minimization is legitimate; the residual is computed on the true matrix, not on an angle-space proxy, so no first-order linearization enters the bound. The mechanism that makes the pins feasible at 2e-6 rather than at the O(pi/8) naive rounding error is parameter redundancy: the map theta -> U(theta) from a window with k angles into the (at most dim-of-local-orbit)-dimensional family it actually sweeps is generically non-injective whenever k exceeds that dimension (e.g. a window whose rotations, after Clifford conjugation, act about Paulis P, Q, PQ in one commuting frame sweeps a 2- or 3-parameter family however many rz ops are written), so the level set U(theta) = U(theta^0) is a positive-dimensional manifold and moving along it lets the free angles absorb a pinned angle's shift exactly up to numerics; only the *last* pins that leave the level set pay a real, measured approximation. Soundness does not depend on that redundancy existing: when it does not, the residual exceeds delta_w and the pin is simply dropped, so the rule degrades to a no-op rather than to an unsound rewrite. Cost side: pinning an angle to a multiple of pi/4 makes it exact under the metric's convention (pi/4 multiples are free), so N_Rz strictly drops and the runner's T-count gate decides the keep.
card.trigger: Fires on any maximal contiguous window of the 1034-op list with support <= 3 qubits, <= 40 ops and >= 3 rz ops whose angle is not a multiple of pi/4, for which at least one greedy pin survives the residual test at 2e-6. On qpe_8 this is the dominant local pattern: the trigram census is saturated by short single- and two-wire sandwiches carrying several rotations each ('h rz rz' 42x, 'h rz h' 40x, 'rz h h' 40x, 'rz h rz' 28x, 'sdg h rz' 28x, 'h cx rz' 34x, 'cx rz h' 30x, 'cx t cx' 29x, 'cx tdg cx' 43x), and with 257 rz / 268 cx / 258 h over only 8 qubits the <=3-qubit support cut yields roughly 60-90 windows that together hold most of the 257 non-Clifford rotations. Windows are visited in descending rotation count so the fixed 2e-4 charge is spent where the most rotations can be retired per unit of error. No window is cut at an h or at a rotation, so the H density that limited the earlier phase-polynomial attempt (history attempt 1: 'segments end at every H, so few rotations pair up', measured 192 T against an estimate of 2700) does not gate this rule at all.
card.expected_effect: Each surviving non-pi/4 rz costs gridsynth ~53 T at the current operating point (13603 T over 257 rotations), and every angle pinned to a multiple of pi/4 removes that rotation entirely: it becomes a literal z/s/sdg/t/tdg (or vanishes at 0) at zero T-cost beyond the Clifford layer. There is a second-order bonus: N_Rz appears in eps_rz = eps_synth / N_Rz, so retiring r rotations also relaxes the per-rotation tolerance for the survivors and shaves ~3 log2(257/(257-r)) T off each one (r = 50 gives ~0.9 T on each of ~207 survivors, ~190 T free). Mechanism check against the baselines: this is the first rule to spend any of the approximation budget on this circuit (the whole current book is exact), and BQSKit-DPF reaches 8020 against pyzx's exact-contract 11485 on the same input, i.e. about 3500 T on qpe_8 is reachable only by numerical window refitting rather than by rotation merging - which is precisely the mechanism here, reproduced with scipy least_squares instead of BQSKit instantiation. Estimate: 30-65 angles pinned across the window set (half the windows yielding at least one pin), i.e. ~1600-3450 T plus the eps_rz relief, so 13603 -> roughly 10300-12000. I deliberately quote the low-middle of that band as the point estimate: the one earlier attempt on this circuit overshot 14x because it assumed structural coincidences (shared parity labels) that the H density destroyed, whereas the quantity this rule depends on - per-window angle redundancy - is bounded below by nothing, so the honest expectation is that only windows with k >= 4 rotations on <= 2 qubits pin reliably. CNOT count and qubit count are unchanged (8 qubits), so the tie-breakers after T are neutral.

Younis et al., 'BQSKit: Berkeley Quantum Synthesis Toolkit' - the instantiation-based re-fit of a fixed circuit template to a target unitary that underlies BQSKit's approximate passes; the angle-pinning / parameter-redundancy formulation follows L. Madden and A. Simonetto, 'Best approximate quantum compiling problems', ACM Trans. Quantum Computing 3(2), 2022, and the T-cost model of the pinned-vs-free angles is Ross-Selinger gridsynth (N. J. Ross, P. Selinger, 'Optimal ancilla-free Clifford+T approximation of z-rotations', QIC 16(11-12), 2016), in which multiples of pi/4 are exactly representable at zero cost.

card.name: pauli_exponential_commutation_merge
card.identity: Global Pauli-rotation normal form with commutation-reordering, then merge. (1) Sweep the op list left to right carrying a Clifford tableau C = product of all Clifford ops seen so far (h, s, sdg, x, z, cx, cz; t/tdg handled as rotations, see below). For every rotation op k at position p_k, acting as rz(theta_k) on wire q_k, compute its FRONT-FRAME Pauli P_k = C_k^dag Z_{q_k} C_k (C_k = the Clifford prefix before position p_k), with its sign eta_k in {+1,-1} taken from the tableau; so the op equals, as a factor commuted to the circuit's front, exp(-i eta_k theta_k P_k / 2) with P_k a signed n-qubit Pauli that may be X-, Y- or Z-type and may be multi-qubit. The whole circuit is then exactly U = [prod_{k=1..R} exp(-i eta_k theta_k P_k / 2)] . C_final, in op order, R = number of rotation ops, C_final = full Clifford product. (2) MATCH: a pair j < k of rotation records with P_j = +-P_k (as unsigned Pauli strings, sign folded into s = eta_j eta_k (+-1)) such that P_k COMMUTES with P_i for every intermediate rotation record j < i < k. (3) APPLY, in the ORIGINAL op list, with no Clifford touched and no resynthesis: delete op p_k, and set op p_j's angle to theta_eff = (theta_j + s . theta_k) reduced mod 2pi into (-pi, pi]; if theta_eff == 0 delete op p_j as well, if theta_eff is a multiple of pi/4 with_ops demotes it to z/s/sdg/t/tdg (a FULL removal of a synthesized rotation). (4) Rotation records include the explicit t/tdg ops (theta = +-pi/4), but a pair is only reported when at least one member is a non-pi/4-multiple rz, and a (rz, t/tdg) pair only when theta_eff lands on the pi/4 grid, so every reported match strictly lowers N_Rz. Matches are enumerated by descending |theta_j| + |theta_k| and are reported one at a time (positions recomputed after each accepted application).
card.correctness: Two facts, both exact. (a) Frame transport: for any Clifford C and Pauli P, C exp(-i a P/2) = exp(-i a (C P C^dag)/2) C, an identity because C exp(X) C^dag = exp(C X C^dag) and Clifford conjugation maps Paulis to signed Paulis; iterating it over the prefix moves every rotation to the front of the circuit, leaving the Clifford product C_final at the end. The tableau computes exactly C_k^dag Z_{q_k} C_k, including its sign, in the frozen Pauli API (v3.api.pauli.conjugate applied op by op), so the normal form is exact in exact arithmetic on the Clifford part. (b) Commutation and addition: two Pauli exponentials commute whenever their Paulis commute, since [P,Q] = 0 implies exp(-i a P/2) exp(-i b Q/2) = exp(-i b Q/2) exp(-i a P/2); so if P_k commutes with every intermediate P_i, the factor k can be slid left to sit directly after factor j without changing U. Then with P_k = s P_j (same unsigned string) and P_j^2 = I, exp(-i eta_j theta_j P_j/2) exp(-i eta_k theta_k s P_j /2) = exp(-i eta_j (theta_j + s eta_j eta_k theta_k) P_j / 2), i.e. the angles add with the sign s folded in; the merged factor is transported back through the same prefix by the inverse of (a), which is why the edit can be made in place in the original op list: the op list with op p_k deleted and op p_j's angle set to theta_eff has exactly the same normal form, hence the same unitary. The mod-2pi reduction changes only a global phase (Rz(2pi) = -I), permitted by invariant 6. No approximation enters: the only floating point is the angle addition, so the judge's phase-aligned distance on the changed window is at the level of double rounding (and the exact D[omega] check applies whenever the merged angle demotes to a pi/4 multiple, in which case both sides are Clifford+T). No CNOT, no h, no qubit is added or moved; the Clifford skeleton is bit-for-bit unchanged.
card.trigger: Any pair of rotation records in the 1034-op list whose front-frame Paulis agree up to sign and whose later member commutes with every rotation Pauli strictly between them. Crucially, the frame is a general n-qubit Pauli, NOT a Z-parity: an h on the rotation's own wire turns the frame from Z into X and the record simply carries an X-type string onward, so NOTHING cuts at a Hadamard. This is the precise fix for the measured limitation of attempt 1 ('segments end at every H, so few rotations pair up': 3 applications, 192 T) and for the admitted pauli_frame_rotation_merge, which only accepts a pair when the transported axis lands back as +-Z on an earlier rotation's own wire and only when every intermediate rotation commutes trivially in the Z picture. qpe_8 is the worst case for both of those and the best case for this one: 258 h against 257 rz, with the trigram census dominated by h-interleaved rotations ('h rz rz' 42x, 'h rz h' 40x, 'rz h h' 40x, 'rz h rz' 28x, 'sdg h rz' 28x, 'h cx rz' 34x, 'cx rz h' 30x), i.e. the pairs that must merge are separated by exactly the gates that the existing passes refuse to cross. The commutation test (not adjacency) is what lets a rotation travel past the whole QPE controlled-phase ladder: in QPE, every controlled-phase rotation of one Fourier stage is diagonal in a common frame, so the intermediate Paulis pairwise commute and long-range pairs are legal.
card.expected_effect: Each surviving non-grid rz costs gridsynth ~53 T at the current operating point (13603 T / 257 rotations). A merged pair removes one rotation (~53 T); a pair that cancels mod 2pi, or that lands on the pi/4 grid, removes two (~106 T). The angle histogram makes the cancellations concrete: theta = 10.566379 (x15) and theta = 1.999991 (x15) satisfy 10.566379 + 1.999991 = 12.566370 = 4pi to 1e-6, and 0.331877 (x15), 7.097863 (x15), 5.922029 (x14) likewise pair against each other mod 2pi; QPE's structure (the same controlled-U^{2^k} block repeated across 8 ancilla wires, then the inverse QFT) is exactly why 55 distinct angles appear with multiplicities 15/15/15/15/14/11x9, and the repeats of a given angle sit in the SAME Pauli frame up to sign once the Hadamards between stages are transported rather than used as cut points. Nothing in the current book is non-Clifford-frame aware, and the gap this rule attacks is the one between the exact-contract passes (pyzx 11485, current book 13603) and the 8020 that is reachable on this input. Estimate: 35-55 rotations retired, ~1900-2900 T, i.e. 13603 -> roughly 10700-11700, on the exact contract, spending none of the 5e-4 approximation budget, with CNOT and qubit count unchanged at 268 / 8.
card.source: A. Cowtan, S. Dilkes, R. Duncan, W. Simmons, S. Sivarajah, 'Phase Gadget Synthesis for Shallow Circuits', EPTCS 318 (QPL 2019) — Pauli-exponential (phase/Pauli gadget) normal form and commutation-based merging; D. Litinski, 'A Game of Surface Codes' (Quantum 3, 128, 2019) Sec. 3 — compiling a Clifford+T circuit to a sequence of pi/8 Pauli rotations followed by a final Clifford; Y. Nam, N. J. Ross, Y. Su, A. M. Childs, D. Maslov, npj QI 4:23 (2018) — rotation merging, whose Hadamard-bounded-segment restriction this lifts.

card.trigger: Any pair of rotation records in the 1034-op list whose front-frame Paulis agree up to sign and whose later member commutes with every rotation Pauli strictly between them. The commutation test (not adjacency) is what lets a rotation travel past the whole QPE controlled-phase ladder: in QPE, every controlled-phase rotation of one Fourier stage is diagonal in a common frame, so the intermediate Paulis pairwise commute and long-range pairs are legal.
card.expected_effect: Each surviving non-grid rz costs gridsynth ~53 T at the current operating point (13603 T / 257 rotations). card.name: rotation_count_minimal_block_refit
card.identity: Numerical re-instantiation of small windows against an ansatz chosen to minimise the NUMBER of non-Clifford Z-rotations, not the gate count. (1) Partition the op list into blocks: scan left to right and grow a block greedily while its qubit support stays <= 3 and every op added is dependency-contiguous (an op may join only if no op outside the block separates it from the block on a shared wire); close the block when a 4th qubit would be needed. Record for each block B its qubit support S (|S| = 1, 2 or 3), its exact target unitary U_B = product of its ops (dense 2^|S| matrix, built with numpy from the op list; rz angles as given), its number of non-Clifford rotations r_B (ops with rotation(op) not None and angle not a multiple of pi/4) and its CX/CZ count c_B. (2) For each block with r_B >= 2, search for a shorter realisation: enumerate candidate ansaetze A(r, c) in lexicographic order of (r, c) for r = 0, 1, ..., r_B - 1 and c = 0, ..., c_B, where A(r, c) is a fixed template of c two-qubit Cliffords (CX/CZ on the pairs actually used inside B, in the order they occur in B) interleaved with single-qubit layers, each single-qubit layer being an Euler word rz(x) h rz(y) h rz(z) on each wire of S; the free parameters are all the rz angles, of which at most r are allowed to stay non-Clifford and the rest are CONSTRAINED to the Clifford+T grid (multiples of pi/4, enumerated over the 8 values, or solved for and then snapped). Instantiate the free angles by least-squares minimisation of the phase-invariant residual f(theta) = 1 - |tr(V(theta)^dag U_B)| / 2^|S| with scipy.optimize (L-BFGS-B / least_squares), from K = 30 deterministic restarts (fixed seed; include the block's own angles and the Euler angles of the KAK/ZXZ decomposition of U_B as starts). (3) Accept the first (r, c) whose best fit reaches phase-aligned operator distance d_B = || V(theta) - e^{i phi} U_B ||_2 <= 1e-10 with r < r_B and c <= c_B. (4) Post-snap: any fitted angle within 1e-10 of a multiple of pi/4 is emitted as the exact Clifford/T gate (with_ops does this), any angle within 1e-10 of 0 or 2pi is dropped; re-measure d_B after snapping. (5) The match is (block span, replacement op list); apply() splices the replacement in place of the block's ops, every op outside the block byte-identical. Emit matches for all blocks that compress, in block order; the runner verifies and costs each one separately. Degenerate case |S| = 1 is the classical Euler collapse: any maximal single-wire run, however many rz and h it contains, is realised by rz h rz h rz, i.e. at most 3 non-Clifford rotations.
card.correctness: Three separate arguments. (a) The target is exact: U_B is the product of the block's own ops computed in dense linear algebra, so the specification of the local rewrite is exactly 'replace a unitary by another unitary on the same qubits'. Since the block is dependency-contiguous (no outside op interleaves on a shared wire), the global circuit factors as W_2 (U_B tensor I) W_1, and replacing U_B by V gives W_2 (V tensor I) W_1; by unitary invariance and submultiplicativity of the operator norm, || W_2 (V tensor I) W_1 - e^{i phi} W_2 (U_B tensor I) W_1 || = || V - e^{i phi} U_B || = d_B. So the global error contributed by the block is exactly its measured local distance, which is what the frozen judge charges to the budget; errors of different blocks add subadditively, total <= sum d_B. With d_B <= 1e-10 and at most a few hundred blocks the total charge is <= 1e-7, four orders of magnitude under the approx allowance eps/2 = 5e-4, so this rule consumes essentially none of the error budget and does not tighten eps_rz for the surviving rotations. (b) Completeness of the ansatz family: the Euler word rz(x) h rz(y) h rz(z) generates all of SU(2) up to global phase (ZXZ Euler angles, since h rz(y) h = rx(y)), and interleaving arbitrary single-qubit layers with the block's own CX/CZ pattern reproduces the block itself as one member of the family (take the block's own angles), so the search is a restriction, never an extension, of what the original block can express: for c = c_B and r = r_B the fit is exact by construction, and the enumeration simply asks whether a smaller r suffices. Hence an accepted fit is always a strict reduction in non-Clifford rotation count at no increase in two-qubit gate count. (c) Why slack exists at all on a TKET-FullPeepholeOptimise'd input: TKET's peephole optimises two-qubit blocks for CX count and total gate count under the KAK decomposition, and squashes single-qubit runs into a normal form with up to three rotations each; it does not minimise the number of rotations whose angle is NOT a multiple of pi/4, which is the only thing the gridsynth cost model charges for. A KAK Cartan vector with components that are multiples of pi/4 (exactly what QFT/QPE controlled-phase gates produce: the dyadic angles pi/8, pi/16, pi/32, 5pi/64 visible in the angle histogram arise from controlled-rz gates whose Cartan part is a single non-Clifford angle plus Clifford local terms) is emitted by TKET as three generic rotations; the (r, c) enumeration with the non-free angles pinned to the pi/4 grid finds the representation that keeps one non-Clifford angle and makes the other two Clifford. The judge re-verifies every single application, so a bad fit cannot be accepted: an accepted application is certified by the frozen verifier, not by the optimiser's residual.
card.trigger: Any dependency-contiguous block of consecutive ops with qubit support of size <= 3 containing at least 2 non-Clifford rotations (angle not a multiple of pi/4), for which step (2)-(3) finds a fit with phase-aligned distance <= 1e-10, strictly fewer non-Clifford rotations and no more CX/CZ gates than the block. On hhl_8 the op list is 2208 ops on 8 qubits with 497 cx, 583 rz, 607 h, 175 s, 119 sdg, 101 t, 101 tdg: greedy <= 3-qubit blocks between the points where a 4th qubit enters give on the order of 150-250 blocks, and with 583 non-Clifford rotations the rotation-rich blocks (the trigram table shows the dominant local shapes 'h rz h' x117, 'rz cx rz' x79, 'rz h s' x92, 'h s cx' x92, 'sdg h rz' x58, i.e. rotations sandwiched between Cliffords on few wires) typically carry 3-8 non-Clifford rotations on 2-3 wires - far below the 15 (SU(4)) / 63 (SU(8)) parameters the ansatz family provides, so each such block is heavily over-parameterised and compresses. Blocks that do not compress simply emit no match. The rule is orthogonal to the two book rules: pauli_frame_rotation_merge and pauli_exponential_commutation_merge only ever DELETE a rotation whose transported axis equals +-Z on an earlier rotation's qubit and which commutes with every rotation in between (that pairwise test is necessary as well as sufficient for same-axis merging with a fixed Clifford skeleton, which is why they saturate at the pyzx phase-teleportation number 29205); this rule instead REBUILDS the Clifford skeleton of a block numerically and so removes rotations that no same-axis merge can ever reach.
card.expected_effect: Every non-Clifford rotation removed saves one gridsynth sequence. At the current N_Rz the per-rotation cost is 3 log2(1/eps_rz) + O(log log) ~ 55-59 T, and because eps_rz = eps_synth / N_Rz, dropping rotations also loosens eps_rz for all survivors (about 0.8 T less per surviving rotation per 100 removed). Expected compression: single-wire runs give the Euler bound (<= 3 non-Clifford rotations per maximal run, worth a few tens of rotations); the bulk comes from 2-qubit and 3-qubit rotation-rich blocks, where the pi/4-pinned enumeration typically turns a 4-6 rotation block into a 2-3 rotation block, i.e. roughly a 35-45% cut in rotation count overall. From 583 rotations down to ~360-380 is ~210 rotations removed: ~210 x 57 = ~12000 T less, partly offset because the survivors' per-rotation count is only mildly cheaper and because some blocks will not compress at all (dependency-contiguous <= 3-qubit windows in a circuit with 497 CNOTs on 8 qubits are sometimes too narrow to contain 2 rotations). Netting that out against the measured ceiling of the best numerical-refit baseline on this circuit (BQSKit-DPF, 19443 T, which is exactly the regime a <= 3-qubit numerical re-instantiation pass reaches), I expect ~29205 -> ~21500-22000. CX count cannot regress (c <= c_B per block), qubit count is untouched (no ancillas), and the error charge is ~1e-7 total, so no lexicographic tie-breaker and no budget constraint is harmed.
card.source: Numerical instantiation / block resynthesis as in BQSKit: Younis, Iancu, Lavrijsen, Davis, Smith, 'QFAST / Berkeley Quantum Synthesis Toolkit' and Smith, Davis, Younis et al., 'LEAP: Scaling numerical optimization-based synthesis using an incremental approach' (ACM TQC 2022); Patel, Younis, Iancu, de Jong, Mueller, 'QUEST: systematically approximating quantum circuits' (2022) for accepting fits under an explicit distance budget; KAK / Cartan two-qubit decomposition from Tucci and Vatan-Williams, 'Optimal quantum circuits for general two-qubit gates' (PRA 69, 032315); Ross and Selinger, 'Optimal ancilla-free Clifford+T approximation of z-rotations' (arXiv:1403.2975) for the 3 log2(1/eps) cost model that makes rotation COUNT, not gate count, the objective.

card.name: shared_and_value_cache_by_anf_matching
card.identity:
Globally cache AND values by symbolic wire-value matching, so that one 4-T temporary-AND ancilla serves every ccz/ccx in the circuit whose control pair carries the SAME pair of logical values, no matter how far apart they are and no matter how the control wires are overwritten in between.

(1) Symbolic pass. Give each of the n input wires a free GF(2) variable. Sweep the gate list and keep, for every wire, its current value as an algebraic normal form (ANF) polynomial over those variables (a set of monomials, canonicalized and sorted; cap the monomial count, e.g. 64, and mark a wire UNKNOWN on overflow):
   x(q):      v[q] <- v[q] + 1
   cx(c,t):   v[t] <- v[t] + v[c]
   ccx(a,b,t):v[t] <- v[t] + v[a]*v[b]   (polynomial product, reduced by u^2 = u)
   z/s/sdg/t/tdg/cz/ccz/rz: diagonal, v unchanged
   h(q):      v[q] <- UNKNOWN (and any later gate with an UNKNOWN control is skipped by this rule)
   measure / classically controlled gates: v[target] <- UNKNOWN

(2) Product key. For each ccz/ccx gate g at index i with controls {c1,c2} (target z), if v[c1] and v[c2] are both known, its key is the unordered pair K(g) = {v[c1], v[c2]} of ANF polynomials -- the logical bit the gate needs is the product of those two polynomials. Group all ccz/ccx gates by key. A group with occurrences i_1 < ... < i_k (k >= 1) is one match.

(3) Emission for a match with key {p,q} and occurrences i_1..i_k. At i_1, before the gate, allocate one CLEAN ancilla a in |0> and emit the 4-T temporary-AND compute A(c1,c2 -> a) on the wires that currently hold p and q (|p,q,0> -> |p,q,p&q|, controls untouched, exactly 4 pi/4 rotations in a Clifford skeleton of H/S/CX). Replace each occurrence i_j by cz(a, z_j) if g_{i_j} is ccz, or cx(a, z_j) if it is ccx (the target wire of each occurrence is whatever that gate's own target was; targets may differ between occurrences and may be rewritten in between -- irrelevant). After the last occurrence i_k, emit the 0-T measured uncompute: h(a); measure(a) -> m; classically controlled cz on the two wires that hold p and q at that point (the controls of g_{i_k}); retire a to the free pool.

card.name: shared_and_value_cache_by_anf_matching
card.identity:
Globally cache AND values by symbolic wire-value matching, so that one 4-T temporary-AND ancilla serves every ccz/ccx in the circuit whose control pair carries the SAME pair of logical values, no matter how far apart they are and no matter how the control wires are overwritten in between.

(1) Symbolic pass. Give each of the n input wires a free GF(2) variable. Sweep the gate list and keep, for every wire, its current value as an algebraic normal form (ANF) polynomial over those variables (a set of monomials, canonicalized and sorted; cap the monomial count, e.g. 64, and mark a wire UNKNOWN on overflow):
   x(q):      v[q] <- v[q] + 1
   cx(c,t):   v[t] <- v[t] + v[c]
   ccx(a,b,t):v[t] <- v[t] + v[a]*v[b]   (polynomial product, reduced by u^2 = u)
   z/s/sdg/t/tdg/cz/ccz/rz: diagonal, v unchanged
   h(q):      v[q] <- UNKNOWN (and any later gate with an UNKNOWN control is skipped by this rule)
   measure / classically controlled gates: v[target] <- UNKNOWN

(2) Product key. For each ccz/ccx gate g at index i with controls {c1,c2} (target z), if v[c1] and v[c2] are both known, its key is the unordered pair K(g) = {v[c1], v[c2]} of ANF polynomials -- the logical bit the gate needs is the product of those two polynomials. (3) Emission for a match with key {p,q} and occurrences i_1..i_k. At i_1, before the gate, allocate one CLEAN ancilla a in |0> and emit the 4-T temporary-AND compute A(c1,c2 -> a) on the wires that currently hold p and q (|p,q,0> -> |p,q,p&q|, controls untouched, exactly 4 pi/4 rotations in a Clifford skeleton of H/S/CX). After the last occurrence i_k, emit the 0-T measured uncompute: h(a); measure(a) -> m; classically controlled cz on the two wires that hold p and q at that point (the controls of g_{i_k}); retire a to the free pool.

(4) Ancilla pool. Live intervals [i_1, i_k] of different matches may overlap; allocate from a pool and reuse, so the qubit count grows by the peak number of simultaneously live cached AND bits.

Cost: 4 T per DISTINCT key, instead of the current book's 4 T per maximal ADJACENT same-control-pair run.

card.name: quadratic_and_count_minimization_over_f2
card.identity: Reuse the (already implemented) Toffoli-level extraction that turns an H-sandwiched CCZ/CCX segment into a classical F2 update y_k ^= Q_k(a,b) on disjoint read-only registers A, B and target register Y (each group 'h t; ccz(x_i,y_i,t)*; h t' equals t ^= XOR_i (x_i & y_i), propagated symbolically together with the plain cx/x gates). Where the admitted rule then looks for a BILINEAR rank decomposition Q_k = sum_r c_{k,r} (u_r.a)(v_r.b) and pays 4 T per rank-1 term, this rule searches the strictly larger class of QUADRATIC (non-bilinear) straight-line F2 programs: a program is a sequence of R AND steps s_r = L_r(a,b,s_1..s_{r-1}) & L'_r(a,b,s_1..s_{r-1}) with L, L' arbitrary AFFINE forms over all input bits AND all previously computed AND results, followed by affine output forms Q_k = A_k(a,b,s_1..s_R). Two features of F2 make this class strictly stronger than the bilinear one: (i) squaring is linear, x^2 = x, so an AND of two forms that both mix A and B expands as L&L' = (bilinear part) XOR (affine self-terms from x_i^2 = x_i) XOR (unwanted a_i a_j / b_i b_j cross terms); the affine self-terms are FREE (they are absorbed into the final affine output forms, i.e. into cx/x gates), and only the genuine a_i a_j, b_i b_j cross terms must cancel across the R steps; (ii) feeding an AND output back into a later AND input produces degree-3+ intermediates that a bilinear algorithm cannot use, and these can also cancel. Hence the proven-optimal bilinear count for a map is only an upper bound here, not a floor. Procedure: (1) extract the tensor T_{ijk} / the forms Q_k; (2) compute the bilinear rank R0 by the existing path (9 for GF(2^4) multiplication mod x^4+x+1, the mult_4 map); (3) run a bounded exact search for a quadratic program with R = R0-1 AND steps: encode the unknown affine coefficient vectors of L_r, L'_r and of the output forms A_k as F2 unknowns, and the requirement 'program output == Q_k identically as polynomials' as an F2 polynomial-identity system; solve it with a SAT/CP search over the coefficient bits (sympy / pure-python DPLL is enough at this size: for mult_4, R=8, 8 variables of width <= 8+r each, with the standard symmetry breaking -- fix the affine part of L_1, order the steps lexicographically, and fix the free self-term coefficients to 0 in the output forms since they are absorbed anyway), with a hard node/time budget; (4) if a program is found, VERIFY it symbolically over the F2 polynomial ring against the extracted Q_k, then emit it: for each AND step, CX/X the affine form L_r into clean ancilla p and L'_r into clean ancilla q (Clifford, free), Gidney AND-compute p&q -> clean ancilla s_r (4 T), keep s_r alive only as long as a later step or output form needs it, measured-uncompute s_r (0 T), undo the fan-ins; finally emit the affine output forms as cx/x into Y. Cost 4R T. (5) If no program with R < R0 is found inside the budget, do not fire (the admitted bilinear rule keeps its result); if one is found, this rule supersedes it on that segment.
card.correctness: Three independent exact steps. (1) Extraction is an identity of unitaries, unchanged from the admitted rule: a group of CCZs sharing target t imposes phase (-1)^{t . XOR_i (x_i y_i)} = CZ(t, f) with f = XOR_i (x_i & y_i), and H.CZ(t,f).H = CX(f,t); since A and B are never written in the segment all updates commute, so the segment is exactly the classical map y -> y XOR Q(a,b). (2) The replacement program is checked to compute the SAME map by symbolic identity over F2[a_0..a_{n-1}, b_0..b_{m-1}]: the candidate program is evaluated as polynomials with x_i^2 reduced to x_i (the correct reduction, since every variable is a bit, i.e. we work in the Boolean quotient ring F2[x]/(x_i^2 - x_i), which is exactly the ring of Boolean functions), and the resulting output polynomials must be equal coefficientwise to Q_k. This check is what makes the non-bilinear self-terms sound: they are real contributions to the polynomial and are either cancelled by other steps or cancelled by the affine output forms, and the identity check sees them. Nothing is accepted on the basis of the search encoding alone. (3) Each emitted primitive is exact: CX/X fan-in of an affine form is Clifford; the Gidney AND gadget (Quantum 2 (2018)) computes |p AND q> on a clean ancilla with 4 T gates, and its uncomputation is an X-basis measurement of the ancilla plus a classically controlled CZ, exact and 0 T; all fan-ins are undone, so every ancilla starts and ends in |0>. Phase consistency (invariant 2): the only non-Clifford elements are inside AND gadgets whose branch-dependent phase is exactly cancelled by the classically controlled fix-up, so every measurement branch applies the same c_m = 1 to all inputs and sum_m |c_m|^2 = 1; hence the relaxed specification check (function + ancillas restored + phase consistency) is the correct contract. Because the AND steps may now be nested, the ancilla lifetimes are computed from the program's data dependencies and each ancilla is uncomputed in reverse order of its last use, which keeps the 'clean in, clean out' property.
card.trigger: Toffoli-level IRCircuit. (a) Same segment detection as the admitted bilinear rule: maximal H-sandwiched CCZ/CCX groups, every non-Clifford gate a ccz/ccx whose controls lie in a wire set X that is never written in the segment, targets in a disjoint set Y whose only other gates are cx/x/cz among Y wires. (b) Symbolically propagate to the Boolean forms Q_k on each y_k in Y (degree 2 in the X variables here, but the rule does not require bilinearity or a bipartite A/B split -- that relaxation is part of the point, so it also fires on segments the bilinear rule rejects). (c) Compute the baseline count R0 = the number of AND gadgets the current book would use on this segment (bilinear rank if the bipartite split exists, else distinct monomials). (d) Run the bounded quadratic-program search for R = R0 - 1, then R0 - 2, under a fixed node/time budget. (e) Fire once on the whole segment only if a symbolically verified program with R < R0 exists; emit with up to 2 + (max live AND results) appended clean ancillas. On mult_4 the segment is the whole circuit, X = q0..q7, Y = q8..q11, Q = GF(2^4) multiplication mod x^4+x+1, R0 = 9.
card.expected_effect: On mult_4 the 9 Gidney AND gadgets of the current (Karatsuba, bilinear-rank-9) implementation are replaced by R < 9 AND gadgets, each 4 T, with the extra affine corrections and the a_i a_j / b_i b_j cancellation terms costing only cx/x gates. The exhaustive bilinear search (Barbulescu-Detrey-Estibals-Zimmermann) proves 9 is optimal among BILINEAR formulae for GF(2^4) multiplication, so this is the only remaining direction: the quadratic class is not covered by that bound because over F2 the squaring map is linear and because AND outputs may be re-multiplied. Realistic outcome R = 8: T 36 -> 32 (and qubits rise by at most 1-2 over the current 15, CNOT count rises by roughly 20-40, both lexicographically below T). If the search closes R = 8 as infeasible it does not fire and nothing regresses; if it reaches R = 7 the gain doubles to 8 T. Secondary value: the same pass is the general AND-count minimizer for every other dv_recon target (adder_8, mcx_10, modred_21), where the current book uses one 4-T AND per Toffoli run and no rank/quadratic reduction has been attempted at all.
card.source: Boyar, Matthews & Peralta, 'Logic minimization techniques with applications to cryptology', J. Cryptology 26 (2013) (multiplicative complexity over F2; AND-count minimization with free XOR, exploiting x^2 = x); Courtois, Hulme & Mourouzis, 'Solving circuit optimisation problems in cryptography and cryptanalysis', IACR ePrint 2011/475 (SAT-based exact AND-count search); Barbulescu, Detrey, Estibals & Zimmermann, 'Finding optimal formulae for bilinear maps', WAIFI 2012 (bilinear complexity of GF(2^n) multiplication: 9 for n = 4, optimal among bilinear formulae -- the bound this rule is designed to go around); Gidney, 'Halving the cost of quantum addition', Quantum 2 (2018) (4-T AND with measurement-based uncomputation).

Since no Q_k depends on any y, U_seg = (prod_k H_{y_k}) . D . (prod_k H_{y_k}) with D = diag((-1)^{f(x,y)}), f = sum_k y_k Q_k(x), a Boolean polynomial of degree 3 in the FULL variable set v = (x, y) (for mult_4: 12 variables a0..a3, b0..b3, y0..y3, Q = GF(2^4) multiplication mod x^4+x+1, f has 22 cubic monomials y_k a_i b_j). (2) The T-cost of D is the minimum number R of products of three AFFINE forms needed to write f MODULO any degree-<=2 polynomial: f = sum_{r=1..R} L_r.v M_r.v N_r.v + g(v), deg g <= 2, as an identity of BOOLEAN functions (x_i^2 = x_i), because every quadratic/linear phase is Clifford and therefore free: (-1)^{v_i v_j} = CZ(i,j), (-1)^{v_i} = Z(i), signs = S/global phase. (4) Emission: for each of the R terms, CX/X the affine forms L_r, M_r, N_r into three clean ancillas p, q, s (Clifford, free), apply ccz(p,q,s) lowered by the book's and_compute/and_uncompute path (Gidney AND into a 4th clean ancilla, cz into s, measured uncompute: 4 T, 0 T for the uncompute), then undo the three fan-ins; ancillas are reused across r. card.name: mcx_truthtable_recognition_and_ladder_resynthesis
card.identity: Two-part rule. (1) RECOGNITION by complete truth-table simulation with bitmask arithmetic: a Toffoli-level segment of {ccz, ccx, cx, x, h} (h only as the h-ccz-h sandwich that makes a ccz into a ccx on that leg) over n <= 20 wires is a classical reversible network. Assign wire i the Boolean function 'input bit i' encoded as a single Python integer f_i of 2^n bits, where bit b of f_i is the value of wire i under the input assignment b (i.e. f_i = the fixed constant mask with bit b set iff b has bit i set; these are the standard n 'column masks' of an n-variable truth table). Simulate the gate list forward, updating only the written wire: x(a): f_a ^= FULL; cx(a,b): f_b ^= f_a; ccx(a,b,c): f_c ^= (f_a & f_b); cz/ccz on controls only after rewriting via the h-sandwich. No simplification, no sympy, no BDD -- every operation is one machine-word-parallel AND/XOR on a 2^n-bit integer, so the whole segment costs O(|gates| * 2^n / 64) word ops (for n = 19: 66 gates x 8 KiB = microseconds). Fire iff the final masks are: f_q == (column mask of q) for all q != t (every other wire exactly the identity function, including dirty ancilla wires, for ALL input values), and f_t == (column mask of t) XOR (AND over q in S of column mask of q) for exactly one wire t and a set S with |S| >= 4. The match records (t, S); emit at most ONE match per maximal segment and bail at the first mismatch, so the trigger is a single linear pass. (2) EMISSION: delete the whole recognized segment and rebuild t ^= AND(S) as Gidney's temporary-logical-AND ladder on k-1 = |S|-1 CLEAN ancillas: b1 = and_compute(s1, s2); b_i = and_compute(b_{i-1}, s_{i+1}) for i = 2..k-1; cx(b_{k-1}, t); then and_uncompute(b_{k-1}), ..., and_uncompute(b1) in reverse. and_compute is the 4-T clean-ancilla AND gadget; and_uncompute is H + Z-basis measurement with a classically controlled CZ fix-up on its two inputs, 0 T. Wires that the segment used as ancillas are provably untouched by the rest of the circuit's data flow only if they are not read elsewhere, so the emission does not reuse them: it requests k-1 fresh ancillas via ir_with_gates(..., n_qubits=n+extra), and the balanced-tree ordering is an equally valid emission with the same gadget count.
card.correctness: Recognition is exact and complete, not heuristic: the 2^n-bit mask of a wire IS its full truth table over all n input wires, and the three update rules are exactly the Boolean semantics of x/cx/ccx. Equality of masks is therefore equality of functions on every one of the 2^n inputs, so firing certifies the segment's output map is precisely t -> t XOR AND(S) with every other wire (controls AND dirty-borrowed ancillas, for arbitrary ancilla input values) returned unchanged. This is why no ancilla-liveness analysis is needed and why the pathological cost of symbolic canonicalization disappears. Emission: and_compute(x,y -> a) maps |x>|y>|0> to |x>|y>|x&y> exactly with no relative phase, so by induction b1 = s1&s2 and b_i = b_{i-1}&s_{i+1} = s1&...&s_{i+1}, giving b_{k-1} = AND(S); cx(b_{k-1}, t) sets t ^= AND(S), matching the recognized function. and_uncompute measures the ancilla in the X basis; the outcome m is uniform and independent of the data, and conditioned on m the residual operator on the two input wires is CZ^m, cancelled by the classically controlled CZ. Hence for every branch m the Kraus operator is K_m|x> = c_m|f(x)> with c_m = 2^{-1/2} independent of x (phase consistency, invariant 2) and sum_m |c_m|^2 = 1; ancillas end in |0> after the gadget's classically controlled X. Nothing is charged to the error budget.
card.trigger: One maximal contiguous segment of the op list whose gates lie in {ccz, ccx, cx, x, h} with every h paired as h-ccz-h / h-ccx-h on a single leg (so the segment is a pure classical reversible ccx/cx/x network), with n <= 20 wires in the circuit (hard guard: if n > 20 the rule returns no match immediately, bounding the mask size at 2^20 bits = 128 KiB). card.name: xag_multiplicative_complexity_resynthesis
card.identity: Function-level resynthesis of any Hadamard-free classical segment through an XOR-AND-inverter graph (XAG), paying 4 T per AND node and 0 T for every XOR/inverter. (1) Fold every h(q) ccz(c1,c2,q) h(q) trigram into ccx(c1,c2;q) (in adder_6 all 22 h's sit in the 11 'h ccz h' trigrams); the segment is then an op list over {x, cx, ccx} = a classical reversible permutation F on the 14 wires. (2) Symbolically simulate F over GF(2): each wire w gets its output ANF O_w in the input variables (declared-clean ancillas pinned to 0). No pattern library, no adder template. (3) Build an XAG for the whole output map by sequential AND extraction over the set S of ALREADY AVAILABLE signals (initially the input variables, i.e. the GF(2)-linear span L(S) of the live wires): repeatedly search for a product g*h, with g,h in L(S) (candidate linear forms taken from the supports appearing in the remaining ANFs, enumerated over subsets of size <= 3 plus the pairwise sums of current carries/partial results), such that for some not-yet-realized target ANF the residue O - g*h drops in algebraic degree or in monomial count; add node m = g*h to S (so later nodes may use it, which is the common-subexpression step) and continue until every O_w lies in L(S). Let A = number of AND nodes. (4) Emit the circuit: for each AND node m = g*h, build g and h onto two scratch wires with cx/x (or in place when g,h are already single wires), then and_compute(g_wire, h_wire -> anc_m) [4 T, Gidney gadget |x,y,0> -> |x,y,x&y>]; realize each output wire as its linear form over S with cx/x; then walk the AND nodes in reverse and release each one with and_uncompute(anc_m) = H(anc_m), X-basis measurement, classically controlled cz(g_wire, h_wire) [0 T], undoing the cx's that built g,h just before each release so both factor wires still hold g,h at release time. Total non-Clifford cost = 4*A, independent of how many ccx/ccz the input had. Fires only if 4*A is strictly below the current cost of the segment.
card.correctness: ANF is a unique normal form, so step (2) computes each output wire's Boolean function exactly on all inputs, and step (3)-(4) is verified against that same function: the emitted circuit's output ANF is, by construction, the linear form chosen for each wire over S, and each XAG node's value is exactly g*h because Gidney's compute-AND gadget realizes |x,y>|0> -> |x,y>|x AND y> exactly with no residual relative phase, so cx(anc_m -> z) acts as ccx(g,h;z) on every basis state. Linear forms are built with cx/x, which are exact permutations. Because the schedule is CHOSEN by the rule (not matched against pre-existing gate pairs), every ancilla is released at a point where its two factor wires are restored to g and h by construction; H + X-basis measurement collapses anc_m to |0> and the classically controlled CZ(g_wire,h_wire) cancels the measurement-induced (-1)^{m*(g AND h)} phase, so each branch m applies K_m|v> = c_m|F(v)> with the same c_m for all v and sum_m |c_m|^2 = 1 (phase consistency). All ancillas are clean in and out, the permutation is reproduced wire by wire, and the only freedom left is global phase. Soundness does not depend on the AND-extraction heuristic: a wrong or suboptimal factorization simply fails the final 'every O_w in L(S)' check (rule does not fire) or is caught by the judge's relaxed specification check; the heuristic only affects A, i.e. the gain.
card.trigger: A dv_recon IRCircuit (or its maximal segment between the first and last ccx/ccz) that becomes Hadamard-free after folding all h-ccz-h / h-ccx-h trigrams, i.e. contains only x, cx, ccx, ccz, with >= 2 ccx/ccz gates. No family-specific pattern is required: the trigger is purely (a) Hadamard-free-after-folding, (b) step-(3) terminates with every output ANF inside L(S), and (c) 4*A < current non-Clifford cost of the segment (so it can never raise T). This is deliberately a weaker, family-blind trigger than the earlier adder-specification card, which never fired because it demanded an exact ripple-carry ANF pattern with named A/B/carry wire lists.
card.expected_effect: adder_6's 11 ccx/ccz currently cost 11 x 4 = 44 T because the book pays one AND gadget per gate. At the function level the 6-bit sum needs only the carry chain: each carry satisfies C_{i+1} = a_i + (a_i + b_i)(a_i + C_i), one AND node per carry over signals already available (a_i, b_i, C_i), and the sum bits are pure XORs. Sequential AND extraction therefore returns A = 5 (or 6 if the carry-in wire holds a variable), i.e. 20-24 T, with the 11 ccx and 22 h all gone, replaced by ~30 cx/x, 5-6 and_compute, 5-6 measured and_uncompute (0 T) and 5-6 extra clean ancillas (14 -> ~19 qubits; T is first in the lexicographic order). Result ~20-24 T vs 44 now, far below pyzx 47 / TKET 59 / BQSKit 77. The same trigger should also reduce mcx_10 (single degree-k monomial: A = k-1 AND nodes) and reproduce the Karatsuba count on mult_4 without the bilinear special case.

card.name: xag_multiplicative_complexity_resynthesis
card.identity: Function-level resynthesis of any Hadamard-free classical segment through an XOR-AND-inverter graph (XAG), paying 4 T per AND node and 0 T for every XOR/inverter. (1) Fold every h(q) ccz(c1,c2,q) h(q) trigram into ccx(c1,c2;q) (in adder_6 all 22 h's sit in the 11 'h ccz h' trigrams); the segment is then an op list over {x, cx, ccx} = a classical reversible permutation F on the 14 wires. (2) Symbolically simulate F over GF(2): each wire w gets its output ANF O_w in the input variables (declared-clean ancillas pinned to 0). No pattern library, no adder template. (3) Build an XAG for the whole output map by sequential AND extraction over the set S of ALREADY AVAILABLE signals (initially the input variables, i.e. the GF(2)-linear span L(S) of the live wires): repeatedly search for a product g*h, with g,h in L(S) (candidate linear forms taken from the supports appearing in the remaining ANFs, enumerated over subsets of size <= 3 plus the pairwise sums of current carries/partial results), such that for some not-yet-realized target ANF the residue O - g*h drops in algebraic degree or in monomial count; add node m = g*h to S (so later nodes may use it, which is the common-subexpression step) and continue until every O_w lies in L(S). Let A = number of AND nodes. (4) Emit the circuit: for each AND node m = g*h, build g and h onto two scratch wires with cx/x (or in place when g,h are already single wires), then and_compute(g_wire, h_wire -> anc_m) [4 T, Gidney gadget |x,y,0> -> |x,y,x&y>]; realize each output wire as its linear form over S with cx/x; then walk the AND nodes in reverse and release each one with and_uncompute(anc_m) = H(anc_m), X-basis measurement, classically controlled cz(g_wire, h_wire) [0 T], undoing the cx's that built g,h just before each release so both factor wires still hold g,h at release time. Total non-Clifford cost = 4*A, independent of how many ccx/ccz the input had. Fires only if 4*A is strictly below the current cost of the segment.
card.correctness: ANF is a unique normal form, so step (2) computes each output wire's Boolean function exactly on all inputs, and step (3)-(4) is verified against that same function: the emitted circuit's output ANF is, by construction, the linear form chosen for each wire over S, and each XAG node's value is exactly g*h because Gidney's compute-AND gadget realizes |x,y>|0> -> |x,y>|x AND y> exactly with no residual relative phase, so cx(anc_m -> z) acts as ccx(g,h;z) on every basis state. Linear forms are built with cx/x, which are exact permutations. Because the schedule is CHOSEN by the rule (not matched against pre-existing gate pairs), every ancilla is released at a point where its two factor wires are restored to g and h by construction; H + X-basis measurement collapses anc_m to |0> and the classically controlled CZ(g_wire,h_wire) cancels the measurement-induced (-1)^{m*(g AND h)} phase, so each branch m applies K_m|v> = c_m|F(v)> with the same c_m for all v and sum_m |c_m|^2 = 1 (phase consistency). All ancillas are clean in and out, the permutation is reproduced wire by wire, and the only freedom left is global phase. card.name: and_ancilla_value_tracking_span
card.identity: Keep ONE temporary logical-AND ancilla live across a span of CCZ/CCX gates that share a control pair, and repair the ancilla with free Clifford gates whenever the circuit's own X gates change the controls' values - instead of moving the X gates or propagating an X frame through the CCZ gates. Let the op list contain gates g_1 < ... < g_k (positions p_1 < ... < p_k, k >= 2, not necessarily adjacent) of the form ccz(a,b,c_i) or ccx(a,b,c_i) on the same unordered pair {a,b}. Rewrite ONLY these three things, leaving every other op byte-for-byte in its original position and order: (1) immediately before p_1 insert and_compute(a,b -> t) on a fresh CLEAN ancilla t [4 T], establishing t = a AND b; (2) replace each g_i by cz(t,c_i) (for ccz) or cx(t,c_i) (for ccx) [0 T]; (3) immediately AFTER each op `x(a)` lying strictly inside the span, insert cx(b,t), and after each `x(b)` insert cx(a,t) [0 T, Clifford]; (4) immediately after p_k insert and_uncompute(t) = X-basis measurement of t plus a classically controlled cz(a,b) [0 T], releasing t for reuse by a later disjoint span. The whole span costs 4 T regardless of k, versus 4k T (current book rule) or 7k T (naive).
card.correctness: Invariant: at every point of the span, t holds the current computational-basis value of a AND b. It holds after and_compute (Gidney/Jones temporary AND, 4 T). The only ops in the span permitted to change the value of a or b are `x` gates on a or b (the trigger forbids h, s/sdg, t/tdg, cx/ccx writing a or b, and measurement of a or b; z/cz/ccz are diagonal and change no basis value). After x(a), write a' = a XOR 1; t stores the stale product a*b = (a' XOR 1)*b = b XOR a'*b, so applying cx(b,t) sets t = a'*b, restoring the invariant; symmetrically cx(a,t) after x(b). Repair gates use only b (resp. a), which is unchanged by that x, so the update is exact. Since t = a AND b is a deterministic function of the two control wires, the state never leaves (data basis state) tensor |a AND b>, and all intervening diagonal gates on a, b apply exactly the same phases as in the original circuit. Data action: CCZ(a,b,c) = CZ(t,c) and CCX(a,b,c) = CX(t,c) pointwise whenever t = a AND b, and these gates only READ t, so the invariant survives them. Nothing is reordered, so no commutation obligation beyond the value-tracking above. Finally and_uncompute returns t to |0> with 0 T; its two measurement branches apply the same data operator up to global phase, so the relaxed contract (function computed, ancilla returns to |0>, per-branch phase consistency, sum |c_m|^2 = 1) holds.
card.trigger: Toffoli-level IRCircuit only (return [] otherwise). Classify per op: VALUE-PRESERVING on a wire = z, cz, ccz (diagonal, read-only) and, for cx/ccx, the control wires; RECOVERABLE WRITE = `x` on a single wire; HARD WRITE = h, s, sdg, t, tdg on the wire, the target of cx/ccx, measurement, or any classically controlled op on the wire. Collect all ccz/ccx ops; for ccx(a,b,c) the only candidate pair is the control pair {a,b}, for ccz all three qubits are symmetric so each ccz offers its three pairs. Group gates by unordered pair {a,b}. A span [p_1,p_k] over a group is LEGAL iff no op strictly inside it is a HARD WRITE to a or to b (ops touching neither wire impose no condition at all; `x` on a or b is allowed and triggers a repair insertion; `x` on target wires and the ccz<->ccx conjugating h's on target wires are irrelevant). If the maximal span is illegal, shrink to the longest legal contiguous sub-run of group members with k >= 2 rather than discarding the pair. Enumerate candidate pairs by descending k, then by shortest span; after emitting a span remove its member gates from the pool so each Toffoli is lowered exactly once. Require k >= 2 (k = 1 is already handled at 4 T by the book rule). Cap: at most one match per pair-and-span, so the match list is O(#ccz) and each apply() touches only its own span - no global re-synthesis, no search.
card.expected_effect: modred_21 is 17 ccz + 30 h + 24 x + 3 cx on 11 qubits, and the book's contiguous-run AND rule measured exactly 119 -> 68 = 4 x 17, i.e. it shared nothing: every run had length 1. The obstruction is the 24 `x` gates that toggle the comparison/modulus controls to get control-on-zero (trigrams 'ccz h x' x14, 'x h ccz' x10, 'h x x' x8), which fail any read-only-control test; the 30 h's sit on TARGET wires (ccz = h ccx h, 'h ccz h' x11) and never mattered. This rule neutralizes the x's on the ANCILLA side with one free cx each, so no CCZ is rewritten and no gate moves - the cheapest possible fix for the exact blocker. Each modular-reduction stage holds one control pair fixed (modulo x toggles) while the target sweeps the register, so the 17 ccz should cover roughly 4-6 legal spans. Spans costing 4 T each: ~5 spans over ~13 ccz = 20 T, plus ~4 leftover singletons at 4 T = 16 T, i.e. 68 -> about 36-44 T, using 1-2 extra clean ancillas (T-count is the first tie-break, so the qubit growth is accepted). Well under pyzx's 73 and BQSKit's 119.

card.name: complementary_control_toffoli_pair_collapse
card.identity: Non-local collapse of a PAIR of Toffoli-level gates on the SAME qubit triple separated only by X gates on those wires. Step 0 (normalization, exact): wherever the op list contains h(w), ccz(u,v,w), h(w) with no other op on wire w between them, fuse to ccx(u,v,w); unmatched ccz stay ccz. Step 1: find two normalized Toffolis g_p, g_q (p<q) of the same type and on the same unordered triple {a,b,c} (for ccx also the same target c) such that EVERY op strictly between p and q either touches none of a,b,c, or is an `x` on one of a,b,c. Let alpha, beta, gamma be the parities of the numbers of x(a), x(b), x(c) gates strictly between. Step 2 (rewrite): delete BOTH Toffolis, leave every other op (including all those x gates) byte-for-byte where it is, and insert at position q the Clifford residue below, written in the wire VALUES at position q (A,B,C). CCZ case: the composite phase is (-1)^f with f = (A^alpha)(B^beta)(C^gamma) XOR A*B*C; the cubic terms cancel identically, so f expands over GF(2) into monomials of degree <= 2: emit z(q_i) for each surviving linear monomial, cz(q_i,q_j) for each surviving quadratic monomial, and ignore the constant (global phase). Explicitly: (alpha,beta,gamma)=(0,0,0) -> nothing (the two CCZ annihilate); (1,0,0) -> cz(b,c); (0,1,0) -> cz(a,c); (0,0,1) -> cz(a,b); (1,1,0) -> cz(a,c) cz(b,c) z(c); (1,0,1) -> cz(a,b) cz(b,c) z(b); (0,1,1) -> cz(a,b) cz(a,c) z(a); (1,1,1) -> cz(a,b) cz(a,c) cz(b,c) z(a) z(b) z(c). CCX case (target c): the composite flips c by (A^alpha)(B^beta) XOR A*B = alpha*B XOR beta*A XOR alpha*beta, so emit cx(b,c) if alpha, cx(a,c) if beta, x(c) if alpha AND beta (gamma is irrelevant: X on the target commutes with CCX); (alpha,beta)=(0,0) -> nothing. Cost: 8 T -> 0 T per matched pair, no ancilla, no measurement, nothing reordered. If the pair survives but its Toffolis were produced by the h-ccz-h fusion, re-emit the untouched h's only where the Toffoli was NOT deleted.
card.correctness: CCZ = diag(1,...,1,-1) applies phase (-1)^{abc}; CCX flips c by a*b. X gates are the only ops between the two gates that touch a, b or c, so the values seen by g_p are exactly (A^alpha, B^beta, C^gamma) where A,B,C are the values at position q, and no op between reads or writes a, b, c otherwise (ops on disjoint wires commute with both Toffolis as tensor factors, so deleting the pair and inserting the residue at q is an identity on the full operator, not a reordering of anything else). Hence the composite of the two deleted CCZ is the diagonal operator (-1)^{(A^alpha)(B^beta)(C^gamma) + ABC}. Expanding over GF(2): (A^alpha)(B^beta)(C^gamma) = ABC + gamma*AB + beta*AC + alpha*BC + beta*gamma*A + alpha*gamma*B + alpha*beta*C + alpha*beta*gamma, so the ABC term cancels and the exponent is a degree-<=2 polynomial, i.e. a product of CZ and Z gates (plus a global phase) - Clifford, 0 T. The listed eight cases are this expansion. For CCX, X on the target commutes with CCX (CCX X_c = X_c CCX) so gamma only moves the x gates past, and the composite flip of c is (A^alpha)(B^beta) + AB = alpha*B + beta*A + alpha*beta, realized by cx(b,c), cx(a,c), x(c). Both rewrites are exact up to global phase, use no ancilla and no measurement, so the exact D[omega] check on the changed window decides them. Step 0 is the defining identity CCX(u,v,w) = H_w CCZ(u,v,w) H_w, applied only when the two h's are adjacent on wire w.
card.trigger: Toffoli-level IRCircuit only (return [] otherwise; this never applies to Clifford+Rz angle circuits). (a) Normalize: scan for h(w) ... ccz(u,v,w) ... h(w) where the two h are the ops immediately preceding/following that ccz ON WIRE w (arbitrary ops on other wires may sit in between in the flat list) and record the fused ccx(u,v,w). (b) Index the normalized Toffolis by their qubit triple (unordered for ccz; (controls, target) for ccx). (c) For every pair p<q with the same key, scan the ops strictly between: ACCEPT the pair iff every such op has an empty intersection with {a,b,c} OR is exactly `x` on a, b or c; REJECT it the moment any other op touches a, b or c (h, s/sdg/t/tdg, z/cz on them, cx/ccx/ccz with any of a,b,c among its qubits, measurement, classically controlled op). card.name: complementary_control_toffoli_pair_collapse
card.identity: Non-local collapse of a PAIR of Toffoli-level gates on the SAME qubit triple separated only by X gates on those wires. Step 0 (normalization, exact): wherever the op list contains h(w), ccz(u,v,w), h(w) with no other op on wire w between them, fuse to ccx(u,v,w); unmatched ccz stay ccz. Step 1: find two normalized Toffolis g_p, g_q (p<q) of the same type and on the same unordered triple {a,b,c} (for ccx also the same target c) such that EVERY op strictly between p and q either touches none of a,b,c, or is an `x` on one of a,b,c. Let alpha, beta, gamma be the parities of the numbers of x(a), x(b), x(c) gates strictly between. Step 2 (rewrite): delete BOTH Toffolis, leave every other op (including all those x gates) byte-for-byte where it is, and insert at position q the Clifford residue below, written in the wire VALUES at position q (A,B,C). CCZ case: the composite phase is (-1)^f with f = (A^alpha)(B^beta)(C^gamma) XOR A*B*C; the cubic terms cancel identically, so f expands over GF(2) into monomials of degree <= 2: emit z(q_i) for each surviving linear monomial, cz(q_i,q_j) for each surviving quadratic monomial, and ignore the constant (global phase). Explicitly: (alpha,beta,gamma)=(0,0,0) -> nothing (the two CCZ annihilate); (1,0,0) -> cz(b,c); (0,1,0) -> cz(a,c); (0,0,1) -> cz(a,b); (1,1,0) -> cz(a,c) cz(b,c) z(c); (1,0,1) -> cz(a,b) cz(b,c) z(b); (0,1,1) -> cz(a,b) cz(a,c) z(a); (1,1,1) -> cz(a,b) cz(a,c) cz(b,c) z(a) z(b) z(c). card.name: joint_budget_direct_rotation_synthesis
card.identity: Do the Clifford+T approximation of the surviving Rz rotations INSIDE the rule, with one shared, measured error budget, instead of leaving them to the harness's per-rotation budget eps_rz = eps_synth / N_Rz. Procedure: (1) run the existing exact merging first, so the op list carries only the N_Rz unavoidable non-pi/4 rotations (on qft_8: N_Rz = 31, one per non-grid Walsh character of the diagonal content of each Hadamard-free segment). (2) Implement a self-contained Ross-Selinger z-rotation grid synthesiser (stdlib + sympy only: solve the 1-D grid problem for the scaled ellipse, test each candidate u in Z[omega] for the Diophantine condition xi = 2^k - u u^dag = t t^dag by factoring N(xi) with sympy.factorint and taking modular square roots, then extract the Matsumoto-Amano / Kliuchnikov-Maslov-Mosca exact-synthesis word over h,s,t,x,z). It returns, for a target angle theta and accuracy delta, an explicit Clifford+T word W with ||W - rz(theta)|| <= delta and T-count approximately 3*log2(1/delta) + c. (3) Replace every rz(theta_i) by such a word, all at ONE common accuracy delta, and set delta by binary search on the MEASURED whole-circuit phase-aligned operator distance D(delta) (8 qubits: build the 256x256 unitary of candidate and original with numpy and compute the phase-aligned spectral distance exactly, the same quantity the judge computes), taking the largest delta with D(delta) <= 0.9 * 5e-4. (4) Optional refinement: for each rotation keep the 2-4 cheapest words within 2*delta, and run a greedy pass that swaps in the candidate word minimising the current measured D, exploiting cancellation between residuals instead of their worst-case sum. Emit no ancilla, no measurement; the rewritten region's ORIGINAL side still contains rz, so the judge takes the numerical-distance (approx) path, not the exact D[omega] path.
card.correctness: Each replacement is an explicit unitary W_i with a certified bound ||W_i - rz(theta_i)|| <= delta (Ross-Selinger: the returned u,t in Z[omega] satisfy |u|^2 + |t|^2 = 2^k exactly, so W_i is an exact Clifford+T unitary, and the grid condition gives the stated distance; the exact-synthesis step is lossless). The composite circuit error therefore obeys ||U_new - U_old|| <= sum_i delta_i, which is the bound the harness's ledger uses; but the bound is not what is charged. The judge charges the MEASURED phase-aligned operator distance, and that is strictly and typically much smaller than the sum: the N_Rz residuals act about N_Rz distinct Pauli axes (distinct Walsh characters of the segments' diagonal content, plus small off-axis parts), so to first order the total error operator is sum_i delta_i * E_i with orthogonal (trace-orthogonal) E_i, whose spectral norm grows like sqrt(N_Rz) * delta (Khintchine / orthogonality of distinct characters), not N_Rz * delta. Uniform allocation is optimal for a SUM constraint (minimise sum of 3*log2(1/delta_i) subject to sum delta_i = E is achieved at equal delta_i), which is exactly why no reallocation of the harness's budget can help; the gain here comes only from replacing the sum constraint by the measured norm. Because step (3) binary-searches on the measured distance itself, and step (4) only ever accepts a swap that lowers it, the candidate handed to the judge is already known to satisfy distance <= 0.9 * 5e-4, inside the approx half of the ledger (eps/2 = 5e-4); the whole rewrite is one approx charge and the circuit then contains no rz at all, so the synthesis half of the ledger is not drawn on. No ancillas and no measurement are introduced, so the spec/relaxed path (which demands a literally Clifford+T candidate and is what killed attempt 1 on this circuit) is never entered.
card.trigger: A Clifford+Rz op list with N_Rz >= 8 non-pi/4 rotations after exact merging, n <= 12 qubits (so the 2^n x 2^n unitary can be formed for the internal measured-distance check), and an approx budget eps_approx > 0 that is not already spent. Fire once, globally, as the last pass: it consumes the whole approx half of the ledger and removes every rz from the op list. Do not fire if any rz angle is already a multiple of pi/4 (those are exact and must be emitted as Clifford/T, not synthesised), and do not fire on a region whose original side is already purely Clifford+T (that side would be checked exactly, and an approximation can never pass).
card.expected_effect: qft_8 is at the ancilla-free Walsh-character floor: the input's 48 rotations (21 parity characters x_i^x_j at distance >= 2, plus the per-wire merged linear characters) reduce to N_Rz = 31 non-grid rotations, and both the book (1583 T) and pyzx (1577 T) sit there, so no further exact merging or ancilla-free rewrite can remove a rotation, and the approx budget 5e-4 is far too small to drop even the smallest rotation (angle pi/256, phase-aligned distance 0.0061). The only remaining lever is the synthesis constant. Harness today: delta = 5e-4/31 = 1.6e-5 per rotation, ~50.6 T each, 31*50.6 + 15 = 1583 T. With one shared measured budget, the 31 orthogonal residuals let delta rise to roughly 1e-4 (measured distance ~ 3.5*sqrt(31)/2 * delta, binary-searched, so the factor is confirmed not assumed), giving 3*log2(1/1e-4) + c ~ 43 T per rotation: 31*43 + 15 ~ 1348 T. Expected 1583 -> ~1350-1400, i.e. 180-230 T, and the same pass applies unchanged to qpe_8, qae_13, hhl_8 and tfim_6, where N_Rz is in the hundreds to thousands and the sqrt(N) gap is correspondingly larger (at N_Rz = 600 the relaxation factor is ~25, about 13 T per rotation). The risk is implementation size, not idea: if the grid synthesiser is too slow for 31 angles at delta ~ 1e-4, the pass can be restricted to the rotations whose residual axes are most nearly orthogonal and the rest left to the harness, in which case the gain degrades smoothly rather than vanishing.

Selinger, 'Optimal ancilla-free Clifford+T approximation of z-rotations', QIC 16 (2016), arXiv:1403.2975 (T-count 3*log2(1/eps), grid problem + Diophantine condition); P. Selinger, 'Efficient Clifford+T approximation of single-qubit operators', arXiv:1212.6253; V. Kliuchnikov, D. Maslov, M. Mosca, 'Fast and efficient exact synthesis of single-qubit unitaries generated by Clifford and T gates', QIC 13 (2013), arXiv:1206.5236 (exact synthesis / Matsumoto-Amano normal form); for the sum-versus-norm gap in aggregated rotation-synthesis error: M. Amy, D. Maslov, M. Mosca (2014) phase-polynomial normal form for the character decomposition, and the Khintchine/orthogonality bound on sums of independent small Pauli errors as used in error-budget accounting by Campbell and Hastings, 'Efficient quantum compilation for hybrid/Trotter error budgeting' (randomised-compiling error allocation, arXiv:1811.08017).

(4) Optional refinement: for each rotation keep the 2-4 cheapest words within 2*delta, and run a greedy pass that swaps in the candidate word minimising the current measured D, exploiting cancellation between residuals instead of their worst-case sum. Emit no ancilla, no measurement; the rewritten region's ORIGINAL side still contains rz, so the judge takes the numerical-distance (approx) path, not the exact D[omega] path.

The composite circuit error therefore obeys ||U_new - U_old|| <= sum_i delta_i, which is the bound the harness's ledger uses; but the bound is not what is charged. The judge charges the MEASURED phase-aligned operator distance, and that is strictly and typically much smaller than the sum: the N_Rz residuals act about N_Rz distinct Pauli axes (distinct Walsh characters of the segments' diagonal content, plus small off-axis parts), so to first order the total error operator is sum_i delta_i * E_i with orthogonal (trace-orthogonal) E_i, whose spectral norm grows like sqrt(N_Rz) * delta (Khintchine / orthogonality of distinct characters), not N_Rz * delta. Uniform allocation is optimal for a SUM constraint (minimise sum of 3*log2(1/delta_i) subject to sum delta_i = E is achieved at equal delta_i), which is exactly why no reallocation of the harness's budget can help; the gain here comes only from replacing the sum constraint by the measured norm. Because step (3) binary-searches on the measured distance itself, and step (4) only ever accepts a swap that lowers it, the candidate handed to the judge is already known to satisfy distance <= 0.9 * 5e-4, inside the approx half of the ledger (eps/2 = 5e-4); the whole rewrite is one approx charge and the circuit then contains no rz at all, so the synthesis half of the ledger is not drawn on. No ancillas and no measurement are introduced, so the spec/relaxed path (which demands a literally Clifford+T candidate and is what killed attempt 1 on this circuit) is never entered.
card.trigger: A Clifford+Rz op list with N_Rz >= 8 non-pi/4 rotations after exact merging, n <= 12 qubits (so the 2^n x 2^n unitary can be formed for the internal measured-distance check), and an approx budget eps_approx > 0 that is not already spent. Fire once, globally, as the last pass: it consumes the whole approx half of the ledger and removes every rz from the op list. Do not fire if any rz angle is already a multiple of pi/4 (those are exact and must be emitted as Clifford/T, not synthesised), and do not fire on a region whose original side is already purely Clifford+T (that side would be checked exactly, and an approximation can never pass).

The only remaining lever is the synthesis constant. Harness today: delta = 5e-4/31 = 1.6e-5 per rotation, ~50.6 T each, 31*50.6 + 15 = 1583 T. card.name: phase_gradient_addition_for_dyadic_rotation_cascades
card.identity: Work inside a maximal Hadamard-free segment of {cx, x, z, s, sdg, t, tdg, cz, rz}, where every diagonal rotation rz(a) sitting on a wire with GF(2) affine parity label p contributes, up to global phase, the phase e^{i a p} (same parity-label formalism as pauli_frame_rotation_merge). Suppose a set G of k rotations in one segment has parity labels p_1..p_k (distinct, since equal labels are already fused by the book rule) and DYADIC angles a_i = 2*pi*s_i/2^{e_i} with s_i in {+1,-1} and pairwise DISTINCT exponents e_i (3 <= e_i <= B). Their joint action is |x> -> exp(2*pi*i * sum_i s_i p_i(x) / 2^{e_i}) |x> = exp(2*pi*i * v(x) / 2^B) |x>, where v(x) = sum_i s_i * 2^{B-e_i} * p_i(x) is a signed integer read off a B-bit two's-complement register. Replace G by: (1) ONCE per circuit, prepare a B-qubit phase-gradient catalyst register from |0>^B as |phi_B> = H^{\otimes B} followed by rz(2*pi/2^j) on the j-th gradient qubit (j = 1..B), i.e. |phi_B> = 2^{-B/2} sum_{m=0}^{2^B-1} e^{2*pi*i*m/2^B} |m>; only the j >= 3 rotations are non-Clifford (B-2 of them). (2) Per group: allocate a clean B-qubit work register |0>^B and write v into it with CNOTs only - for each i, CNOT every wire in the support of p_i into work bit (B - e_i), and for s_i = -1 use the complement/two's-complement bookkeeping (X gates plus a constant offset folded into one extra Clifford/T phase); affine constants in p_i are X gates. All of this is Clifford, 0 T. (3) Apply an in-place B-bit ripple-carry ADDITION of the work register into the gradient register using Gidney's measurement-uncomputed AND adder: B-1 AND gadgets at 4 T each, 4(B-1) T total, no rotations. (4) Uncompute the work register by running step (2) backwards (CNOTs, 0 T), freeing it for the next group. (5) At the end of the circuit, uncompute the gradient catalyst by the inverse of step (1) (B-2 non-Clifford rotations) so it returns to |0>^B. Every original rotation in G is deleted; the gradient register is prepared and unprepared exactly once and shared by all groups. Groups are formed by a greedy partition of the segment's dyadic rotations into maximal distinct-exponent sets (on a QPE/QAE controlled-phase cascade this is the natural per-cascade grouping).
card.correctness: Adding a value v into a phase-gradient register is exactly a phase kickback: ADD_v |phi_B> = 2^{-B/2} sum_m e^{2*pi*i*m/2^B} |m + v mod 2^B> = 2^{-B/2} sum_{m'} e^{2*pi*i*(m'-v)/2^B} |m'> = e^{-2*pi*i*v/2^B} |phi_B>, so the gradient state is an exact eigenvector of modular addition with eigenvalue e^{-2*pi*i*v/2^B}; it is returned unchanged (a true catalyst) and the controlled-on-|x> value v(x) produces exactly the phase e^{-2*pi*i*v(x)/2^B} on |x> (use subtraction, or negate the loaded sign bits, to get the + sign). Because the arithmetic is mod 2^B and the phase e^{2*pi*i*m/2^B} is also periodic mod 2^B, wraparound is harmless - this is why the identity is exact, not approximate. The target phase is exactly the product of the k original gadget phases: sum_i a_i p_i = 2*pi * sum_i s_i p_i / 2^{e_i} = 2*pi * v / 2^B by construction, with each rotation's rz(a) = diag(1, e^{ia}) convention differing from exp(-i a Z/2) by a global phase only. The parity labels are realized exactly by CNOTs (GF(2) linear forms) and X gates (affine constants); all rotations in the segment are diagonal and hence commute, so deleting them as a set and reinstating one joint diagonal operator at the position of the last one is an exact unitary identity. Gidney's AND gadget computes a AND b into a clean |0> with 4 T exactly, and uncomputes it with an X-basis measurement plus a classically controlled CZ: deterministic in effect, so each measurement branch applies the SAME operator with the same scalar (phase consistency) and every ancilla - work register, adder carries, gradient register - starts and ends in |0>. The only inexactness anywhere is the gridsynth synthesis of the B-2 gradient-prep rotations and their inverses, which is the ordinary per-rz synthesis error already accounted for by the metric at eps_rz, not a rewrite error.
card.trigger: (1) Split the op list into maximal Hadamard-free segments (cut at every h and at any non-diagonal op). (2) Inside a segment, propagate affine parity labels through cx (target ^= control) and x (flip constant), and collect every t/tdg/rz with angle normalized to (-pi, pi] mod 2*pi; the histogram entries 6.283952, 12.173672, 12.370021, 12.468196, ... must be reduced first (they are 2*pi + pi/4096, -pi/8, -pi/16, -pi/32, ...). (3) Keep a rotation if |a| is within 1e-9 of 2*pi/2^e for some integer e in [3, 14] (dyadic test by e = log2(2*pi/|a|), round, check); record (sign, e, parity label, position). (4) Greedily partition the kept rotations of a segment into groups with pairwise distinct e; emit a match for every group with k >= 4, largest first, with B = max e over the group (capped at 14). (5) Skip any group whose rotations are not all in the same Hadamard-free segment. On qae_13 the kept set is exactly the QAE/QPE controlled-phase cascade: +-pi/8 (10 each), +-pi/16 (9), +-pi/32 (8), +-pi/64 (7), +-pi/128 (6), +-pi/256 (5), +-pi/512 (4), +-pi/1024 (3), +-pi/2048 (2), +-pi/4096 (1), i.e. roughly 10 nested cascades of 8-11 distinct exponents each, so about 9-10 matches with B ~ 12.
card.expected_effect: Each surviving non-Clifford rotation costs about 3*log2(1/eps_rz) ~ 50 T at eps_rz = eps/N_Rz, and the book merge leaves roughly 90 of them (4526 T). The dyadic cascade structure means essentially all of them are capturable: about 9 groups of 8-10 rotations each, say 70-80 rotations deleted (~3500-4000 T). Added cost: one 12-bit Gidney addition per group, 4*(B-1) = 44 T, 9 groups = ~400 T; the shared gradient catalyst costs B-2 = 10 non-Clifford rotations to prepare plus 10 to unprepare, ~20 rotations = ~1000 T (and those 20 are the ONLY rotations left, so N_Rz collapses from ~90 to ~20 and eps_rz rises from 6.9e-6 to ~3e-5, cutting each of them to ~43 T, ~860 T). Rotation-free CNOT overhead: a few hundred CNOTs for parity loading/unloading. Space: a 12-bit work register, a 12-bit gradient register and 11 adder ancillas, reused across groups, so 13 -> ~48 qubits; T-count is lexicographically first so this trade is the intended one. Net on qae_13: 4526 -> ~1900-2600. Note this is also the mechanism that makes qft_8 / qpe_8 / hhl_8 cascades cheap, so the rule is not qae-specific.
card.source: C. Gidney, 'Halving the cost of quantum addition', Quantum 2, 74 (2018) (4-T measured-uncompute AND, ripple-carry adder); C. Gidney & A. Fowler, 'Flexible layout of surface code computations using AutoCCZ states' (2019) and Gidney's 'phase gradient' construction: addition into |phi> = sum_m e^{2 pi i m / 2^B}|m> applies an exact dyadic phase and leaves the state invariant (catalytic); R. Babbush, C. Gidney, D. Berry, N. Wiebe, J. McClean, A. Paler, A. Fowler, H. Neven, 'Encoding electronic spectra in quantum circuits with linear T complexity', PRX 8, 041015 (2018), Appendix on phase-gradient rotations; Y. Nam, N. Ross, Y. Su, A. Childs, D. Maslov, npj QI 4, 23 (2018) for the parity-label/phase-polynomial frame this plugs into.

d at the end.
- I did not run the adder or the AND gadget through any simulator, because `test_rule` was the only command allowed. They are derived by hand.

**What `test_rule` showed:**
- The rule fires on qae_13 with 1 match and 2 application attempts.
- Verification fails on the first one: `candidate not exact: rz(-0.00076699…) is not a multiple of pi/4`.
- The judge's relaxed mode requires a Clifford+T candidate. The construction needs the gradient-state rotations rz(±2π/2^j) for j ≥ 4. Those are continuous rotations by definition, so they can't be removed.
- The same `test_rule` failure ended the earlier rejected attempt `phase_gradient_catalysis_dyadic_rotations` on qft_8.
- Approx mode can't cover it either. It needs the candidate and reference to have the same qubit count and at most 20 qubits. The catalyst adds about 35 qubits (13 → 48).

**Other limits I found:**
- The angle circuit has no measurement, so the AND uncompute is unitary and costs 4 T instead of 0. The adder is therefore 8(B−1) T, not 4(B−1).
- The T-count is untested. The candidate never passed the judge, so the runner never priced it.

LIMITATION: no saving was measured. Whatever the saving would be, the judge's exact-candidate and qubit-count limits would block it.

IDEA_FAILS: the construction needs non-Clifford+T gradient-prep rotations and ~35 extra qubits, and the frozen judge only accepts exact Clifford+T candidates (relaxed) or equal qubit counts of 20 or fewer (approx), so it can never verify.
