card.name: shared_and_by_control_product_anf
card.identity: Match Toffoli-level gates by the ANF of the PRODUCT of their two control forms, not by the pair of control forms, and apply the sharing ONE PAIR AT A TIME. (1) Fold every h(t) ccz(c1,c2,t) h(t) trigram to ccx(c1,c2;t) so the op list is x/cx/ccx/ccz only; symbolically simulate over GF(2) so every wire w carries an ANF P_t(w) (declared-clean ancillas pinned to 0). (2) For each ccz/ccx gate g at position p with controls (c1,c2), form the single Boolean polynomial Q(g) = P_p(c1) * P_p(c2) (expanded in ANF, using u*u = u). (3) Trigger on a PAIR of gates g_i at p and g_j at q>p with Q(g_i) = Q(g_j) as ANFs (the pair of control forms need NOT be equal), with target wires not among either gate's control wires, and with no other ccz/ccx between them that the rule has already rewritten. (4) Rewrite exactly that pair: at p, and_compute(c1,c2 -> a) on one fresh clean ancilla a [4 T, |x,y,0> -> |x,y,x&y>], then cx(a, target_i) (cz for ccz, with the target's h's kept); a is left alive and untouched through [p,q]; at q, cx(a, target_j) / cz(a, target_j) in place of g_j; immediately after q, and_uncompute(a) = H(a), X-basis measurement, classically controlled cz(d1,d2) on g_j's OWN control wires d1,d2 [0 T]. Each application removes two 4-T AND gadgets and installs one, adds one ancilla and exactly ONE measurement. The pass re-runs; disjoint or nested pairs are handled by successive applications.
card.correctness: ANF is a unique normal form, so Q(g) is exactly the Boolean function 'the AND of this gate's two controls' on every input, and Q(g_i) = Q(g_j) means the two gates need the SAME bit, even when their control wires were rewritten in between. This is strictly weaker than control-pair equality and is the only thing the shared AND needs: in a Cuccaro MAJ/UMA mirror pair the UMA Toffoli sees (u, v ^ u ^ 1) where the MAJ Toffoli saw (u, v), and u*(v ^ u ^ 1) = uv ^ u ^ u = uv over GF(2) (u*u = u), so the products agree although the pairs do not. Gidney's compute-AND gadget realizes |x,y>|0> -> |x,y>|x&y> exactly with 4 T and no residual relative phase, and while a holds u&v, cx(a,z) acts as ccx(u,v;z) and cz(a,z) as ccz(u,v,z) on every basis state, reproducing both members exactly (the target wire is excluded from the control set, so no self-interference). The measurement-based uncompute returns a to |0>; the induced phase is (-1)^{m*(stored bit)} and the fix-up cz(d1,d2) applies (-1)^{m*(d1&d2)} with d1&d2 = Q(g_j) = stored bit at that very position, so it cancels on every branch: K_m|x> = c_m|F(x)> with the same c_m for all x and sum_m |c_m|^2 = 1 (phase consistency). Ancillas are clean in and out, so the relaxed specification check applies unchanged; equality is up to global phase only.

Matches are emitted as INDIVIDUAL pairs, innermost/latest first, each a separate application; the rule never rebuilds the whole circuit. Fires only when the pair's current cost (two AND gadgets, 8 T) strictly exceeds the replacement (one gadget, 4 T).

Between each mirror pair the second control is hit by exactly one x and one cx from the first control (e.g. x q9 then cx q8,q9 for the (q8,q9) pair), so the control pairs differ -- which is why ANF PAIR matching found only 10 classes -- while the control PRODUCTS are identical for all five pairs (u*(v^u^1) = uv); the (q0,q1) pair is untouched in between and matches trivially. card.name: and_value_memoization_over_classical_segments
card.identity: Step 0 (exact normalization): wherever the op list contains h(w) ... ccz(u,v,w) ... h(w) with no other op on wire w in between, fuse to ccx(u,v,w) (CCX = H_w CCZ H_w). Step 1: cut the op list into maximal segments containing no h (ops drawn from x, z, cx, cz, ccx, ccz). Inside one segment every op is a classical permutation or a diagonal phase that depends only on computational-basis wire VALUES, so track values symbolically: at the segment start give wire q the fresh GF(2) variable v_q, and propagate the algebraic normal form (ANF, a set of monomials over v_1..v_n) through the segment: x(q): V[q] ^= 1; cx(a,b): V[b] ^= V[a]; ccx(a,b,c): V[c] ^= V[a]*V[b]; z/cz/ccz: values unchanged (diagonal). Step 2 (the rewrite): at each ccx(a,b,c) / ccz(a,b,c) in the segment, form the ANF product P = V[a]*V[b] and try, in this order, to express P as a GF(2) linear combination of the CURRENT wire values: (i) P == 0 -> delete the gate; (ii) P == 1 -> emit x(c) (for ccz: z(c)); (iii) P == V[w] for some live wire w != c -> emit cx(w,c) (for ccz: cz(w,c)); (iv) general case: run Gaussian elimination over the monomial space on the n+1 vectors {V[w] : all wires w != c} u {1} and, if P is in their span, emit the corresponding chain of cx(w_i,c) gates (plus x(c) if the constant 1 is used) - for ccz emit cz(w_i,c) and z(c) instead. In every case the Toffoli is replaced by Clifford gates only: 4 T (book AND lowering) or 7 T (naive) -> 0 T. Toffolis whose P is not in the span are left untouched and keep their book lowering. Nothing is moved or reordered: each gate is rewritten in place, and the value table is updated with the gate's true effect (V[c] ^= P) so later gates in the segment see correct values. The match is the whole segment, so the window the judge verifies is the full segment, in which the equality holds exactly.
card.correctness: Inside an h-free segment every op is either a basis permutation (x, cx, ccx) or diagonal (z, cz, ccz), so the segment operator acts as |x> -> e^{i*phi(x)}|pi(x)> and both pi and phi are determined by the Boolean values the gates read. The ANF table V is exactly those values: it is initialized with independent variables (making no assumption about the state entering the segment) and updated by the defining action of each gate, so V[q] is the value of wire q at that point as a Boolean function of the segment's input, for every input. CCX(a,b,c) flips c by the product V[a]*V[b] = P and CCZ(a,b,c) applies (-1)^{V[a]*V[b]*V[c]} = (-1)^{P*V[c]}. If P equals a GF(2) linear combination L = (XOR_i V[w_i]) XOR eps of other wires' current values AS ANF IDENTITIES (equality of monomial sets, i.e. equality on all inputs, not just reachable ones), then the chain cx(w_1,c)...cx(w_k,c) [x(c) if eps=1] flips c by exactly L = P, and cz(w_1,c)...cz(w_k,c) [z(c) if eps=1] applies (-1)^{L*V[c]} = (-1)^{P*V[c]}; the w_i are only READ by these gates, so none of their values changes and the substituted gates may sit at the original position with no commutation obligation. Hence the replacement realizes the same permutation and the same phase on every basis state: equal unitaries up to no phase at all. Cases (i)-(iii) are the specializations P=0, P=1, P=V[w]. Step 0 is the exact identity CCX = H CCZ H. Since the result is Clifford+T on both sides, the judge's exact D[omega] check on the segment decides it; no ancilla, no measurement, no qubit growth, no error budget.
card.trigger: Toffoli-level IRCircuit only (return [] for Clifford+Rz angle circuits). (a) Fuse h-ccz-h pairs as in step 0 (only when the two h are the ops immediately before/after that ccz ON WIRE w; ops on other wires may interleave). (b) Split at every remaining h into maximal h-free segments; a segment is a candidate iff it contains >= 1 ccx/ccz. Treat measure and classically controlled gates as segment breaks too. (c) Build the ANF table for the segment (monomials as frozensets of wire indices; cap the table at 4096 monomials per wire and abandon the segment if exceeded, so the pass is linear in segment length). (d) For each Toffoli in order, compute P = V[a]*V[b] and test membership of P in the span of {V[w], w != c} u {1} by Gaussian elimination in the monomial space (n+1 <= 12 vectors - cheap). (e) Emit ONE match per segment, and only if at least one Toffoli in it is reducible by (i)-(iv); the match payload is the segment range plus the per-gate substitutions. Matches are ordered by descending number of reducible Toffolis. Total work is O(#segments * length * n^2) with no search over spans and no pair enumeration, so the pass cannot time out.
card.expected_effect: modred_21 is 17 ccz + 30 h + 24 x + 3 cx on 11 qubits at 68 T (= 4 x 17: the book AND rule shared nothing here, every Toffoli is an isolated 4 T). Step 0 consumes the h's: 'h ccz h' x11 and the QASM note `gate ccz = h ccx h` say almost every ccz is an h-conjugated ccx, so after fusion the circuit is a pure classical reversible network of ccx + x + cx - one or two large h-free segments covering nearly all 17 Toffolis. Modular reduction by a constant is compare-then-conditionally-correct, and the 24 x gates are the control-on-zero / constant-modulus toggles: the same AND of register bits is formed in the comparison phase, used, and formed again in the correction/uncompute phase, with the x toggles merely complementing the operands. Value memoization catches that automatically: a recomputed product whose value is still carried by a live wire (possibly up to XOR with other live wires, case (iv)) becomes a free CNOT fan-in, and complemented-control products that collapse to a constant or to a single bit (P = a*(a^1) = 0, P = a*1 = a) vanish outright. Unlike the two earlier attempts this needs NO shared control pair, NO span legality test and NO gate motion - the exact structural reasons they failed (attempt 1 timed out on span search, attempt 2 never fired because no two Toffolis share a stable control pair in these circuits) - it only needs value equality, which the x toggles cannot break. I expect 4-7 of the 17 Toffolis to be reducible, i.e. 68 -> 40-52 T with 11 qubits unchanged, versus pyzx 73, TKET 107, BQSKit 119.

Hence the replacement realizes the same permutation and the same phase on every basis state: equal unitaries up to no phase at all. Cases (i)-(iii) are the specializations P=0, P=1, P=V[w]. Step 0 is the exact identity CCX = H CCZ H. Since the result is Clifford+T on both sides, the judge's exact D[omega] check on the segment decides it; no ancilla, no measurement, no qubit growth, no error budget.
card.trigger: Toffoli-level IRCircuit only (return [] for Clifford+Rz angle circuits). (a) Fuse h-ccz-h pairs as in step 0 (only when the two h are the ops immediately before/after that ccz ON WIRE w; ops on other wires may interleave). (b) Split at every remaining h into maximal h-free segments; a segment is a candidate iff it contains >= 1 ccx/ccz. Treat measure and classically controlled gates as segment breaks too. (c) Build the ANF table for the segment (monomials as frozensets of wire indices; cap the table at 4096 monomials per wire and abandon the segment if exceeded, so the pass is linear in segment length). (d) For each Toffoli in order, compute P = V[a]*V[b] and test membership of P in the span of {V[w], w != c} u {1} by Gaussian elimination in the monomial space (n+1 <= 12 vectors - cheap). (e) Emit ONE match per segment, and only if at least one Toffoli in it is reducible by (i)-(iv); the match payload is the segment range plus the per-gate substitutions. The rule never fires on `modred_21`, and it can't. I used two of the five `test_rule` runs. I wrote the rule as specified (ANF value table, cases (i)–(iv), Gaussian elimination over the monomial space), and the first run matched 0 times on all four circuits.

For the second run I temporarily made `trigger` raise an error that dumped the target's gate list and segments, then removed that code. The dump shows two things:

- **Segments:** After the h-ccz-h fusion the circuit splits into five h-free segments, because the 30 h gates cannot all be fused.
- **Repeated products:** Several Toffoli products do recur, for example `ccz(1,3,4)`, `ccz(4,5,6)`, `ccz(2,3,4)`, `ccz(0,1,2)` and `ccz(10,9,8)` each appear twice. The second Toffoli of each pair is the uncompute of the first.
- **Why value reuse fails:** The product a·b is held only in its own target wire, because the Toffoli XORs it into that wire. The rule's span test excludes the target wire c. So no other live wire carries the product, and the span test never succeeds. Removing these Toffolis needs a compute/uncompute cancellation, which means moving gates and is outside this card.

IDEA_FAILS: In `modred_21` every Toffoli product is carried only by its own target wire (repeats are compute/uncompute pairs), so no product lies in the span of the other wires' values and the rule cannot lower the T-count.

card.name: staircase_knapsack_exact_angle_assignment
card.identity: Replace every surviving non-pi/4 rz by an EXACT Clifford+T word taken from one precomputed table, with the per-rotation accuracy chosen by a knapsack against the MEASURED whole-circuit distance instead of the harness's uniform eps_rz = eps_synth/N_Rz. (1) Build the table ONCE per rule-process, independent of the circuit: enumerate Matsumoto-Amano normal forms W = (T|eps)(HT|SHT)^* C over the generators h,s,t (Kliuchnikov-Maslov-Mosca / Giles-Selinger exact synthesis), keep only those whose 2x2 matrix is within 0.3 of SOME z-rotation, and record for each the triple (theta(W) = the z-rotation angle it best approximates = arg of its diagonal ratio, offaxis(W) = ||W - rz(theta(W))|| from its off-diagonal mass, tcount(W)). Enumerate by increasing T-count up to T_max ~ 60, but store only, for each T-count k, the sorted list of the achievable angles modulo the Clifford symmetry group (theta -> theta + j*pi/2, theta -> -theta), so the table is a few 10^5 floats, built in seconds and reused for every circuit. (2) For each rotation i with angle theta_i, binary-search the table to get its STAIRCASE cost curve: T_i(d) = min{ k : exists W with tcount(W) = k and ||W - rz(theta_i)|| <= d }, together with the witness word, for d on a dyadic ladder d in {2^-j}. This curve is a staircase with a rotation-dependent random offset: for some theta_i a word 6-12 T cheaper than 3*log2(1/d) happens to sit just inside d, for others not. (3) Allocate: let D(d_1..d_N) be the MEASURED phase-aligned operator distance (build the 2^n unitary of candidate and original with numpy, n <= 12) of the circuit with word i chosen at accuracy d_i. Start from the uniform harness point d_i = eps_approx/N, then run a budgeted greedy: repeatedly take the rotation whose next staircase step down in T-count costs the least increase in the current error estimate (first-order surrogate sum_i d_i^2 for ranking, since the N residuals act about distinct Walsh characters of the segments' diagonal content and therefore add in quadrature, not in sum), apply the step, and re-MEASURE D after every batch of steps; accept the batch only while D <= 0.9 * eps_approx (eps_approx = eps/2 = 5e-4), and bisect the last batch to the boundary (continue until the bisection interval is below 2 percent, so no allowance is left unspent). (4) Emit the chosen words in place of the rz; the op list then contains no rz at all. No ancilla, no measurement: the original side still contains rz, so the judge takes the numerical operator-distance (approx) path. Runtime: the table is built once and every per-rotation query is a binary search, so a circuit with thousands of rotations costs milliseconds of allocation plus the measured-distance evaluations, whose number is capped (<= 24 unitary builds; for n > 12 or N_Rz > 2000 skip the measured step and fall back to the quadrature surrogate with a 1/sqrt(N) safety factor, which is still admissible and still cheaper than uniform).
card.correctness: Each emitted word is an EXACT Clifford+T unitary (its matrix entries lie in Z[omega]/sqrt(2)^k by construction of the exact-synthesis normal form), and the table stores its certified distance to the rotation it replaces, so ||W_i - rz(theta_i)|| <= d_i holds by table construction, not by assumption. Subadditivity gives ||U_new - U_old|| <= sum_i d_i, so the allocation is always at least as safe as the harness's uniform split; but the quantity CHARGED is the measured phase-aligned operator distance, and the rule computes exactly that quantity (same phase-aligned spectral norm the judge uses) before emitting, accepting only configurations with D <= 0.9 * 5e-4. Hence admissibility does not depend on the quadrature heuristic at all: the heuristic only ranks candidate steps, while the measurement + bisection decides. The quadrature ranking is justified because, to first order, the residual of W_i is d_i * E_i with E_i a Pauli-type operator supported on the distinct Walsh character that rotation i rotates about (distinct characters are trace-orthogonal), so ||sum_i d_i E_i|| grows like sqrt(sum d_i^2) rather than sum d_i. The improvement over uniform allocation has two independent sources, and the second is the new one: (a) the constraint is a norm, not a sum, which lets every d_i rise by up to ~sqrt(N); (b) the per-rotation cost curve T_i(d) is a STAIRCASE with an angle-dependent offset, not the smooth 3*log2(1/d), so the optimum of min sum_i T_i(d_i) subject to sum_i d_i^2 <= E^2 is NOT at equal d_i (the standard Lagrange argument that forces uniform d applies only to the smooth curve): rotations whose next step is cheap in error should be stepped first, and rotations sitting just above a step boundary should be given extra allowance taken from rotations that would gain nothing from it. The greedy over the staircase with a measured feasibility test is the standard knapsack relaxation and is monotone: no step is kept unless the measured distance stays inside budget and the T-count strictly drops, which is also what the runner re-checks. Because the circuit ends with no rz, the synthesis half of the ledger is not drawn on and the whole rewrite is a single approx charge.
card.trigger: A Clifford+Rz op list, after the book's exact merging passes, containing N_Rz >= 8 rz whose angles are not multiples of pi/4, with an unspent approx budget eps_approx > 0. Fire once, globally, as the last pass. Per rotation, require that the table contain at least one word with tcount strictly below the harness's implied cost 3*log2(N_Rz/eps_approx) + 3 at the allocated accuracy, else leave that rz untouched (so the pass degrades smoothly, never upward). Do not touch any rz whose angle IS a multiple of pi/4 (those are exact Clifford/T already), do not fire on a region whose original side is purely Clifford+T (that side is checked exactly and no approximation can pass), and do not introduce ancillas or measurement (on this circuit family the relaxed path demands a literally exact candidate, which an approximation can never satisfy).
card.expected_effect: qft_8 is at its ancilla-free character floor: 31 non-grid rotations (21 two-qubit parity characters x_i^x_j at distance >= 2, plus the merged per-wire linear characters), and both the book (1583) and pyzx (1577) sit there, so the only remaining lever is the synthesis constant. Harness today: d = 5e-4/31 = 1.61e-5 per rotation, ~50.6 T each, 31*50.6 + 15 = 1583. The 31 residuals rotate about 31 distinct characters, so the measured distance scales like ~sqrt(31) = 5.6 times smaller than the sum, allowing d ~ 9e-5 at the bisected boundary: 3*log2(1/9e-5) + 3 ~ 43 T per rotation, i.e. 31*43 + 15 ~ 1354. On top of that the staircase table typically finds, for a third to a half of the angles, a word 3-6 T cheaper than the smooth-curve value at the same accuracy, and the greedy moves the freed allowance to the rotations that are stuck just above a step: another ~1.5-2 T per rotation, ~1310-1330. Expected 1583 -> ~1330-1390, i.e. 190-250 T removed, 8 qubits unchanged, no ancilla, no measurement. The two fixes relative to the earlier shared-budget attempt (which measured only 76 T and timed out on qpe_8) are structural: the allowance is now bisected to within 2 percent of the measured boundary instead of probing two points above the starting guess, so the sqrt(N) relaxation is actually spent; and all Diophantine/grid work is moved into one circuit-independent table so the per-circuit work is table lookups plus a bounded number of unitary builds, which is what keeps qpe_8 and qae_13 inside the runtime limit (with the surrogate fallback for hhl_8-scale N_Rz). The saving grows at smaller eps, since the relaxation factor is independent of eps while the per-rotation cost is logarithmic in it.
card.source: N. J. Ross and P. Selinger, 'Optimal ancilla-free Clifford+T approximation of z-rotations', QIC 16 (2016), arXiv:1403.2975; V. Kliuchnikov, D. Maslov, M. Mosca, 'Fast and efficient exact synthesis of single-qubit unitaries generated by Clifford and T gates', QIC 13 (2013), arXiv:1206.5236, and B. Giles, P. Selinger, 'Exact synthesis of multiqubit Clifford+T circuits', PRA 87 (2013) (Matsumoto-Amano normal form, the enumerable set of exactly representable z-rotation angles per T-count); M. Amy, D. Maslov, M. Mosca (2014) for the Walsh/phase-polynomial character decomposition that makes the residual axes orthogonal; E. Campbell, M. Hastings, arXiv:1811.08017, and Kivlichan et al., 'Improved fault-tolerant quantum simulation of condensed-phase correlated electrons' (2020), for norm-based (rather than additive) rotation-synthesis error budgeting and non-uniform allocation across many rotations.

Runtime: the table is built once and every per-rotation query is a binary search, so a circuit with thousands of rotations costs milliseconds of allocation plus the measured-distance evaluations, whose number is capped (<= 24 unitary builds; for n > 12 or N_Rz > 2000 skip the measured step and fall back to the quadrature surrogate with a 1/sqrt(N) safety factor, which is still admissible and still cheaper than uniform).
card.correctness: Each emitted word is an EXACT Clifford+T unitary (its matrix entries lie in Z[omega]/sqrt(2)^k by construction of the exact-synthesis normal form), and the table stores its certified distance to the rotation it replaces, so ||W_i - rz(theta_i)|| <= d_i holds by table construction, not by assumption. Subadditivity gives ||U_new - U_old|| <= sum_i d_i, so the allocation is always at least as safe as the harness's uniform split; but the quantity CHARGED is the measured phase-aligned operator distance, and the rule computes exactly that quantity (same phase-aligned spectral norm the judge uses) before emitting, accepting only configurations with D <= 0.9 * 5e-4. Hence admissibility does not depend on the quadrature heuristic at all: the heuristic only ranks candidate steps, while the measurement + bisection decides. The quadrature ranking is justified because, to first order, the residual of W_i is d_i * E_i with E_i a Pauli-type operator supported on the distinct Walsh character that rotation i rotates about (distinct characters are trace-orthogonal), so ||sum_i d_i E_i|| grows like sqrt(sum d_i^2) rather than sum d_i. The improvement over uniform allocation has two independent sources, and the second is the new one: (a) the constraint is a norm, not a sum, which lets every d_i rise by up to ~sqrt(N); (b) the per-rotation cost curve T_i(d) is a STAIRCASE with an angle-dependent offset, not the smooth 3*log2(1/d), so the optimum of min sum_i T_i(d_i) subject to sum_i d_i^2 <= E^2 is NOT at equal d_i (the standard Lagrange argument that forces uniform d applies only to the smooth curve): rotations whose next step is cheap in error should be stepped first, and rotations sitting just above a step boundary should be given extra allowance taken from rotations that would gain nothing from it. The greedy over the staircase with a measured feasibility test is the standard knapsack relaxation and is monotone: no step is kept unless the measured distance stays inside budget and the T-count strictly drops, which is also what the runner re-checks. Because the circuit ends with no rz, the synthesis half of the ledger is not drawn on and the whole rewrite is a single approx charge.
card.trigger: A Clifford+Rz op list, after the book's exact merging passes, containing N_Rz >= 8 rz whose angles are not multiples of pi/4, with an unspent approx budget eps_approx > 0. Fire once, globally, as the last pass. Per rotation, require that the table contain at least one word with tcount strictly below the harness's implied cost 3*log2(N_Rz/eps_approx) + 3 at the allocated accuracy, else leave that rz untouched (so the pass degrades smoothly, never upward). Do not touch any rz whose angle IS a multiple of pi/4 (those are exact Clifford/T already), do not fire on a region whose original side is purely Clifford+T (that side is checked exactly and no approximation can pass), and do not introduce ancillas or measurement (on this circuit family the relaxed path demands a literally exact candidate, which an approximation can never satisfy).

card.name: budgeted_pi_over_4_grid_snapping_of_residual_rotations
card.identity: A single-step, ancilla-free, measurement-free global pass that spends the otherwise unused approximation budget on the cheapest possible target: making a non-Clifford rotation exactly Clifford+T. (1) Normalize every t/tdg/rz angle a into (-pi, pi] modulo 2*pi (rz(a + 2*pi*k) = (-1)^k rz(a), a global phase, so the reduction is exact; this matters because this circuit's angle histogram is full of 2*pi + tiny and 4*pi - tiny entries, e.g. 6.283952 = 2*pi + pi/4096, 6.284719 = 2*pi + pi/2048, 12.564837 = 4*pi - pi/2048). (2) For each rotation let m = (pi/4) * round(4*a/pi) be the nearest multiple of pi/4 and delta = a - m. The single-gate rewrite is rz(a) -> rz(m), i.e. rz(a) = rz(m) * rz(delta) and the factor rz(delta) = diag(1, e^{i delta}) is DROPPED. If m == 0 the gate is deleted outright; otherwise rz(m) is emitted as the corresponding Clifford/T gate (z, s, sdg, t, tdg, or their products), which the metric charges at its exact T-count (0, 0, 0, 1, 1, ...) instead of ~3*log2(1/eps_rz) ~ 50 T. (3) Candidate selection is an explicit knapsack over the remaining approx budget E (= eps/2 = 5e-4 minus what earlier approx rules charged): each candidate i has exact phase-aligned cost d_i = 2*|sin(delta_i/4)| and gain g_i = (T cost of gridsynth(a_i) at eps_rz) - (exact T cost of m_i); emit candidates in increasing d_i (equivalently decreasing g_i/d_i, since all g_i are nearly equal) and have the runner accept them one at a time while the cumulative judge-measured distance stays <= 0.9*E. Each accepted snap also lowers N_Rz by one, which raises eps_rz = eps_synth/N_Rz for every surviving rotation and shaves a fraction of a T off each of them; and a snapped rotation that becomes Clifford unblocks the Clifford frame for the book rule pauli_frame_rotation_merge on the next pass. Nothing else in the op list is touched: no reordering, no ancilla, no measurement, no qubit-count change, no CNOT change.
card.correctness: The rewrite is a single-qubit local substitution rz(a) -> rz(m) with a = m + delta. On the changed window the two unitaries differ by exactly the right factor rz(delta) = diag(1, e^{i delta}) on one wire, tensored with the identity. Up to global phase, min_phi || e^{-i phi} diag(1, e^{i delta}) - I || is attained at phi = delta/2 and equals |e^{-i delta/2} - 1| = 2|sin(delta/4)|, so the phase-aligned operator distance contributed by one snap is EXACTLY 2|sin(delta_i/4)|, independent of where the gate sits and of the rest of the circuit (unitary invariance of the operator norm: || A (X - Y) B || = || X - Y || for unitaries A, B). For a set S of accepted snaps the triangle inequality gives distance <= sum_{i in S} 2|sin(delta_i/4)|, so the ledger bound is explicit and conservative; acceptance never relies on the bound, since the judge re-measures the phase-aligned distance of each application and charges that. Angle reduction mod 2*pi is exact up to global phase: diag(1, e^{i(a + 2*pi k)}) = diag(1, e^{i a}). Emitting rz(m) with m a multiple of pi/4 as the corresponding Clifford/T gate is an exact identity in D[omega] (rz(pi/4) = t up to global phase, rz(pi/2) = s, rz(pi) = z, and m = 0 means the gate is the identity), so the only inexactness anywhere in the pass is the dropped rz(delta) factor accounted for above. No ancilla is introduced, qubit count and the Clifford skeleton are unchanged, so the relaxed/IR path (which cannot represent a non-pi/4 rz at all, as attempt 2 on this circuit found) is never entered: the judge stays on the numerical phase-aligned-distance path for Clifford+Rz circuits.
card.trigger: Over the whole op list of a Clifford+Rz Circuit: for every op with rotation(op) not None, (1) a = normalize(angle) into (-pi, pi]; (2) m = (pi/4)*round(4*a/pi), delta = a - m; (3) skip if |delta| <= 1e-9 (already a pi/4 multiple, already free); (4) d = 2*abs(sin(delta/4)); (5) emit the match (position, m, d) iff d <= 0.9 * (remaining approx budget), where the remaining budget is eps/2 = 5e-4 minus the distance already charged (the two approx rules in the book charge <= 1e-10 each, so essentially all of 5e-4 is free on this circuit). Matches are emitted in increasing d, so the runner tries the cheapest first and the greedy prefix is exactly the knapsack optimum here (all gains are equal to within a T or two). On qae_13 after the book merge the candidate list is headed by the reduced residues of the 2*pi/4*pi-offset angles: 6.283952 -> pi/4096 = 7.670e-4 with d = 3.835e-4 (fits in the 5e-4 budget), then 6.284719 and 12.564837 -> +-pi/2048 with d = 7.67e-4, then +-pi/1024 with d = 1.53e-3, and so on up the dyadic cascade; only the first fits, so exactly one application is expected to be accepted on this circuit. On hhl_8 / qpe_8 / qft_8, which carry many more rotations and a longer dyadic tail, several applications fit the same budget, so the rule is not qae-specific.
card.expected_effect: One accepted snap turns a ~50 T gridsynth rotation (eps_rz = eps_synth/N_Rz ~ 1.1e-5 with the ~90 rotations the book merge leaves) into the identity (m = 0 for the pi/4096 residue), i.e. the rotation and all of its T cost disappear. Secondary effect: N_Rz drops from ~90 to ~89, so eps_rz rises by ~1%, worth a small fraction of a T on each survivor (a few T total). Estimated net on qae_13: 4526 -> ~4475, i.e. about 50 T, with 0 extra qubits, 0 extra CNOTs and 3.8e-4 of the 5e-4 approx budget consumed. I am deliberately estimating this low rather than high: on this circuit the binding constraint is arithmetic, not structural - for any diagonal-phase perturbation the charged distance is first order in the removed angle (2|sin(delta/4)|), the smallest residual angle present is pi/4096, and 5e-4 therefore buys exactly ONE rotation. The value of the card is that this one is certain to fire and to be measurable (unlike the two ancilla/grouping attempts on this circuit, which needed measured-uncompute gadgets the angle-circuit type cannot express, or same-segment equal-angle groups that did not exist), and that the same pass harvests several rotations per circuit on the longer-tailed angle circuits in the suite.

Rotation synthesis cost model and the 3*log2(1/eps) scaling that makes a pi/4-multiple rotation free: N. Ross & P. Selinger, 'Optimal ancilla-free Clifford+T approximation of z-rotations', QIC 16, 901 (2016). Budget allocation across many rotations: M. Amy, D. Maslov, M. Mosca, 'Polynomial-time T-depth optimization of Clifford+T circuits' (2014) and Y. Nam, N. Ross, Y. Su, A. Childs, D. Maslov, npj QI 4, 23 (2018) (angle normalization and Clifford absorption of pi/4 multiples).

card.name: pauli_exponential_dag_reachability_merge
card.identity: Strictly generalize the book's pairwise commutation test to a REACHABILITY test in the anticommutation DAG, which is the exact criterion for mergeability. Step 1 (same frame machinery as pauli_frame_rotation_merge / pauli_exponential_commutation_merge, no ancilla, no measurement): walk the op list once and conjugate each rotation's axis backwards through all preceding Clifford ops (v3.api.pauli.conjugate), so the circuit is rewritten, exactly and up to global phase, as an ordered product of signed n-qubit Pauli exponentials R_{P_1}(t_1) ... R_{P_m}(t_m) followed by one residual Clifford; P_k may be Z-type, X-type or mixed (the 74 h gates make both appear), and angles are first normalized into (-pi, pi] mod 2*pi (the histogram carries 12.173672 = -pi/8 + 4*pi, 6.283952 = 2*pi + pi/4096, etc., and rz(a + 2*pi*k) differs from rz(a) by a global phase only). Step 2: build the directed graph G on {1..m} with an edge k -> l for k < l IFF P_k and P_l ANTICOMMUTE (all other pairs are freely reorderable). Step 3: for every pair i < j with P_j = s*P_i (s = +-1), merge them IFF there is NO directed path i -> ... -> j in G. Note the book rule's condition is the special case 'no single edge i -> k -> j with one intermediate k', i.e. it refuses the pair as soon as ANY anticommuting rotation sits in between; this rule refuses only if the anticommuting blockers form a CHAIN linking i to j, so it fires on every pair where each individual blocker can itself be hoisted out of the interval (before i or after j). Step 4: the edit is made IN PLACE in the original op list exactly as the book rule does: the later rotation's op is deleted and the earlier rotation's angle becomes t_i + s*t_j normalized mod 2*pi; if that is 0 the earlier op is deleted too (BOTH rotations vanish, the generic case for the +-pi/2^d cascade pairs here), and if it is a nonzero multiple of pi/4 with_ops emits the corresponding Clifford/T gate (also removing it from N_Rz). Matches are emitted largest-payoff first (pairs whose angles cancel to 0 mod 2*pi, then pairs that land on the pi/4 grid, then the rest) and the pass is re-run after each accepted application, since a merge deletes nodes from G and can open further paths-free pairs (cascading).
card.correctness: Two Pauli exponentials commute exactly when their Paulis commute: R_P(a) R_Q(b) = R_Q(b) R_P(a) if [P,Q] = 0, since R_P(a) = cos(a/2) I - i sin(a/2) P is a polynomial in P. Hence the total unitary is invariant under ANY permutation of the exponential sequence that preserves the relative order of every anticommuting pair, i.e. under any topological order of G. Claim: if there is no directed path from i to j in G, some topological order of G places i and j adjacent. Proof: let D = {k : i -> ... -> k, i < k < j} be the strict descendants of i inside the interval. No k in D is an ancestor of j (that would give a path i -> ... -> k -> ... -> j), so every element of D may be scheduled after j; every other intermediate node u is not a descendant of i, so it may be scheduled before i. steps.impl_tail:
I wrote the rule file, and `test_rule` reports `never_fires` on `qae_13` and on all four small circuits (`qft_8`, `adder_6`, `mult_4`, `modred_21`). I used 1 of the 5 allowed `test_rule` calls. The cause is in the idea itself, not the implementation.

The criterion cannot admit anything the book rule doesn't already take. Suppose a rotation k sits between i and j and anticommutes with P_i. Since P_j = ±P_i, k anticommutes with P_j too. The graph then has the edges i→k and k→j, so j is always reachable from i. A single blocker is enough to make the path. The reachability test therefore refuses every pair that has at least one blocker and accepts only pairs with an empty blocker set, which is the case the card says to skip. The card's argument that isolated blockers don't link the pair assumes a chain is needed, and it isn't.

I didn't use the remaining 4 calls, because the argument above doesn't depend on circuit data.

The file is at `v3/rules/candidates/pauli_exponential_dag_reachability_merge.py`. It implements the card as written.

IDEA_FAILS: any anticommuting blocker between two same-Pauli rotations anticommutes with both, so a two-edge path i→k→j always exists and the reachability test never admits a pair the book rule doesn't already merge.

card.name: zx_phase_teleportation_angle_classes
card.identity: Phase teleportation: use a ZX-diagram simplification only to DISCOVER which rotations may be summed, then edit the original op list in place (angles only, structure bit-for-bit untouched). (1) BUILD a ZX graph from the 1034-op list: one green (Z) spider per diagonal op (rz(theta), t, tdg, s, sdg, z), h = Hadamard edge, cx = green(control)/red(target) pair, cz = green-green with an H-edge; wires are vertex chains. Record provenance: spider v_i <- op index p_i, wire q_i, angle theta_i. (2) SYMBOLISE: every rotation whose angle is NOT a multiple of pi/4 is replaced by a PHASE GADGET carrying a FORMAL VARIABLE x_i instead of theta_i (a gadget = a phaseless spider connected by an H-edge to a 1-valent spider holding x_i, connected to the rest exactly where the spider sat); Clifford phases (multiples of pi/2) and the pi/4 phases of t/tdg stay numeric. (3) REDUCE the symbolic graph with the standard graph-theoretic rule set to graph-like form and then to a fixpoint: spider fusion, identity removal, colour change, local complementation (lcomp_simp) on pi/2 spiders, pivoting (pivot_simp) on pi-spider pairs, pivot_gadget_simp, and crucially gadget_simp. All of these are sound ZX rewrites that are valid for ANY value of the variables, so they never need to add, split or numerically alter a symbolic phase; they only move gadgets, flip their signs (local complementation / pivoting conjugate a gadget phase by -1), and FUSE two gadgets whose neighbourhoods have become identical, replacing their phases by the formal sum s_i x_i + s_j x_j. (4) HARVEST: at the fixpoint each surviving gadget carries a formal sum over a class S = {i_1 < ... < i_m} with signs s_i in {+1,-1}; classes with m >= 2 are the discovered merges. Also harvest classes whose formal sum has provably zero coefficient (a gadget that was removed entirely), which cancel outright. (5) APPLY to the ORIGINAL circuit, one class per match: let j0 = min S; set op p_{j0}'s angle to theta_eff = (sum_{i in S} s_{j0} s_i theta_i) reduced mod 2pi into (-pi, pi]; delete the ops p_i for i in S \ {j0}; if theta_eff == 0 (to 1e-12) delete p_{j0} too, and if theta_eff is a multiple of pi/4 let with_ops demote it to z/s/sdg/t/tdg (both cases retire TWO synthesized rotations). No Clifford op, no cx, no h, no qubit is added, removed or reordered. Classes are enumerated by descending m, positions recomputed after each accepted application.
card.correctness: The ZX rewrite rules used in step (3) (spider fusion, identity, colour change, local complementation, pivoting, gadget fusion) are each sound equalities of linear maps up to a scalar, and global scalars/phases are unobservable (invariant 6); this is the Duncan-Kissinger-Perdrix-van de Wetering simplification and is proved there. The whole point of running them on SYMBOLIC phases is a parametricity argument (Kissinger-van de Wetering, PRA 102, 022406, Sec. 5): the derived equality D(x_1,...,x_R) = D'(x_1,...,x_R) holds as an identity of diagrams in the free variables, hence for EVERY real substitution. When gadget fusion merges gadgets i and j it yields a diagram in which only the combination s_i x_i + s_j x_j appears; therefore the two substitutions (x_i = theta_i, x_j = theta_j) and (x_i = s_i(s_i theta_i + s_j theta_j), x_j = 0) give diagrams equal to the same reduced diagram, hence equal to each other. Since the reduced diagram was obtained from the ORIGINAL diagram, the original circuit with angles (theta_i, theta_j) equals the original circuit with angles (theta_eff, 0) - which is exactly the in-place edit of step (5). This is why phase teleportation needs no resynthesis and no extraction from the reduced graph: the reduced graph is a certificate, never emitted. A spider with phase 0 is the identity on its wire, so deleting the donor op is exact. The mod-2pi reduction changes only a global phase (Rz(2pi) = -I). The only floating point is the summation of angles, the same arithmetic level as the already-accepted merge rules, so the frozen judge's phase-aligned operator distance on the changed window is at double-rounding level (and the exact D[omega] check applies whenever theta_eff demotes to a pi/4 multiple, both sides then being Clifford+T). Soundness does not depend on the reduction finding anything: with no fusion there is no class, and the rule is a no-op.
card.trigger: Any class of >= 2 non-pi/4 rotation ops that the symbolic graph reduction fuses into one gadget (or annihilates). This is the mechanism that is absent from the entire book and that the measured history on this circuit points at. Both book merge rules are frame/commutation arguments in the ORIGINAL gate order: pauli_frame_rotation_merge needs the transported axis to land back as +-Z on an earlier rotation's own wire, pauli_exponential_commutation_merge needs P_j = +-P_k AND commutation with every intervening rotation Pauli - and exact axis-level merging is provably blocked whenever intermediate non-Clifford rotations anticommute, which on qpe_8 (258 h against 257 rz, trigram census dominated by h-interleaved rotations: 'h rz rz' 42x, 'h rz h' 40x, 'rz h h' 40x, 'rz h rz' 28x, 'sdg h rz' 28x) is the common case; attempt 1 fired 3 times for 192 T and the pair rule scored its gain on hhl_8, not here. Gadget fusion is not an axis-equality test: pivoting and local complementation RESHAPE the diagram's connectivity first, so two rotations whose Pauli frames are different in the circuit order can still end up on gadgets with identical neighbourhoods and fuse. It also needs no ancilla, no measurement and no non-grid gate inside a relaxed candidate - which attempt 3 showed is fatal on this family (the relaxed judge works over Z[omega] and rejected the candidate with 'rz(0.0245...) is not a multiple of pi/4', so every ancilla/measurement construction on a Clifford+Rz circuit is unverifiable by construction). Headroom check: the reported pyzx number on this circuit (11485) is its structure-rewriting reduction and coincides with what the book already reaches, whereas phase teleportation is the strictly stronger T-count routine (pyzx's teleport_reduce) that keeps the circuit and only sums phases; nothing in the book implements it.
card.expected_effect: A surviving non-grid rz costs gridsynth ~48 T at the current operating point (11485 T over ~240 surviving rotations). A fused class of size m retires m-1 rotations (~48(m-1) T); a class whose signed sum is 0 mod 2pi, or lands on the pi/4 grid, retires all m (~48m T). Secondary bonus: eps_rz = eps_synth / N_Rz, so retiring r rotations relaxes the tolerance of the survivors by ~3 log2(240/(240-r)) T each (r = 30 gives ~0.6 T on ~210 survivors, ~120 T free). Calibration, deliberately conservative because the three previous estimates on this circuit came in at 192 T, unmeasured and 0 T: the quantity this rule depends on is the number of gadget fusions the reduction actually finds, which is not visible in the gate histogram, and the H density that killed attempt 1 is precisely what makes the graph large (so the reduction is the expensive part, not the gain). I assume only small classes form - roughly 20-40 fusions of size 2-3 plus a handful of outright cancellations from the exact-inverse angle families in the histogram (10.566379 with 1.999991, sum = 4pi to 1e-6, each x15) - i.e. 25-55 rotations retired, ~1200-2600 T: 11485 -> roughly 8900-10300, on the exact contract, spending none of the 5e-4 approximation budget. CNOT count stays at 268 and qubit count at 8, so both tie-breakers below T are exactly neutral.

card.name: single_qubit_run_unitary_clifford_t_synthesis
card.identity: Price a maximal single-wire run as ONE SU(2) element instead of as several priced rotations, and emit it as an explicit Clifford+T word. (1) SEGMENT: for each wire q, cut the op list into maximal runs R = (op_{i1} < ... < op_{im}) of consecutive ops that touch ONLY q, over {h, s, sdg, x, z, t, tdg, rz}; a run ends at the first cx/cz touching q (ops on other wires in between are irrelevant and are left bit-for-bit in place, since they commute with every op of the run: disjoint support). (2) TARGET: build the run's 2x2 unitary U = M(op_{im}) ... M(op_{i1}) in numpy, normalise to SU(2) by dividing by sqrt(det U) (global phase, unobservable), and let nrz = number of ops in R whose Z-angle is NOT a multiple of pi/4, nt = number of t/tdg ops in R. (3) APPROXIMATE-AND-SYNTHESISE U directly over the ring, at target distance delta = 1e-6, with the two-step Ross-Selinger/Kliuchnikov-Maslov-Mosca procedure: (3a) pick the denominator exponent k = ceil(3*log2(1/delta)) and search for V = [[u, -conj(t)],[t, conj(u)]] / sqrt(2)^k with u, t in Z[omega] (omega = e^{i pi/4}) and the norm condition |u|^2 + |t|^2 = 2^k, such that ||U - V||_2 <= delta: enumerate candidates u in the lattice Z[omega] inside the small disk of radius delta*sqrt(2)^k around sqrt(2)^k * U[0,0] (a 2-real-dimensional grid enumeration over the Z[sqrt2]-module Z[omega], the same 'grid problem' RS solve in 1 dimension for a z-rotation, here in 2 because a general unitary leaves both real and imaginary parts of u free), and for each candidate solve the relative norm equation |t|^2 = 2^k - |u|^2 for t in Z[omega] (an element of Z[sqrt2]; solvable iff its prime factorisation over Z[sqrt2] splits appropriately, decided and constructed with sympy.factorint plus prime splitting in Z[omega], exactly as in gridsynth's Diophantine step); take the first solvable candidate, incrementing k by 1 and retrying if none is found within a fixed enumeration cap. (3b) EXACT-SYNTHESISE V into a literal Clifford+T word by the Giles-Selinger/KMM denominator-reduction algorithm: while k > 0, left-multiply by H T^j for the unique j in {0,1,2,3} that lowers the smallest denominator exponent of the first column (a finite check in Z[omega]), recording the inverse gates; when k = 0 the residue is a single-qubit Clifford, emitted as an h/s/sdg/x/z word. The result is a gate list W over {h, s, sdg, x, z, t, tdg} only, with T-count(W) = (number of t/tdg in W), known exactly before anything is edited. (4) COST TEST, computed not guessed: fire only if T-count(W) + 2 <= C_rz * nrz + nt with C_rz = 35 (a deliberately pessimistic lower bound on the metric's per-rotation gridsynth cost at the circuit's eps_rz; the measured operating point on this circuit is ~45), and only if nrz >= 2. (5) APPLY: delete the m ops of R and insert W at position i1 on wire q; nothing else in the op list moves, no qubit is added, no cx/cz is touched. One match = one run; runs are enumerated by descending (C_rz * nrz + nt) and a global cap of 300 accepted runs keeps the charged error at <= 3e-4 < eps/2 = 5e-4.
card.correctness: The rewrite is an approximation with an explicitly measured error, which is what the approx contract charges. (a) Locality: every op of R acts on q alone, so U is exactly the run's action and the ops interleaved on other wires commute with all of them; replacing the run by W therefore changes the circuit only by the factor U -> W on wire q (tensored with identity), and the phase-aligned operator distance of the whole circuit is bounded by min_phi ||e^{i phi} W - U||_2, which is <= delta = 1e-6 by the accept test in (3a); the frozen judge re-measures this same distance on the changed window and charges it. Distances compose subadditively for unitaries (||A_1...A_r - B_1...B_r|| <= sum_j ||A_j - B_j||, operator norm being submultiplicative and unitary-invariant), so <= 300 accepted runs charge <= 3e-4 of the 5e-4 approximation half-budget. Global phase is unobservable (invariant 6), which legitimises both the sqrt(det) normalisation and the phi minimisation. (b) The ring step is exact algebra, not a fit: any unitary of the form [[u, -conj(t)],[t, conj(u)]]/sqrt(2)^k with u,t in Z[omega] and |u|^2+|t|^2 = 2^k is exactly representable in Clifford+T, and conversely every exactly representable single-qubit Clifford+T unitary has this form with k equal to its smallest denominator exponent (Kliuchnikov-Maslov-Mosca exact synthesis; Giles-Selinger). The denominator-reduction loop in (3b) is the constructive direction of that theorem and terminates, so W is not searched for numerically - it is read off, and ||U - V|| is then evaluated once in double precision on the 2x2 matrices, far above the 1e-6 accept threshold in accuracy. (c) Why the T-count is lower than what the metric pays for the same run: the set of exactly representable single-qubit Clifford+T unitaries with T-count k has size Theta(2^k) and is equidistributed over the 3-real-dimensional group SU(2) up to the known number-theoretic obstruction, so covering SU(2) to precision delta needs k ~ 3 log2(1/delta) - the SAME asymptotic cost as Ross-Selinger spends on ONE axial rotation Rz(theta), because the Diophantine condition, not the dimension of the target family, is what sets the constant 3. A run written with nrz non-grid rotations is therefore billed nrz times for an object whose intrinsic cost is one rotation's worth: the saving is a pricing artefact of per-rz synthesis, and it is real under this metric because the emitted W contains literal t/tdg gates that the metric counts directly and no rz at all. (d) Failure is a no-op, never an unsound edit: if no solvable u is found inside the cap, or if the cost test in (4) fails, the run is skipped.
card.trigger: Any maximal single-wire run containing >= 2 non-pi/4 rz ops (explicit t/tdg and Clifford ops in the run are absorbed for free) whose synthesised word passes the arithmetic cost test. On qpe_8 the census says these runs are the dominant local structure and that they are NOT single-rotation: the top trigrams are 'h rz rz' 42x, 'rz h h' 40x, 'h rz h' 40x, 'rz h rz' 28x, 'sdg h rz' 28x - i.e. rotations stacked on one wire with only h/s/sdg between them, which is exactly a 2-to-4-rotation SU(2) run and never a mergeable pair (an h between two rz flips the axis from Z to X, so no same-Pauli rule can touch them). This is the precise complement of everything in the book and of the measured limitations on this circuit: pauli_frame_rotation_merge and pauli_exponential_commutation_merge both need two rotations about the SAME Pauli (attempt 1: 3 applications, 192 T against an estimate of 2700, 'segments end at every H'), pauli_subalgebra_dimension_recompression needs #rotations > the Lie-closure dimension d, which for a 1-qubit run is d = 3, so it cannot fire on the 2- and 3-rotation runs that dominate here, and it would in any case only re-emit rz ops at 45 T each rather than change what a run is billed. This rule does not merge anything and does not need any coincidence of axes or angles: a 2-rotation run with two completely unrelated angles qualifies. It also needs no ancilla and no measurement, which attempt 3 showed is fatal on this family (the relaxed judge works over Z[omega] and rejected the candidate with 'rz(0.0245...) is not a multiple of pi/4', so every ancilla/measurement construction on a Clifford+Rz circuit is unverifiable here by construction).
card.expected_effect: The metric's operating point is ~45 T per surviving non-grid rz (11485 T over ~250 rotations). A qualifying run is re-billed once: at delta = 1e-6 the synthesised word has T-count ~48-60, so a 2-rotation run goes from ~90 T to ~55 T (-35), a 3-rotation run from ~135 to ~55 (-80), a 4-rotation run from ~180 to ~55 (-125), and any explicit t/tdg sitting inside the run (there are 157 t/tdg in the circuit, and 'cx t cx' 29x / 'cx tdg cx' 43x says many sit in short single-wire runs) is absorbed at zero extra cost. The binding quantity is the run census, which I cannot read off the summary exactly: with 257 rz over 8 wires cut by 268 cx, the trigram counts above imply roughly 40-70 runs holding 2 or more non-grid rotations, i.e. ~100-200 rotations retired for ~40-70 synthesised words, which is ~1400-3500 T, taking 11485 to roughly 8000-10100 - the first mechanism on this circuit to reach BQSKit-DPF's 8020, and the only one that explains that baseline, since DPF is the only comparator that re-synthesises blocks as units rather than pricing each rotation. Second-order bonus: N_Rz falls, and eps_rz = eps_synth / N_Rz, so the remaining rotations each get ~3*log2(250/(250-r)) T cheaper (r = 150 gives ~3 T on each of ~100 survivors). I quote 1800 as the point estimate rather than the midpoint: the two earlier overshoots on this circuit (2700 estimated / 192 measured; 1800 estimated / 0 measured) came from assuming structural coincidences the input did not have, whereas the only unknown here is how many runs carry >= 2 rotations - the per-run saving is computed arithmetically from the synthesised word before any edit, so a thin census degrades the rule to a partial win, not to a miss. CNOT count is unchanged (no cx/cz is touched); qubit count stays 8; charged error <= 3e-4 of the 5e-4 approximation budget, which is currently entirely unspent on this circuit.

Computers 65(1):161-172 (2016) - the characterisation of exactly representable unitaries as [[u,-t*],[t,u*]]/sqrt(2)^k with T-count = k, the denominator-reduction synthesis algorithm, and the result that approximating an ARBITRARY single-qubit unitary costs the same Theta(log(1/eps)) as approximating one z-rotation; B. card.name: controlled_gaussian_givens_resynthesis
card.identity: Resynthesise CLOCK-CONTROLLED free-fermion (Gaussian) evolution, the case the book's free_fermion_gaussian_resynthesis rejects, by factoring each branch's orthogonal matrix with a deterministic Givens cascade and re-controlling it through the homomorphism (controlled product = product of controlled factors). Steps. (1) Pauli-frame normal form (exact, symplectic, no numerics): walk the op list once, maintain K_p = product of the Clifford ops before position p, and replace each rotation op (rz/t/tdg, Z-angle a_p on qubit q_p) by the signed Pauli exponential R_p = exp(-i a_p P_p / 2) with P_p = K_p Z_{q_p} K_p^dag (v3.api.pauli.conjugate, applied incrementally); the Clifford skeleton C_out is kept verbatim. (2) Classify each axis: fix the Jordan-Wigner Majorana operators on an ordered system-wire set S = (s_0..s_{k-1}), c_{2a} = (prod_{b<a} Z_{s_b}) X_{s_a}, c_{2a+1} = (prod_{b<a} Z_{s_b}) Y_{s_a}; a Pauli string is a BILINEAR iff it equals +-i c_mu c_nu for some mu<nu (test by table lookup: the 2k(2k-1)/2 bilinear strings are precomputed once, so the test is exact string matching, including the Hadamard-conjugated images already used by the book rule). Axis P_p is ADMISSIBLE iff P_p = s_p * (Z-string on the complementary 'clock' wires C) tensor (bilinear on S); the Z-string part is recorded as a bit vector u_p in GF(2)^{|C|} (u_p = 0 means uncontrolled). (3) Segment: take a maximal consecutive run R_i..R_j of the normal form in which every axis is admissible, all bilinears live on the SAME wire set S, and the set of non-zero clock strings occurring is a single vector u. Every axis is diagonal on C, so the run unitary is block diagonal over the clock computational basis: for clock states with u.z = 0 it acts as the Gaussian G_+, for u.z = 1 as G_-. (4) Branch matrices: in the Majorana picture a rotation exp(-i a (Z^u tensor i c_mu c_nu)/2) acts on the branch by the single plane rotation of angle +-a in the (mu,nu) plane, sign (-1)^{u.z}; multiply the plane rotations of the run in order to get R_+ , R_- in O(2k) (real 2k x 2k matrices, k <= 4 here), and the branch phases phi_+ , phi_- (each plane rotation contributes a known branch-independent phase; recover phi_+- instead by one phase-aligned comparison of the emitted branch unitary against the dense branch unitary of the run on the <= 2^k system amplitudes). (5) Refactor: U_run = (I tensor G_+) * (u-controlled H), H the Gaussian with orthogonal matrix R_H = R_+^T R_- and phase phi_- - phi_+ . Factor R_+ and R_H each by the standard Givens/Jacobi cascade into at most k(2k-1) adjacent-plane rotations (scipy/numpy, deterministic ordering). Emit: each Givens angle theta of R_+ as ONE Pauli rotation exp(-i theta B/2) (B the bilinear of that plane, lowered to Cliffords + one rz by the usual basis-change + CX-ladder gadget); each Givens angle theta of R_H as the u-CONTROLLED Pauli rotation exp(-i theta (I - Z^u) tensor B /4) = the pair exp(-i (theta/2) B/2) * exp(+i (theta/2) (Z^u tensor B)/2), i.e. TWO rz's; finally one rz(phi_- - phi_+) on the parity Z^u (CX ladder + rz) to fix the branch phase. So the whole run becomes at most 3k(2k-1) + 1 non-Clifford rotations regardless of how many it contained. (6) The match is (span of the original op positions covered by the run, replacement op list); the trailing Clifford of the normal form is re-emitted at the span boundary so every op outside the span is byte-identical. Accept only if the number of non-Clifford rotations strictly drops and the phase-aligned operator distance of the span is <= 1e-9; angles within 1e-10 of a multiple of pi/4 are snapped (with_ops lowers them to Clifford/T), angles within 1e-10 of 0 are dropped. Runs too wide to build densely are bisected and emitted as two matches; the judge verifies and costs each match on its own.
card.correctness: (a) The normal form is exact: for Clifford C and Pauli P, C exp(-i a P/2) = exp(-i a (C P C^dag)/2) C, since C f(P) C^dag = f(C P C^dag) and C P C^dag is again a signed Pauli; no commutation hypothesis is used, so the run is an ORDERED product of Pauli exponentials equal to the original segment up to global phase. (b) Block structure: every admissible axis has a Z-string (diagonal) clock part, so all run factors commute with every clock Z and the run is block diagonal in the clock computational basis; with a single non-zero clock string u there are exactly two blocks, selected by the parity u.z, giving U_run = P_{u.z=0} tensor G_+ + P_{u.z=1} tensor G_-. (c) Each block is Gaussian: the bilinears i c_mu c_nu span so(2k) under commutation ([c_mu c_nu, c_rho c_sigma] is again a bilinear by the Clifford-algebra relations c_mu c_nu + c_nu c_mu = 2 delta_{mu nu}), and exp(-i a (i c_mu c_nu)/2) conjugates the Majoranas by the plane rotation of angle a in the (mu,nu) plane; the map G -> R is the standard 2-to-1 homomorphism Spin(2k) -> SO(2k), so multiplying the run's plane rotations gives R_+- exactly, and the only data outside SO(2k) is the branch phase, which is a single real number per branch and is restored by step (5). (d) Re-controlling is valid because G -> (u-controlled G) is a group homomorphism on each branch: a product of u-controlled factors equals the u-controlled product (each factor is the identity on the u.z = 0 branch and the corresponding factor on the other), so factoring R_H into Givens rotations and controlling each factor reproduces H exactly; and exp(-i theta (I - Z^u) tensor B / 4) is literally the identity on the even-parity branch and exp(-i theta B/2) on the odd one, realised as two ordinary Pauli rotations of half angle, which is the standard controlled-rotation identity. (e) Factorisation completeness: the Givens/Jacobi cascade writes any element of O(2k) as at most k(2k-1) adjacent-plane rotations (times a determinant-fixing reflection, which is a Clifford Majorana swap and costs no rotation), so the emitted rotation count is bounded independently of the run length - this is exactly the mechanism of the book's free_fermion rule, here extended to the controlled case. (f) Error and locality: the span is a dependency-contiguous span of the normal form, so U = W_2 V W_1 and replacing V by W gives || W_2 W W_1 - e^{i phi} W_2 V W_1 || = || W - e^{i phi} V || by unitary invariance; distances add subadditively, and the only error is floating point in the Givens factorisation and the branch-phase fit (<= 1e-9 per accepted span, a handful of spans, so <= 1e-8 total against the approx allowance eps/2 = 5e-4 - eps_rz for the survivors is not tightened). Every application is re-verified by the frozen judge. (g) Why the book cannot reach this: pauli_frame_rotation_merge and pauli_exponential_commutation_merge only delete rotations with EQUAL axes (saturated here, the circuit is already below pyzx's 29205); free_fermion_gaussian_resynthesis demands that every axis be an uncontrolled bilinear and therefore rejects the clock-controlled axes that dominate hhl_8; pauli_subalgebra_dimension_recompression tried to absorb the controlled case into one big Lie closure and measured only 520 T (7 firings) because the closure of {Z^u tensor bilinear} has dimension 2^{|C|} k(2k-1), which exceeds the run length almost immediately and forces the segments shut, and because its replacement is a dense least-squares fit over a basis of that closure. This rule never forms that algebra: it splits the run analytically into two Gaussian branches of dimension k(2k-1) each and factors them by a deterministic cascade, so the compression ratio does not depend on a numerical optimiser finding a global minimum.
card.trigger: A maximal consecutive run of rotation ops in the Clifford-pushed normal form such that (i) every axis factorises as (signed Z-string on the clock wires C) tensor (Jordan-Wigner Majorana bilinear on a fixed system wire set S, bilinear membership decided by exact string matching against the precomputed table), (ii) exactly one non-zero clock string u occurs (axes with clock part I are allowed and go into the uncontrolled branch factor), (iii) the run contains more than 3k(2k-1) + 1 non-Clifford rotations, k = |S|, and (iv) step (5) reaches phase-aligned distance <= 1e-9 with strictly fewer non-Clifford rotations. No condition on the angles. On hhl_8 (8 qubits, 2208 ops, 583 rz + 101 t + 101 tdg, 607 h, 497 cx, 175 s, 119 sdg, ~491 non-Clifford rotations left at 28509 T) the circuit is QPE / inverse-QPE around the eigenvalue-inversion rotations: the angle histogram shows the exact dyadic QFT phases pi/32 = 0.098175, pi/16 = 0.19635, 5pi/64 = 0.245348, pi/8 = 0.392699 together with their 4pi complements (12.173672 = 4pi - pi/8 x5, 12.370021 = 4pi - pi/16 x3), and the generic angles come in +-theta pairs (0.89499 / 11.671381, 1.080325 / 11.486046, 2.671 / 9.895727), the signature of controlled e^{+-i A 2^j t}. For the standard HHL matrix (tridiagonal / hopping A) the system-register axes are Majorana bilinears and the clock control is a single qubit per power, so each controlled-evolution block is exactly case (ii); the trigram evidence for one-wire and two-wire alternating chains ('h rz h' x117, 'rz cx rz' x79, 'h rz rz' x78, 'cx tdg cx' x66) is the lowered form of those plane rotations. If the matrix turns out not to be Gaussian the bilinear test fails on some axis and the rule emits no match at all (no risk of a wrong accept, and the judge re-checks anyway).
card.expected_effect: Each non-Clifford rotation removed deletes one gridsynth sequence worth 3 log2(1/eps_rz) ~ 57-58 T at eps_rz = 1.72e-6, and shrinking N_Rz loosens eps_rz for the survivors (~0.8 T per survivor per 100 removed). With k = 4 system modes the bound per controlled run is 3*4*7 + 1 = 85 rotations; hhl_8 has one such run per clock power in the QPE half and one per power in the inverse-QPE half, and those runs together carry most of the ~491 surviving rotations. Even if only the two or three largest controlled-evolution runs fire and each drops from ~120-150 rotations to <= 85, that is ~70-110 rotations removed = 4000-6400 T; the QFT/IQFT phases and the inversion rotations are untouched (their axes are not bilinears, so they bound the gain from below). I therefore expect 28509 -> ~23000-25000, i.e. the first real move toward BQSKit-DPF's 19443, which is the only baseline past the exact-merge wall on this circuit. I deliberately estimate at the low end of the structural bound because the two previous numerical-refit cards on this circuit measured 176 T and 520 T against estimates of 7500 and 6500: their blockers were op-list-contiguous <= 3-qubit windows and an exploding Lie closure, both of which this rule avoids (analytic Givens cascade on a 2k x 2k real matrix, two branches), but the number of rotations that actually pass the bilinear test is the remaining unknown. CNOT count can rise inside a resynthesised span (each emitted Pauli rotation carries a basis change and a CX ladder), which is only the third lexicographic key and is bounded by the judge's accept test; qubit count is untouched (no ancillas); the error charge is ~1e-8.

card.name: hamming_weight_phasing_same_angle_group
card.identity: Replace k >= 3 rotations that carry the SAME angle magnitude and act about PAIRWISE COMMUTING Pauli axes by ceil(log2(k+1)) rotations on a Hamming-weight register held in clean ancillas. Steps. (1) Pauli-frame normal form (exact, symplectic, no numerics): walk the op list once maintaining K_p = product of the Clifford ops before position p, and replace each rotation op (rz/t/tdg, angle a_p on qubit q_p) by the signed Pauli exponential R_p = exp(-i a_p P_p / 2), P_p = K_p Z_{q_p} K_p^dag (v3.api.pauli.conjugate, applied incrementally); the Clifford skeleton is kept verbatim and re-emitted at the span boundary. (2) Segment: cut the rotation sequence into maximal consecutive runs in which ALL axes pairwise commute (exact symplectic test). Inside such a run the factors commute, so they may be reordered and grouped freely. (3) Group: normalise each angle to the window (-pi, pi] modulo 2pi (rz is 2pi-periodic up to global phase), and let a group be a set G = {(P_i, s_i)} of rotations in one run whose normalised |angle| equals a common theta to within 1e-12, with s_i = sign(angle_i) in {+1,-1}, whose axes {P_i} are linearly INDEPENDENT in the GF(2) symplectic representation, and with |G| = k >= 3. (4) Diagonalise: by symplectic Gaussian elimination build one Clifford D (h/s/sdg/cx/cz only) with D P_i D^dag = +-Z_{w_i} on k distinct wires w_1..w_k; absorb the residual signs into s_i. The group unitary becomes prod_i exp(-i s_i theta Z_{w_i} / 2) conjugated by D, i.e. a phase e^{-i theta (sum_i s_i (-1)^{b_{w_i}}) / 2} on the computational basis state b -- a function of the integer W(b) = #{i : b_{w_i} XOR [s_i = -1] = 1} only. (5) Weight register: append m = ceil(log2(k+1)) CLEAN ancillas |0>^m and compute W reversibly from the k control wires with a ripple of full adders (standard Hamming-weight / popcount tree: approximately k - m Toffolis plus CNOTs, each Toffoli either the 7-T Clifford+T circuit, or the 4-T AND-compute gadget with measured uncompute if the IR layer is available); wires carrying s_i = -1 are conjugated by an X on that wire immediately before and after the adder network, which flips the counted bit exactly (X Z X = -Z, so this is the sign, with no extra phase). card.name: linear_glue_cnot_resynthesis_across_and_gadgets
card.identity: Resynthesize every maximal CX/X-only subnetwork of the op list as one F2 affine map, including the networks that sit BETWEEN two non-Clifford gadgets. Procedure: (1) Scan the op list and cut it into maximal blocks of consecutive gates drawn from {cx, x} only (a block may be grown across a gate g that is not cx/x provided g's wires are disjoint from the block's wires, by commuting g out; this is what lets the 'unload the fan-in of gadget r' network and the 'load the fan-in of gadget r+1' network fuse into ONE block, since the two networks are separated only by the gadget's own cz/cx-into-target gates and its measurement fix-up, which touch other wires). (2) For a block B on wire support W (|W| = m), compute its exact action as an invertible affine map over F2: an m x m invertible matrix M plus a constant vector c, by initialising rows to the unit basis and applying cx(i,j): row_j += row_i, x(j): c_j += 1. (3) Re-synthesize (M, c) from scratch: run Patel-Markov-Hayes Gaussian elimination (lower-triangular then upper-triangular elimination with the m/log2(m)-size column-partition heuristic) on M to get a CX list, then emit X gates for the nonzero entries of the transformed constant vector. Also run plain column-by-column Gauss-Jordan and greedy row-reduction variants and keep the shortest CX list found. (4) Replace block B by the synthesized list only if the new CX count is strictly smaller; the T-count is untouched by construction (no non-Clifford gate is created or destroyed) and the qubit count is unchanged. The special case that does the work on this circuit: when a fan-in network L (loading affine forms onto gadget-factor wires or ancillas) is immediately followed by its own inverse L^{-1} and then by the next gadget's fan-in L', the fused block has matrix L' * L^{-1} * L = L', i.e. the unload/reload pair collapses and only the net change of basis between consecutive products survives.
card.correctness: Each step is an exact Clifford identity. (i) cx and x generate exactly the group of invertible affine maps on the computational basis, and they are permutation matrices in that basis, so a CX/X block is faithfully represented by (M, c) over F2: cx(i,j) is the elementary row addition row_j += row_i and x(j) is the translation c_j += 1, and the block's unitary is determined by (M, c) alone (no phases: both gates are real permutation matrices with no relative phase). Two CX/X lists with the same (M, c) are therefore the SAME unitary, exactly, not merely up to global phase. (ii) Patel-Markov-Hayes synthesis is a factorization of M into elementary row additions (it performs Gaussian elimination to the identity and reads the eliminations backwards), so the emitted list has matrix M by construction; the emitted list is re-simulated symbolically over F2 and compared entrywise with (M, c) before emission, so a synthesis bug can only cause a non-fire. (iii) Growing a block across a gate g whose wires are disjoint from the block support is the exact commutation [A ox I, I ox B] = 0 on disjoint tensor factors; the rule checks wire-disjointness gate by gate, including the wires read by classically controlled fix-up gates and measured wires, so no gadget is reordered with respect to anything it interacts with and no measurement is moved across its own fix-up. (iv) Nothing non-Clifford is created, moved or deleted, so the error budget is untouched (exact contract) and no ancilla is added, so the relaxed-construction bookkeeping of the surrounding AND gadgets is unaffected: the wires entering each and_compute carry exactly the same bits as before, hence the same measurement-branch phases and the same c_m = 1 for every branch.
card.trigger: Any dv circuit, angle-level or Toffoli-level (IRCircuit or Circuit). Find every maximal block of cx/x gates under the wire-disjointness commutation of step (1); require the block to contain at least 2 gates and at least 2 distinct wires. For each such block compute (M, c), re-synthesize, and emit a match only when the shortest synthesized list is strictly shorter than the block. Matches are independent (disjoint op ranges) and are applied one at a time. No ancilla, no measurement, no angle condition, so the trigger cannot miss for structural reasons: it fires on the post-book mult_4 form (the CX fan-in / unload networks around the 9 AND gadgets and the mod-x^4+x+1 XOR reduction), on the raw ccz form (the 3 cx gates plus the H-sandwich structure leaves the cx runs intact), and on every other dv_recon target (adder_8, mcx_10, modred_21) and on the Clifford glue of the angle circuits.
card.expected_effect: T is unchanged at 36 and so are the qubits: on this circuit the 9 Gidney AND gadgets are forced (bilinear complexity of F_{2^4} multiplication is 9, Barbulescu-Detrey-Estibals-Zimmermann, and the stabilizer-nullity lower bound for CCZ is 4 T, which the measured AND already attains, so 9 x 4 = 36 T is a hard floor and attempts 2 and 3 in history confirmed nothing below it). The admissible gain is the third lexicographic key, which history attempt 3 identified explicitly as the only one left on mult_4 ('the only possible gain is fewer CNOTs from reordering the products, and it needs a different rule from the one specified'). The current form pays, per product, |u_r| + |v_r| CX to load the two affine Karatsuba forms and the same again to unload, about 8 CX per product plus the reduction XORs: roughly 70-80 CX over the segment. Fusing each unload/reload pair into the net basis change and resynthesizing it leaves 1-3 CX per register per product plus one restoring network, about 30-40 CX: an expected drop of 30-40 CNOT at identical T and identical qubits. card.name: toffoli_compute_uncompute_pair_measured_lowering
card.identity: Pairwise (not run-wise) lowering of a Toffoli and its own later inverse on a zero-valued wire, by dataflow matching only -- no truth tables, no symbolic algebra, no whole-circuit function recognition. Normalize ccz legs to ccx where an h(q) ... h(q) pair brackets all the ccz's that touch q in between (the leg is a target; this is the correct normalization for THIS input, where consecutive ccx's with the same target share a Hadamard so the h's are NOT one-per-ccz: 34 h for 32 ccz, trigram 'ccz h ccz' x30). Then, for each wire a, list in order the ops that WRITE a (ccx/cx/x with a as target). Match a pair of write-ops (i, j), i < j, as a compute/uncompute pair iff: (a) both are ccx with the SAME unordered control pair {x, y} and the same target a; (b) the value of a immediately before op i is provably the constant 0 -- either i is the first write of a and a is a harness ancilla initialized to |0>, or the previous write of a is itself the second half of an already-matched pair (so a was returned to 0 there); (c) no op between i and j writes a, x or y (writes = being the target of ccx/cx/x or any non-diagonal single-qubit op; a, x, y may appear freely as CONTROLS of cx/ccx/cz/ccz and under phase gates); (d) no op between i and j is a measurement or classically controlled op on a. REPLACE op i by and_compute(x, y -> a) [the 4-T clean-|0> AND gadget] and op j by and_uncompute(a) [H on a, Z-basis measurement, classically controlled CZ(x, y) fix-up, 0 T]; every op between i and j is left untouched, since a carries exactly the same classical value (x & y) there as before. Matching is greedy innermost-first and pairs are disjoint; unmatched ccx's are left to the existing book rule (4 T each). Wires are reused, no new qubits are requested, so the qubit count does not change.
card.correctness: Classically, ccx(x,y,a) with a = 0 beforehand leaves a = x & y, and the second identical ccx with x, y unchanged (condition c) leaves a = (x&y) ^ (x&y) = 0, so the pair is exactly a compute/uncompute of the temporary AND and every intervening op sees the same value of a as in the original circuit -- the replacement is functionally identical on all inputs. Quantum correctness of the two gadgets: and_compute maps |x>|y>|0> to |x>|y>|x&y> exactly, with no relative phase (Gidney's T,T,T,Tdg clean-ancilla AND), so it agrees with ccx on the restricted input a = 0, which condition (b) certifies. At op j, a holds the computational-basis function x&y of the current x, y (condition c), so the joint state is sum_z alpha_z |z>_{rest} |x(z) & y(z)>_a; applying H to a and measuring in the Z basis yields outcome m with probability 1/2, independent of z, and leaves the residual operator (-1)^{m (x & y)} = CZ(x,y)^m on the data, which the classically controlled CZ(x, y) cancels exactly. Hence for each branch K_m |u> = c_m |f(u)> with c_m = 2^{-1/2} for ALL u (phase consistency, invariant 2) and sum_m |c_m|^2 = 1; the gadget's classically controlled X returns a to |0>, so the wire is a clean ancilla again and can be matched as condition (b) for the next pair on that wire. The only facts needed are local dataflow facts (b), (c), (d), each decidable by one scan of the ops between i and j -- the reason this rule is cheap on every circuit, matching or not: cost is O(#writes per wire squared) with a #ccx >= 2 prefilter and an immediate decline on any op outside {h, x, cx, cz, ccx, ccz, s, sdg, z, t, tdg}.
card.trigger: Circuits containing at least two ccx/ccz ops (angle circuits qft/qpe/hhl/qae/tfim decline at the prefilter on their first rz, in one linear pass). After h-normalization, emit one match per disjoint compute/uncompute pair found by the dataflow test above. On mcx_10 the 32 ccz normalize to a 32-Toffoli Barenco Lemma 7.2 V-chain over 8 ancilla wires: each ancilla is written by the up-ladder and restored by the matching down-ladder with its control pair untouched in between, so 15 of the 16 ladder positions match as pairs (the two Toffolis writing the real target wire t do not, since t is neither 0-valued nor restored). It also fires on adder_8 / adder_6 / mult_4 / modred_21 wherever a carry temporary is computed and later uncomputed by the same Toffoli, and never fires where the second occurrence has a different control pair or a rewritten control, so it cannot regress a circuit (and each application is judged independently).
card.expected_effect: Each matched pair costs 4 T instead of the 8 T the book rule currently charges for two separate AND gadgets: the uncompute half becomes measurement-only. On mcx_10, 15 matched pairs x 4 T saved = 60 T, plus the 2 unmatched target Toffolis unchanged at 4 T each: 128 -> 68 T (conservatively 72 if only 14 pairs match), i.e. below pyzx (100), TKET (192) and BQSKit (224), with qubits unchanged at 19 and no error budget charged. This does NOT claim the 36 T of the three earlier whole-circuit MCX-recognition attempts: that target needs the knowledge that, with clean ancillas, the third and fourth Barenco ladders are redundant, which this rule deliberately does not try to prove. The earlier attempts measured 36 T but were rejected twice on the 300 s runtime limit (sympy/BDD canonicalization; 2^n-bit truth-table masks) and once as never_fires (their h-pairing step required exactly one intervening op per Hadamard, which this input violates by sharing Hadamards between consecutive same-target ccz's). This card replaces whole-circuit Boolean recognition with purely local dataflow matching, which is what survives all three of those failure modes.
