card.name: zero_monomial_dataflow_control_elimination
card.identity: A deletion-only pass (no gadget is ever emitted, no function is ever recognized, nothing is rebuilt) that removes Toffoli-level ops which are provably the identity on the clean-ancilla input set, using a tiny per-wire abstract value. (1) H-FRAME NORMALIZATION, robust to SHARED Hadamards: keep every h in place and never move one; instead carry a frame bit f[q], toggled by each h(q) as the op list is scanned. When a ccz(a,b,c) is met, if exactly one leg q has f[q] = 1 and the other two have f = 0, read it as ccx with target q (this is just H_q Z-basis conjugation: H on one leg of a CCZ makes that leg the target of a CCX, and the surrounding h's need not be adjacent or one-per-ccz). ccx is read as itself; cz/cx/x likewise. If a ccz has 0, 2 or 3 legs in the X frame, or any op is not in {h, x, cx, cz, ccx, ccz}, the pass declines immediately. (2) ABSTRACT VALUE (a 'monomial lattice', three cases per wire, each O(k) set work): val[q] in {ZERO, MONO(S) with S a frozenset of input-wire indices, UNKNOWN}. Initialization: a wire is a TEMPORARY iff it is both WRITTEN somewhere (target of ccx/cx/x) and READ somewhere (control/leg of some other op); temporaries start at ZERO (they are the harness's clean |0> scratch wires, and this is exactly what the relaxed judge checks). Every other wire q starts at MONO({q}). Updates, written wire only: for ccx(a,b -> c): if val[a] == ZERO or val[b] == ZERO, the gate is the IDENTITY -> DELETE it and leave val[c] unchanged; else if val[a] = MONO(S), val[b] = MONO(T) the written term is MONO(S | T) (multilinearity: x^2 = x) and the XOR into c gives val[c] = ZERO if val[c] == MONO(S | T) (the term cancels itself), MONO(S | T) if val[c] == ZERO, else UNKNOWN; if either control is UNKNOWN then val[c] = UNKNOWN. For cx(a -> b): same with the single term; for x(a): val[a] = UNKNOWN unless it is tracked as the constant 1. (3) FIRE only if at least one op was marked DELETE and every temporary wire has val = ZERO at the end of the pass (a restoration certificate: the scratch wires are returned to |0>, which is the relaxed contract's requirement). Emit the original op list with the marked ccz/ccx ops removed and ALL h/cz/cx kept verbatim; orphaned h(q) h(q) pairs are left in place (Clifford, zero T cost). One match per circuit, applied once.
card.correctness: A CCX (or CCZ in the matching H frame) whose control wire is in the computational-basis state |0> is literally the identity operator on the whole register: the controlled operation is CCX = |11><11| (x) X + (I - |11><11|) (x) I, and a factor state |0> on one control annihilates the |11><11| branch, so deleting the gate changes nothing on the clean-ancilla input set. The abstract value is a sound over-approximation of the classical value carried by each wire: MONO(S) means the wire holds exactly the product of the input bits in S, ZERO means it holds the constant 0, UNKNOWN means no claim is made, and deletions are taken ONLY in the ZERO case, so every deleted op is identity on every valid input. The XOR rules are the exact GF(2) semantics restricted to single monomials (union of index sets for the product, cancellation x ^ x = 0, absorption 0 ^ x = x) and fall back to UNKNOWN whenever the value leaves that tiny domain, so soundness never depends on the lattice being expressive. Nothing is rewritten, re-synthesized or re-ordered: the kept ops are the original ops in the original order, hence all relative phases of the surviving circuit are untouched (no phase-consistency argument is needed beyond the one the original circuit already satisfies), and in each measurement branch - there are none, the rule introduces no measurement - K|x> = |f(x)> with the same f. The only assumption is that the temporaries start in |0>, which is the relaxed contract and is re-checked by the frozen judge on each application, together with the pass's own end-state certificate that every temporary returns to ZERO. Nothing is charged to the error budget (exact function equality on valid inputs).
card.trigger: One linear pass over the whole op list, O(#ops * k) with k <= 10 index-set elements, on every circuit: the angle circuits (qft_8, qpe_8, hhl_8, qae_13, tfim_6) abort at their first rz/t/s/z op, so no object larger than a dict of small frozensets is ever allocated (this is the cost failure that killed the truth-table and sympy/BDD versions of the earlier whole-circuit recognition attempts, and there is no 2^n or exponential object anywhere here). Fires iff at least one ccz/ccx has a ZERO control and all temporaries end at ZERO. On mcx_10 (Barenco et al. Lemma 7.2, 4(k-2) = 32 Toffolis over 8 borrowed wires) the frame-bit normalization reads all 32 ccz correctly even though 34 h serve 32 ccz with shared Hadamards (trigram 'ccz h ccz' x 30) - this is precisely the normalization that made the previous ANF attempt never fire, and it is fixed at the root by frame bits instead of sandwich pairing. The pass then finds: wires 10-17 are temporaries (written and read), 0-9 are read-only controls, 18 is the write-only target; in the first ladder the 8 ops ccz(9,17,18), ccz(8,16,17), ..., ccz(2,10,11) all have a ZERO ancilla control and are DELETED, ccz(0,1,10) starts the real computation (val[10] = MONO({0,1})), the 7 ops back up the chain are kept (val[17] = MONO({0..8})) and ccz(9,17,18) is kept; in the second ladder the 8 ops down the chain are kept and each cancels its own term (val[17], ..., val[10] -> ZERO), after which the final 7 ops up the chain all have a ZERO control and are DELETED. 15 of 32 deleted, all 8 temporaries certified ZERO at the end. It also fires wherever an adder/multiplier/modred circuit contains a Toffoli on a scratch wire that is still 0, and can never regress anything since it only deletes provable identities and every application is judged independently.
card.expected_effect: 15 of the 32 ccz gates of mcx_10 disappear (the first ladder's 8 no-ops and the last ladder's 7 no-ops - exactly the dirty-ancilla restoration work that Barenco's 4(k-2) construction pays for and that is pure waste when the scratch wires are clean); 17 ccz survive and each is still lowered at 4 T by the book rule and_ancilla_ccz_lowering_with_measured_uncompute. T 128 -> 68, below pyzx (100), TKET (192) and BQSKit (224). Qubits unchanged at 19 (no ancilla is requested, no wire is added), CNOT count strictly drops, no error budget is charged. This deliberately does NOT claim the 36 T of the whole-circuit MCX recognition attempts: that needs the AND-ladder rebuild and the knowledge that the surviving compute ladder's uncompute can be measured away, which this rule does not attempt - its claim is only the set of gates that are literally identity gates, which is cheap to certify on every circuit and is what survives the two runtime rejections and the never_fires.
card.source: Constant propagation / identity-gate removal in reversible Toffoli networks: Maslov, Dueck, Miller, 'Techniques for the synthesis of reversible Toffoli networks', ACM TODAES 12 (2007), and Soeken & Mishchenko's constant-propagation sweeps in reversible logic synthesis; the structure being pruned is Barenco, Bennett, Cleve, DiVincenzo, Margolus, Shor, Sleator, Smolin, Weinfurter, PRA 52, 3457 (1995), Lemma 7.2 (4(k-2) Toffolis with BORROWED/dirty ancillas, which collapses to the 2(k-2)-Toffoli clean-ancilla V-chain of Nielsen & Chuang 4.3 once the scratch wires are known to be |0>); monomial/ANF value domain as a cheap abstraction of Reed-Muller form: Knuth, TAOCP Vol. 4A, 7.1.1.

card.name: generator_equality_angle_teleportation
card.identity: Angle teleportation discovered by BACK-FRAME GENERATOR EQUALITY, computed as explicit 2^n matrices (n = 8, so 256x256), with the edit made in place in the original op list (angles only; no Clifford, cx, h, qubit or op order is touched). (1) List the rotation ops of the 1034-op list in order: k = 1..R at positions p_k, wire q_k, angle theta_k (rz, plus t/tdg at +-pi/4). (2) Build suffix unitaries from the END of the circuit by one incremental matrix product: S_k = (product of all ops strictly AFTER position p_k, in order) as a 2^n x 2^n complex matrix; this is R matrix multiplications of 256x256 total, since S_k is obtained from S_{k+1} by multiplying in the few ops between p_k and p_{k+1}. (3) For each k form the BACK-FRAME GENERATOR B_k = S_k Z_{q_k} S_k^dag, a traceless Hermitian involution (B_k^2 = I) that is in general NOT a Pauli string: the suffix contains Hadamards AND other non-Clifford rotations, and conjugation by a continuous rotation about an anticommuting axis sends Z -> cos(phi) P + sin(phi) P' , a unit vector in a Pauli 2-plane. (4) MATCH: a pair j < k and a sign s in {+1,-1} with || B_j - s B_k ||_F <= 1e-9, tested at the circuit's actual angles AND at 4 extra points obtained by replacing (theta_j, theta_k) by (theta_j + t, theta_k - s t) for t drawn from {+-0.3, +-1.1} (i.e. on the level set of theta_j + s theta_k) and by randomly perturbing all other non-grid angles by ~0.2 in one of those tests, so that the equality is checked to hold along the whole merge path and not only at one point. Candidate pairs are pre-filtered in O(R) by cheap fingerprints of B_k (Frobenius-normalised traces tr(B_k W_m) against 4 fixed random Hermitian probes W_m), so only same-fingerprint buckets are compared as matrices. Chains of matches are closed transitively into classes; a class of size m is reported as m-1 pair matches, largest |theta| first. A pair is reported only if it strictly lowers N_Rz: at least one member is a non-pi/4 rz, and an (rz, t/tdg) pair only when the merged angle lands on the pi/4 grid. (5) APPLY one match at a time: set op p_j's angle to theta_eff = (theta_j + s theta_k) reduced mod 2pi into (-pi, pi]; delete op p_k; if theta_eff == 0 to 1e-12 delete op p_j as well, and if theta_eff is a multiple of pi/4 let with_ops demote it to z/s/sdg/t/tdg - both cases retire TWO synthesized rotations. Positions are recomputed after each accepted application.
card.correctness: Exact, and it is the algebraic content of phase teleportation without any ZX machinery. Write the circuit as U(theta) = S_k . Rz_{q_k}(theta_k) . Pre_k for rotation k, where Pre_k is everything before p_k and S_k everything after. Since Rz_q(theta) = exp(-i theta Z_q / 2), dU/dtheta_k = S_k (-i Z_{q_k}/2) Rz_{q_k}(theta_k) Pre_k = (-i/2) (S_k Z_{q_k} S_k^dag) U(theta) = (-i/2) B_k U(theta). Hence for the direction v = e_j - s e_k, d/dt U(theta + t v) = (-i/2)[ B_j(theta+tv) - s B_k(theta+tv) ] U(theta + tv). If the bracket vanishes for every t on the segment, U is constant along it, so U(theta_j + s theta_k, 0) = U(theta_j, theta_k) exactly - i.e. the whole angle of op k may be teleported onto op j and op k deleted, with every other gate untouched. This is a strictly weaker hypothesis than both book merge rules: if B_j and B_k are Pauli strings P_j = +-P_k and every intervening rotation Pauli commutes with them, the equality holds trivially, so pauli_frame_rotation_merge and pauli_exponential_commutation_merge are special cases; but the equality can also hold when the generators are non-Pauli Hermitian operators, which is exactly the regime created by Hadamards and by anticommuting intervening rotations (the measured blocker on this circuit). Rz(0) = I, so deleting the donor op is exact; the mod-2pi reduction changes only a global phase (Rz(2pi) = -I), permitted by invariant 6. Soundness does not rest on the sampled test being a proof: the only arithmetic is a sum of two angles, so the frozen judge re-measures the phase-aligned operator distance of the changed window (and uses the exact D[omega] check whenever theta_eff demotes to a pi/4 multiple, both sides then being Clifford+T); a pair whose equality held at the samples but not along the path is simply rejected by the judge, never accepted. Finding nothing is a no-op. Numerics: at n = 8 the generators are dense 256x256 matrices built by exact gate products in double precision, so the 1e-9 Frobenius threshold is ~6 orders above accumulated rounding over ~1000 gates, and no eigen/optimisation step is involved.
card.trigger: Any pair of rotation ops whose back-frame generators agree up to sign at the current angles and at the 4 off-point samples. This is precisely the gap the measured history on qpe_8 identifies. Attempt 1 (parity merging) fired 3 times for 192 T because 'segments end at every H'; the admitted pauli_exponential_commutation_merge lifted the H restriction but still demands P_j = +-P_k as PAULI STRINGS plus commutation with every intervening rotation Pauli, and it scored its gain on hhl_8, not here; attempt 3 showed that every ancilla/measurement construction is unverifiable on a Clifford+Rz input (the relaxed judge rejected 'rz(0.0245...) is not a multiple of pi/4'), and attempt 4's single-wire ring synthesis never fired because the Diophantine lattice search found no candidate. The present rule needs no ancilla, no measurement, no lattice search, no Pauli-string coincidence and no commutation condition: the generator is allowed to be any Hermitian involution, and the test is one matrix comparison. On qpe_8 the relevant structure is that the 157 t/tdg ops and the 258 h ops sit BETWEEN the rotations that ought to merge, so the Pauli-string tests fail while the transported generator of a rotation that is conjugated by an anticommuting pi/4 rotation remains a perfectly well-defined involution that can coincide with another rotation's generator (in QPE, the controlled-U^{2^k} ladder applies the same phase through nested CX/H/T sandwiches on 8 ancilla wires, so the same effective generator recurs across stages). The 55 distinct angles over 257 rotations with multiplicities 15/15/15/15/14/11x9 give many candidate partners, and the exact-inverse families (10.566379 with 1.999991, sum = 4pi to 1e-6; 0.331877 with 7.097863) are the pairs whose merged angle is 0 and which therefore retire BOTH rotations wherever the generator test passes.
card.expected_effect: A surviving non-grid rz costs gridsynth ~46 T at the current operating point (11485 T over ~250 rotations). A merged pair retires one rotation (~46 T); a pair that cancels mod 2pi or lands on the pi/4 grid retires two (~92 T). card.name: convex_dag_block_leap_resynthesis
card.identity: Re-synthesize CONVEX DAG blocks (not contiguous op-list spans) of <= 3 qubits by incremental numerical search, with the objective 'minimum number of angles that are not multiples of pi/4'. (1) Build the op DAG of the Clifford+Rz list: nodes = ops, edge p -> q iff q is the next op after p on some shared qubit. (2) BLOCK FORMATION (this is the part that must change, see expected_effect): choose a qubit subset S with |S| <= 3 and collect candidate ops with support contained in S; grow a block B greedily in topological order and keep B only if B is CONVEX in the DAG, i.e. there is no directed path that leaves B and later re-enters B (test by reachability: for every pair u,v in B, every path u -> ... -> v must stay inside B, equivalently no op outside B is both a descendant of some op in B and an ancestor of another). Convexity, not op-list contiguity, is the correct condition: a convex block can be slid together through ops whose support is disjoint from the ops being commuted past, which is an exact identity (disjoint-support ops commute), so the circuit factors as U = W_2 (U_B tensor I) W_1. Run this for all qubit subsets of size 1, 2, 3 (8 qubits -> 8 + 28 + 56 = 92 subsets, cheap), then select a maximal set of pairwise non-overlapping blocks preferring those with the most non-Clifford rotations; re-run the whole pass to a fixed point after each accepted application. (3) TARGET: U_B = dense 2^|S| matrix (<= 8x8) obtained by multiplying the block's ops in topological order; r_B = number of ops in B whose angle is not within 1e-12 of a multiple of pi/4; c_B = number of cx/cz in B. (4) SYNTHESIS by LEAP/QSearch-style incremental deepening, not a fixed template: start with one single-qubit Euler layer per wire (rz(x) h rz(y) h rz(z)); repeatedly append (one cx/cz on a pair that occurs in B, then Euler layers on the two touched wires); at each depth minimise the phase-invariant residual f(theta) = 1 - |tr(V(theta)^dag U_B)| / 2^|S| with scipy.optimize.least_squares from deterministic multi-starts (fixed seed; include B's own angles and the KAK/ZXZ angles of U_B); LEAP's prefix freezing (keep the best prefix found at depth d when deepening to d+1) keeps the search linear in depth. Stop deepening at c_B cx gates. (5) CLIFFORD PINNING loop, which is where the T-count objective enters: given a fit with residual <= 1e-12, sort its angles by distance to the nearest multiple of pi/4, pin the nearest one to that exact multiple (remove it from the free parameters), refit the rest; keep the pin if the residual stays <= 1e-12, otherwise unpin and try the next angle; iterate until no further angle can be pinned. Report the number of unpinned (non-Clifford) angles r_V. (6) ACCEPT a block iff r_V < r_B and the final phase-aligned operator distance d_B = min_phi ||V - e^{i phi} U_B||_2 <= 1e-10, and c_V <= c_B. (7) The match is (set of op positions in B, replacement op list); apply() deletes the block's ops from their positions and splices the replacement at the position of the block's topologically-first op, which is legal exactly because B is convex. with_ops lowers every pinned angle to an exact Clifford/T gate; angles within 1e-12 of 0 are dropped. Every application is re-verified and re-costed by the frozen judge.
card.correctness: (a) Extraction is exact, not approximate: if B is convex in the op DAG then the ops of B can be brought into one contiguous run by repeatedly transposing adjacent ops with disjoint qubit support, and disjoint-support ops commute exactly (they act on different tensor factors). Convexity is precisely the obstruction-free condition: a path leaving and re-entering B would force an outside op to be both after one member and before another on a shared wire, which no disjoint-support transposition can fix. Hence U = W_2 (U_B tensor I) W_1 identically, with U_B the product of B's ops in topological order (any two topological orders differ by disjoint-support transpositions, so U_B is well defined). (b) Error accounting: replacing U_B by V gives, by unitary invariance of the operator norm, ||W_2 (V tensor I) W_1 - e^{i phi} W_2 (U_B tensor I) W_1|| = ||V - e^{i phi} U_B|| = d_B, so the global charge of a block is exactly its measured local distance and charges of different blocks add subadditively. With d_B <= 1e-10 and at most a few hundred accepted blocks the total is <= 1e-7, four orders under the approx allowance eps/2 = 5e-4; eps_rz for the surviving rotations is therefore not tightened. (c) The ansatz family is complete and the search is a restriction, never an extension: rz(x) h rz(y) h rz(z) covers all of SU(2) up to phase (ZXZ Euler, since h rz(y) h = rx(y)), and alternating such layers with cx/cz on the block's own pairs up to c_B two-qubit gates contains the block itself as one member (take B's own angles), so a fit always exists at depth c_B and the enumeration only asks whether fewer non-Clifford angles suffice. An accepted application therefore strictly reduces the number of gridsynth-charged rotations at no increase in cx count. (d) Pinning is sound because it is verified, not assumed: an angle is pinned to an exact multiple of pi/4 only if the remaining free angles can be refitted to residual <= 1e-12, and the final accept test is the measured phase-aligned distance of the emitted circuit (after snapping), so a pin that is only approximately valid is rejected by the test rather than silently charged. (e) Why slack still exists on this input - two independent reasons. First, TKET's FullPeepholeOptimise minimises cx count and total gate count (KAK + single-qubit squashing into a 3-angle normal form); it never minimises the count of angles that are NOT multiples of pi/4, which is the only quantity the gridsynth cost model charges for, and it emits three generic Euler angles for a single-qubit layer even when that layer is, e.g., h rz(theta) h (one generic rotation) or Clifford times rz(theta). Second, and more importantly, THIS circuit is no longer TKET's output: pauli_frame_rotation_merge made 131 accepted applications, pauli_exponential_commutation_merge and the two refit rules more, each of which rewrote an angle and deleted an op. card.name: convex_dag_block_leap_resynthesis
card.identity: Re-synthesize CONVEX DAG blocks (not contiguous op-list spans) of <= 3 qubits by incremental numerical search, with the objective 'minimum number of angles that are not multiples of pi/4'. (1) Build the op DAG of the Clifford+Rz list: nodes = ops, edge p -> q iff q is the next op after p on some shared qubit. (2) BLOCK FORMATION (this is the part that must change, see expected_effect): choose a qubit subset S with |S| <= 3 and collect candidate ops with support contained in S; grow a block B greedily in topological order and keep B only if B is CONVEX in the DAG, i.e. there is no directed path that leaves B and later re-enters B (test by reachability: for every pair u,v in B, every path u -> ... -> v must stay inside B, equivalently no op outside B is both a descendant of some op in B and an ancestor of another). Convexity, not op-list contiguity, is the correct condition: a convex block can be slid together through ops whose support is disjoint from the ops being commuted past, which is an exact identity (disjoint-support ops commute), so the circuit factors as U = W_2 (U_B tensor I) W_1. Run this for all qubit subsets of size 1, 2, 3 (8 qubits -> 8 + 28 + 56 = 92 subsets, cheap), then select a maximal set of pairwise non-overlapping blocks preferring those with the most non-Clifford rotations; re-run the whole pass to a fixed point after each accepted application. (3) TARGET: U_B = dense 2^|S| matrix (<= 8x8) obtained by multiplying the block's ops in topological order; r_B = number of ops in B whose angle is not within 1e-12 of a multiple of pi/4; c_B = number of cx/cz in B. (4) SYNTHESIS by LEAP/QSearch-style incremental deepening, not a fixed template: start with one single-qubit Euler layer per wire (rz(x) h rz(y) h rz(z)); repeatedly append (one cx/cz on a pair that occurs in B, then Euler layers on the two touched wires); at each depth minimise the phase-invariant residual f(theta) = 1 - |tr(V(theta)^dag U_B)| / 2^|S| with scipy.optimize.least_squares from deterministic multi-starts (fixed seed; include B's own angles and the KAK/ZXZ angles of U_B); LEAP's prefix freezing (keep the best prefix found at depth d when deepening to d+1) keeps the search linear in depth. Stop deepening at c_B cx gates. (5) CLIFFORD PINNING loop, which is where the T-count objective enters: given a fit with residual <= 1e-12, sort its angles by distance to the nearest multiple of pi/4, pin the nearest one to that exact multiple (remove it from the free parameters), refit the rest; keep the pin if the residual stays <= 1e-12, otherwise unpin and try the next angle; iterate until no further angle can be pinned. Every application is re-verified and re-costed by the frozen judge.

card.name: clock_diagonal_multiplexor_walsh_resynthesis
card.identity: Recognise the part of the circuit that is a UNIFORMLY CONTROLLED (multiplexed) single-qubit rotation set and re-emit it from its Walsh (Hadamard-transform) spectrum, which is sparse for phase-estimation-style angle functions. (1) NORMAL FORM (same machinery the book already uses, no new risk): walk the op list once, maintaining the running Clifford K_p = product of Clifford ops before position p, and turn every rotation op p (rz/t/tdg, Z-angle a_p on qubit q_p) into a signed Pauli exponential R_p = exp(-i a_p P_p/2) with P_p = K_p Z_{q_p} K_p^dag (v3.api.pauli.conjugate, exact symplectic arithmetic). (2) DETECT A MULTIPLEXOR RUN. A rotation is 'axis-s diagonal' if its axis P carries X, Y or Z on one distinguished qubit s and only I or Z on every other qubit. Scan the rotation sequence for maximal runs M = (R_i..R_j) all of whose axes are axis-s diagonal for one common s, and ADMIT a non-consecutive rotation R_k into M (k between i and j, axis not axis-s diagonal) only by the exact commutation swap: R_k may be moved out of the run iff its axis commutes with the axes of all members it must cross (symplectic test, exact); otherwise the run is cut at k. Let C = union of the qubits (other than s) carrying Z in the admitted axes, k = |C| (cap k <= 7; if larger, cut the run). (3) EXACT BLOCK PRODUCT. Every admitted axis is Z_S (x) sigma_a with S subset C and sigma_a in {X,Y,Z} on s, so every admitted rotation is block diagonal in the computational basis of C, acting on block j in {0,1}^k as the SU(2) rotation exp(-i (-1)^{S.j} theta sigma_a / 2). Hence the run unitary is V = sum_j |j><j| (x) V_j with V_j in SU(2) computed EXACTLY as an ordered product of 2x2 matrices (2^k products of run-length 2x2 matrices: closed form, no optimiser, no 2^n dense algebra). (4) EULER + WALSH. For each j extract ZXZ Euler angles V_j = Rz(alpha_j) Rx(beta_j) Rz(gamma_j) in closed form; among the few branch liftings that reproduce V_j exactly (checked by recomputing the 2x2 product, never by flipping the sign of V_j, since relative phases between blocks are observable) pick one by a Gray-code continuity sweep over j, choosing the branch that minimises Walsh-spectrum support. Then each of the three multiplexors sum_j theta_j |j><j| (x) Z_s is, by the Walsh-Hadamard transform, exactly sum_{S subset C} c_S Z_S (x) Z_s with c_S = 2^{-k} sum_j (-1)^{S.j} theta_j. (5) RE-EMIT in Moettoenen uniformly-controlled form: for each of the three slots, for each S with |c_S| > tol, a CX ladder from the qubits of S onto s, rz(c_S) on s, ladder inverted (Gray-code ordering so consecutive ladders cancel to one CX per term); the beta slot is conjugated by h on s (Rx = h Rz h). Coefficients with |c_S| <= tol are DROPPED, charging error; tol is set per application so that the measured phase-aligned distance of the whole replacement stays <= 1e-6 (budget per application; at most a few tens of applications, total <= 1e-4 of the 5e-4 approx allowance). Angles that land within 1e-12 of a multiple of pi/4 are lowered to Clifford/T by with_ops, angles within 1e-12 of 0 are dropped. (6) MATCH = (span of op positions covered by the run, replacement op list: the re-emitted multiplexors plus the run's own Clifford skeleton re-emitted unchanged at the span boundary); ACCEPT only if the number of surviving non-Clifford rotations is strictly smaller than in the run. If a run is too long, bisect it and emit two matches. No ancillas, no measurement, so the rz-bearing candidate is checked in the numeric-distance mode, not the relaxed mode.
card.correctness: (a) The normal form is exact: C exp(-i a P/2) = exp(-i a (C P C^dag)/2) C for Clifford C and Pauli P, so transporting rotations through the Clifford skeleton reproduces U up to global phase; reordering inside the run uses only [P,Q] = 0 => the two exponentials commute (exact symplectic test, no numerics). (b) The block decomposition is an identity, not a fit: if every axis is Z_S (x) sigma_a with S not containing s, all admitted rotations are simultaneously block diagonal in the C-basis, so V = (+)_j V_j with V_j the ordered 2x2 product; each generator is traceless on the block, so each factor and hence V_j is in SU(2) exactly (no leftover per-block determinant phase to account for). (c) ZXZ Euler is complete for SU(2) (Rx = h Rz h), and the Walsh-Hadamard transform of the real vector (theta_j) is an exact finite orthogonal change of basis: sum_j theta_j |j><j| (x) Z = sum_S c_S Z_S (x) Z identically, because {2^{-k/2}(-1)^{S.j}} is an orthogonal matrix and Z_S acts on block j as (-1)^{S.j}. So the full-spectrum emission is an EXACT re-expression of V with 3*2^k rotations, and the pass is a strict re-expression plus a truncation; nothing is extrapolated. (d) Error: the run is a dependency-contiguous span in the normal form, so U = W_2 V W_1 and, by unitary invariance, ||W_2 V' W_1 - e^{i phi} W_2 V W_1|| = ||V' - e^{i phi} V||, i.e. the global charge of an application equals its measured local distance, and applications add subadditively; with <= 1e-6 each the total is far under eps/2 = 5e-4 and eps_rz for the survivors is not tightened. Every application is re-verified and re-costed by the frozen judge, so a bad Euler branch or too aggressive a tol is rejected, not silently charged. (e) WHY THIS BEATS THE BOOK, and why it is not the Lie-closure rule again. pauli_frame_rotation_merge / pauli_exponential_commutation_merge only delete rotations with EQUAL axes, which is saturated here (29205 was already passed). pauli_subalgebra_dimension_recompression has the right abstract bound (the axes Z_S (x) sigma generate an algebra of dimension 3*2^rank) but tried to realise it by a generic least-squares fit of ~10^2 parameters against a dense 2^8 x 2^8 matrix over strictly consecutive runs: that is numerically hopeless, which is exactly what its 7 applications / 520 T measured against a 6500 T estimate show. This rule replaces that fit by (i) the exact 2x2 block product, (ii) closed-form Euler extraction, (iii) one orthogonal transform - no optimiser at all - and additionally gathers rotations across commuting interlopers so runs are not cut by traffic on other wires. It also goes BELOW the dimension bound: the real gain is SPECTRAL SPARSITY. In phase estimation the multiplexed angle is (close to) linear in the control integer, theta_j = t * j (controlled e^{-iAt*2^m} on a clock register), and the Walsh spectrum of a linear function of j is supported on the k singleton sets plus the constant, i.e. k+1 nonzero coefficients instead of 2^k - that is the Welch et al. Walsh-series observation. A run of hundreds of clock-controlled system rotations therefore collapses to O(k) rotations per Euler slot, which no dimension-counting argument and no equal-axis merge can reach.
card.trigger: A maximal run of rotation ops in the Clifford-pushed normal form (extended across interlopers whose axes commute with the crossed members) such that every axis carries X/Y/Z on one common qubit s and only I/Z elsewhere, with k = |other qubits carrying Z| <= 7, the run contains at least 6 non-Clifford rotations, and step (5) emits strictly fewer non-Clifford rotations at measured phase-aligned distance <= 1e-6. Purely structural, no condition on angle values. On hhl_8 (8 qubits, 583 rz + 101 t + 101 tdg, 607 h, 497 cx) this is precisely the controlled-e^{iAt} / inverse-QFT skeleton of HHL: a small system register (1-2 qubits) driven by clock-controlled rotations, which in the Pauli frame are axes Z_S (x) sigma on the system qubit, plus the clock-only diagonal runs (s = a clock qubit, axes all Z-type: there the Euler reduction degenerates to the single alpha slot and the rule is a Walsh sparsification of the diagonal QFT phase function). The angle histogram is the fingerprint: dyadic families pi/8 = 0.392699 x7, pi/16 = 0.19635 x4, pi/32 = 0.098175 x2 with their 4pi-complements (12.173672 x5, 12.370021 x3, 12.48654 x2) are a controlled-phase/clock-controlled evolution with angles in geometric progression in the control index, i.e. exactly the linear-in-j case whose Walsh spectrum is sparse; the trigram 'cx tdg cx' x66 and 'rz cx rz' x79 are the CX-ladder-conjugated single-rotation pieces of those multiplexors as TKET left them.
card.expected_effect: Each removed non-Clifford rotation deletes one gridsynth sequence worth 3 log2(1/eps_rz) ~ 57 T at the current eps_rz, and shrinking N_Rz loosens eps_rz for every survivor (~0.8 T per survivor per 100 removed). Firing pattern expected on this circuit: (i) the clock-diagonal (all-Z axis) runs of the QFT/inverse-QFT halves, where the Walsh spectrum of the quadratic/linear phase function is supported on pairs and singletons, should drop tens of rotations; (ii) the clock-controlled system-register runs, where a run of several dozen to a couple of hundred rotations is re-emitted as 3*(k+1) ~ 15-25 rotations per run, which is where the bulk is. I expect 80-130 rotations removed, i.e. roughly 4500-7500 T, taking 28509 to about 21000-24000 and into the regime of the only baseline that beats the exact-merge wall here (BQSKit-DPF, 19443). CX count can rise inside a re-emitted multiplexor (Gray-code ladders, ~1 CX per kept term, partly cancelling against neighbours); that is the third lexicographic key only. No ancillas (qubit count unchanged), error charge <= ~1e-4 of the 5e-4 approx allowance.

Then each of the three multiplexors sum_j theta_j |j><j| (x) Z_s is, by the Walsh-Hadamard transform, exactly sum_{S subset C} c_S Z_S (x) Z_s with c_S = 2^{-k} sum_j (-1)^{S.j} theta_j. (5) RE-EMIT in Moettoenen uniformly-controlled form: for each of the three slots, for each S with |c_S| > tol, a CX ladder from the qubits of S onto s, rz(c_S) on s, ladder inverted (Gray-code ordering so consecutive ladders cancel to one CX per term); the beta slot is conjugated by h on s (Rx = h Rz h). Coefficients with |c_S| <= tol are DROPPED, charging error; tol is set per application so that the measured phase-aligned distance of the whole replacement stays <= 1e-6 (budget per application; at most a few tens of applications, total <= 1e-4 of the 5e-4 approx allowance). Angles that land within 1e-12 of a multiple of pi/4 are lowered to Clifford/T by with_ops, angles within 1e-12 of 0 are dropped. (6) MATCH = (span of op positions covered by the run, replacement op list: the re-emitted multiplexors plus the run's own Clifford skeleton re-emitted unchanged at the span boundary); ACCEPT only if the number of surviving non-Clifford rotations is strictly smaller than in the run. If a run is too long, bisect it and emit two matches. No ancillas, no measurement, so the rz-bearing candidate is checked in the numeric-distance mode, not the relaxed mode.
card.correctness: (a) The normal form is exact: C exp(-i a P/2) = exp(-i a (C P C^dag)/2) C for Clifford C and Pauli P, so transporting rotations through the Clifford skeleton reproduces U up to global phase; reordering inside the run uses only [P,Q] = 0 => the two exponentials commute (exact symplectic test, no numerics). (b) The block decomposition is an identity, not a fit: if every axis is Z_S (x) sigma_a with S not containing s, all admitted rotations are simultaneously block diagonal in the C-basis, so V = (+)_j V_j with V_j the ordered 2x2 product; each generator is traceless on the block, so each factor and hence V_j is in SU(2) exactly (no leftover per-block determinant phase to account for). (c) ZXZ Euler is complete for SU(2) (Rx = h Rz h), and the Walsh-Hadamard transform of the real vector (theta_j) is an exact finite orthogonal change of basis: sum_j theta_j |j><j| (x) Z = sum_S c_S Z_S (x) Z identically, because {2^{-k/2}(-1)^{S.j}} is an orthogonal matrix and Z_S acts on block j as (-1)^{S.j}. So the full-spectrum emission is an EXACT re-expression of V with 3*2^k rotations, and the pass is a strict re-expression plus a truncation; nothing is extrapolated. (d) Error: the run is a dependency-contiguous span in the normal form, so U = W_2 V W_1 and, by unitary invariance, ||W_2 V' W_1 - e^{i phi} W_2 V W_1|| = ||V' - e^{i phi} V||, i.e. the global charge of an application equals its measured local distance, and applications add subadditively; with <= 1e-6 each the total is far under eps/2 = 5e-4 and eps_rz for the survivors is not tightened. Every application is re-verified and re-costed by the frozen judge, so a bad Euler branch or too aggressive a tol is rejected, not silently charged. (e) WHY THIS BEATS THE BOOK, and why it is not the Lie-closure rule again. pauli_frame_rotation_merge / pauli_exponential_commutation_merge only delete rotations with EQUAL axes, which is saturated here (29205 was already passed). pauli_subalgebra_dimension_recompression has the right abstract bound (the axes Z_S (x) sigma generate an algebra of dimension 3*2^rank) but tried to realise it by a generic least-squares fit of ~10^2 parameters against a dense 2^8 x 2^8 matrix over strictly consecutive runs: that is numerically hopeless, which is exactly what its 7 applications / 520 T measured against a 6500 T estimate show. This rule replaces that fit by (i) the exact 2x2 block product, (ii) closed-form Euler extraction, (iii) one orthogonal transform - no optimiser at all - and additionally gathers rotations across commuting interlopers so runs are not cut by traffic on other wires. It also goes BELOW the dimension bound: the real gain is SPECTRAL SPARSITY. In phase estimation the multiplexed angle is (close to) linear in the control integer, theta_j = t * j (controlled e^{-iAt*2^m} on a clock register), and the Walsh spectrum of a linear function of j is supported on the k singleton sets plus the constant, i.e. k+1 nonzero coefficients instead of 2^k - that is the Welch et al. Walsh-series observation. A run of hundreds of clock-controlled system rotations therefore collapses to O(k) rotations per Euler slot, which no dimension-counting argument and no equal-axis merge can reach.
card.trigger: A maximal run of rotation ops in the Clifford-pushed normal form (extended across interlopers whose axes commute with the crossed members) such that every axis carries X/Y/Z on one common qubit s and only I/Z elsewhere, with k = |other qubits carrying Z| <= 7, the run contains at least 6 non-Clifford rotations, and step (5) emits strictly fewer non-Clifford rotations at measured phase-aligned distance <= 1e-6. Purely structural, no condition on angle values. On hhl_8 (8 qubits, 583 rz + 101 t + 101 tdg, 607 h, 497 cx) this is precisely the controlled-e^{iAt} / inverse-QFT skeleton of HHL: a small system register (1-2 qubits) driven by clock-controlled rotations, which in the Pauli frame are axes Z_S (x) sigma on the system qubit, plus the clock-only diagonal runs (s = a clock qubit, axes all Z-type: there the Euler reduction degenerates to the single alpha slot and the rule is a Walsh sparsification of the diagonal QFT phase function). The angle histogram is the fingerprint: dyadic families pi/8 = 0.392699 x7, pi/16 = 0.19635 x4, pi/32 = 0.098175 x2 with their 4pi-complements (12.173672 x5, 12.370021 x3, 12.48654 x2) are a controlled-phase/clock-controlled evolution with angles in geometric progression in the control index, i.e. exactly the linear-in-j case whose Walsh spectrum is sparse; the trigram 'cx tdg cx' x66 and 'rz cx rz' x79 are the CX-ladder-conjugated single-rotation pieces of those multiplexors as TKET left them.
card.expected_effect: Each removed non-Clifford rotation deletes one gridsynth sequence worth 3 log2(1/eps_rz) ~ 57 T at the current eps_rz, and shrinking N_Rz loosens eps_rz for every survivor (~0.8 T per survivor per 100 removed). Firing pattern expected on this circuit: (i) the clock-diagonal (all-Z axis) runs of the QFT/inverse-QFT halves, where the Walsh spectrum of the quadratic/linear phase function is supported on pairs and singletons, should drop tens of rotations; (ii) the clock-controlled system-register runs, where a run of several dozen to a couple of hundred rotations is re-emitted as 3*(k+1) ~ 15-25 rotations per run, which is where the bulk is. I expect 80-130 rotations removed, i.e. roughly 4500-7500 T, taking 28509 to about 21000-24000 and into the regime of the only baseline that beats the exact-merge wall here (BQSKit-DPF, 19443). CX count can rise inside a re-emitted multiplexor (Gray-code ladders, ~1 CX per kept term, partly cancelling against neighbours); that is the third lexicographic key only. No ancillas (qubit count unchanged), error charge <= ~1e-4 of the 5e-4 approx allowance.
